note: R1 (clinical) and R2 (clerking wiring) read version 0.2.0-draft. R3 (clinical) re-read the fixes and found more; its findings are answered here too. 'fixed' means changed in this pack and, for the rule catalog, proved by a vignette. 'fixed_in_part' says what remains. 'cso_decision' and 'phase_0' are not fixed here.

findings.finding: There is no therapy flag for a person ALREADY on metformin with eGFR below 30. The only metformin kidney flag is bounded 30 to 44, so the less dangerous band is flagged and the contraindicated band is silent. Walked through the reference evaluator: type 2, on metformin, eGFR 28, above target -> fires DM-ACT-REFER-EGFR-01 and DM-ACT-RX-02 ('add a sulfonylurea'); nothing says anything about the metformin. The only stop check is a formulary-time check in wiring marked 'proposed', which does not run at review of an existing prescription.
findings.why: The pack's own REF-DM-RX-METFORMIN-STOP-EGFR quotes WHO ('contraindicated ... eGFR <30') and ADA ('should be stopped once eGFR is <30'). Most Ugandan patients are on long-standing metformin and get a creatinine rarely; the visit where eGFR 28 first appears is exactly when the flag is needed. Lactic acidosis risk; and the system instead proposes stepping treatment up.
findings.reviewerFix: Add a red therapy flag: glucose_lowering_therapy == metformin AND egfr < REF-DM-RX-METFORMIN-STOP-EGFR, action 'WHO: contraindicated below this eGFR; ADA: stop. Review today with the prescriber' (no dose). Add a golden vignette (metformin, eGFR 28). Until a live v0.1.0 flag is shown to exist, treat it as absent.
findings.done: Red flag metformin_egfr_below_30. Vignette DMV-35.

findings.where: 60-acute-route.json DM-ACU-ROUTE-01/02 (whole lane); features mental_status, dehydration, effective_osmolality, sodium, urea (unused)
findings.finding: An adult with severe hyperglycaemia and danger signs is not routed unless a ketone result of 2+ or more has been typed in. Evaluator runs: (a) new adult, meter 27, vomiting, deep sighing breathing, drowsy, no ketone result yet -> only DM-ACU-ROUTE-01 'test urine ketones now' and DM-SUS-INCID-01 (routine). (b) 72-year-old known type 2, glucose 38, drowsy, dehydrated, ketones negative (hyperosmolar picture) -> DM-ACU-ROUTE-01 plus DM-ACT-RX-04 'consider insulin'; no triage signal at all. mental_status and dehydration are read by no adult rule; no rule reads the HHS glucose (REF-DM-ACU-HHS-GLU). Urine ketones 'trace/1+' with the full clinical picture also routes nothing (only a non-blocking caveat appears).
findings.why: WHO HEARTS-D, quoted in the pack (REF-DM-ACU-REFER-ALL, REF-DM-ACT-REFER-SAMEDAY): 'Refer to hospital all patients with suspected DKA or HHS' and same-day referral for 'suspicion of ketoacidosis or HHS'. Suspicion is clinical; the pack makes routing conditional on a strip result. HHS is ketone-negative by definition, so the one test the lane asks for clears the patient. At a district site with no strips in stock, or a busy triage desk, the sickest hyperglycaemic adult gets a 'test' prompt and nothing else. Breaches rule 8, and rule 4's intent (danger is routed).
findings.reviewerFix: Add an adult clinical-picture rule mirroring DM-ACU-ROUTE-04: glucose >= 11.1 (any source) or known diabetes, WITH any of vomiting, abdominal pain, deep_rapid_breathing, acetone_breath, dehydration, mental_status in [drowsy, stupor, coma] -> immediate acute_signal 'suspected DKA or HHS: route now; do not wait for ketones'. Add an HHS-range rule on glucose >= REF-DM-ACU-HHS-GLU, or 'HI' on the meter, regardless of ketones. Make DM-ACU-ROUTE-01's text say what to do when ketones are negative but the patient is unwell, or when no strip is available. Add vignettes for both.
findings.done: Rules DM-ACU-ROUTE-11 (clinical picture), -13 (known diabetes and unwell: test now), -14 (glucose 33.3 or HI, whatever the ketones). ROUTE-01 says what to do when ketones are negative or no strip exists. Vignettes DMV-36, DMV-37.

findings.finding: The child rules stay silent on the child most likely to die. (1) Both rules need an osmotic symptom recorded as present; if thirst/polyuria/weight loss/bed-wetting were simply not asked the left arm is 'insufficient'. Evaluator: 7-year-old, vomiting, deep rapid breathing, dehydrated, drowsy, osmotic history not taken -> NOTHING fires. Same child with a meter glucose of 26 -> only 'Glucose 18 or more: test urine ketones now'; 'hospital now' still does not fire. (2) A known type 1 child who is vomiting with abdominal pain fires no acute rule (ROUTE-04 has no 'known diabetes' arm). (3) The display promises 'dry or drowsy' but mental_status is not in the predicates, and DM-SUS-PAED-01's display promises 'tired' but fatigue is not tested (rule 10).
findings.why: In Uganda paediatric DKA presents to a health centre as 'vomiting and fast breathing' and is treated as malaria, gastroenteritis or pneumonia; the pack's own note says so. The history of polyuria is exactly what is missing in a drowsy child brought by a relative. The pack's own note on the rule says NICE sends a child with glucose above 11 mmol/L and these features to hospital immediately; the rule does not read glucose at all. A rule that needs the answer nobody asked cannot protect this child.
findings.reviewerFix: Rewrite ROUTE-04 as: age band child/adolescent AND at least one of [vomiting, abdominal_pain, deep_rapid_breathing, dehydration, mental_status in drowsy/stupor/coma] AND any of [an osmotic symptom present, capillary_glucose/random_pg >= 11.1, dm_status == known, urine ketones >= 2+ or bohb >= 3.0]. Add a paediatric prompt rule (same_day, 'check capillary glucose now') for vomiting with deep breathing, dehydration or drowsiness when no glucose is recorded. Align both displays with the predicates. Add vignettes: history not taken; known type 1 child vomiting.
findings.done: ROUTE-04 rewritten: the osmotic history is no longer required; glucose, HI, ketones or known diabetes stand in for it. New ROUTE-15 (sick child: glucose now). PAED-01 and its display aligned. Vignettes DMV-38, DMV-39, DMV-40.

findings.where: 40-stratify.json targetsProposed (all 8), interpretation (fpg/ppg/bp bands), riskModels hypoglycaemia_risk_ada; 50-act.json therapyFlags (all 14)
findings.finding: Under-16s receive adult management content. Targets, control and blood-pressure bands, the hypoglycaemia risk model and therapy flags carry no age band (only 'rules' have ageBands and only management steps are adult-gated). Evaluator, known type 1 child aged 10 on insulin: fires therapy flag hypoglycaemia_needing_help_on_treatment ('re-evaluate the plan, with deintensification or a switch of the causing medicine'); proposes tgt_hba1c_general, tgt_hba1c_relaxed, tgt_fpg_surrogate, tgt_ppg_surrogate and tgt_bp ('below 130/80'); shows BP 124/78 as 'At target' and a fasting glucose of 3.1 as 'At target'.
findings.why: Breaches rule 3 (under 16: recognition, classification support and referral only). The adult numbers are wrong for children: 124/78 in a 10-year-old would sit in the hypertensive range on paediatric percentile charts, and adult HbA1c/BP targets and 'deintensify' advice are paediatric specialist decisions.
findings.reviewerFix: Give targets, interpretation tables, risk models and therapy flags an ageBands (or ages: adult) gate identical to management, and assert it in a vignette ('no target, band or flag under 16'). For under-16s show only the referral step. Also state where the adolescent band ends: if it runs past 16, 16-19-year-olds lose every adult suspect and act rule.
findings.done: x.ages = adult on every target, stratify band, risk model and therapy flag; the evaluator withholds them under 16. DMV-40 asserts it. Where the adolescent band ends is an open Phase 0 question.

findings.where: 20-confirm.json validityCaveats fundus_undilated_direct (and uacr_transient, egfr_not_steady_state, abi_calcified); 40-stratify.json diabetic_retinopathy; vignette DMV-21
findings.finding: A caveat marked blocksDiagnosis does not stop a NEGATIVE complication result. DMV-21 (retina 'normal' on undilated direct ophthalmoscopy) is expected and computed as diabetic_retinopathy 'not_met' with stage 'No apparent retinopathy' and 'No macular oedema', while the caveat's own text says 'the eyes count as not screened'. The vignette asserts the unsafe state and the build passes.
findings.why: Breaches rule 2: an examination the pack itself calls invalid is being stored as normal. The stage 'none' carries a 24-month recall interval, so a person with sight-threatening retinopathy can be shown as clear for two years. The same hole applies to an ACR taken with fever (transient), an eGFR in AKI or pregnancy, and an ABI above 1.3.
findings.reviewerFix: When a blocking caveat is in force on a feature, every criterion and stage that reads it must evaluate to 'insufficient' in both directions (met and not_met), and the examination must not reset months_since_eye_screen. Change DMV-21's expectation to diabetic_retinopathy: insufficient, stages: none assigned, and add the same test for uacr_transient.
findings.done: A blocking caveat now makes every criterion, stage and classification that reads the feature 'insufficient' in both directions. A second caveat covers the macula. DMV-21 corrected; DMV-55 tests the urine albumin case.

findings.where: 40-stratify.json riskModels hypoglycaemia_risk_ada; 50-act.json DM-ACT-RX-10, DM-ACT-EDU-03, therapyFlag hypoglycaemia_needing_help_on_treatment; feature on_insulin_or_sulfonylurea
findings.finding: All hypoglycaemia logic hangs on a separate tick-box, on_insulin_or_sulfonylurea, which the features file says 'the clinician ticks' until a computed formula exists. If it is not ticked every one of these is 'insufficient'. Evaluator: 78-year-old on glibenclamide (in glucose_lowering_therapy), a low needing help in the last year, fasting 3.2 -> the only thing that fires is the generic glibenclamide_age_60 flag. No risk band, no hypo flag, no DM-ACT-RX-10, no hypoglycaemia education.
findings.why: The medicine list already says she is on a sulfonylurea; the engine ignores it. A redundant manual field that is rarely filled silences the rules that matter most for the elderly patient on glibenclamide, a leading serious drug harm in diabetes care here.
findings.reviewerFix: Replace on_insulin_or_sulfonylurea in every predicate with ANY(glucose_lowering_therapy == insulin | glibenclamide | gliclazide | glimepiride), as DM-ACT-RX-11 and sulfonylurea_with_rifampicin already do. Drop the tick-box. Add a vignette without the tick.
findings.done: The tick-box feature is deleted. Every hypoglycaemia predicate reads glucose_lowering_therapy. DMV-41 has no tick.

findings.where: 40-stratify.json interpretation fpg_control_who, ppg_control_who, hba1c_control_*, bp_*_who_hearts_d; 60-acute-route.json (no hypoglycaemia rule)
findings.finding: Low values are shown as good. The control bands have an upper edge only: fasting glucose 3.2 (and 3.1 in the child above) evaluates to 'At target' with tone 'normal'; HbA1c of any low value on insulin or glibenclamide is 'At target'; systolic 80 is 'At target'. In the same patient a meter reading of 2.6 fires nothing: no rule in this pack's acute lane reads a low glucose, and the hypoglycaemia entry here is a citation re-verification only.
findings.why: A clinician glancing at a green 'At target' beside a fasting glucose of 3.2 in an old woman on glibenclamide is being told to carry on. The pack's own REF-DM-HYPO-L1 (3.9) and REF-DM-HYPO-L2 (3.0) exist and are used by no band or rule. 'Hypoglycaemia is read from the hypoglycaemia table' (the note) does not stop this table mislabelling the same number.
findings.reviewerFix: Add a lowest band to fpg_control_who and ppg_control_who below REF-DM-HYPO-L1 ('Low: hypoglycaemia range', tone alert) so 'At target' starts at that value. Add an acute_route rule: any glucose below REF-DM-HYPO-L2, or below REF-DM-HYPO-L1 on insulin or a sulfonylurea, or mental_status not alert with a low glucose -> immediate acute_signal (route only, no treatment text). If the live v0.1.0 catalog already routes this, cite it and add a vignette proving it; none of the 34 vignettes contains a low glucose.
findings.done: Control bands have a LOW band below 3.9. Rules DM-ACU-ROUTE-06 (below 3.0, LO, or not resolving) and -07 (below 3.9 on insulin or a sulfonylurea). DMV-41.

findings.where: 50-act.json DM-ACT-REFER-FOOT-01, DM-ACT-REFER-PVD-01; feature active_foot_ulcer (read by no rule)
findings.finding: A foot ulcer on its own triggers nothing. DM-ACT-REFER-FOOT-01 needs gangrene present or an infection grade recorded; active_foot_ulcer, previous_foot_ulcer and ulcer_area_reduction_4w are read by no rule. Evaluator: 60-year-old known diabetic, active_foot_ulcer true, infection not graded -> only the two education steps fire. Adding pulses 'absent' and infection 'none' gives a ROUTINE vascular referral (DM-ACT-REFER-PVD-01); an ulcer with absent pulses is limb-threatening. The rule's label 'an ulcer with infection' also does not test for an ulcer (rule 10).
findings.why: The pack's own quote (REF-DM-FOOT-EVERY-VISIT, WHO HEARTS-D): 'Examine feet for ulcers at every visit. REFER to higher level of care if ulcer present or pulse absent.' The market trader who walks on an ulcer with numb feet does not volunteer infection; the nurse ticks 'ulcer' and moves on. Late referral is how Ugandan patients lose legs.
findings.reviewerFix: Add: active_foot_ulcer present -> refer to higher level (urgent; same_day if foot_infection_grade in moderate/severe, foot_gangrene, or pedal_pulses in reduced/absent). Make REFER-FOOT-01 read active_foot_ulcer so the label is true. Escalate absent pulses WITH an ulcer to same_day (critical limb ischaemia is on WHO's same-day list). Add the vignette.
findings.done: DM-ACT-REFER-FOOT-02 (any active ulcer), FOOT-01 now reads the ulcer, FOOT-03 (gangrene or deep infection without an ulcer). An ulcer with absent pulses is same-day. DMV-42, DMV-43.

findings.finding: Pregnancy has no district pathway and unknown pregnancy is treated as not pregnant. (1) Every pregnancy criterion reads laboratory plasma glucose only. Evaluator, health centre with a meter: 30 weeks pregnant, meter 13.0 with thirst and polyuria -> DM-SUS-SYMP-01, DM-SUS-INCID-01 (routine) and 'offer a 75 g OGTT' (not available there); both pregnancy sets 'unavailable'; no referral proposed. Fasting meter 6.2 at 30 weeks -> only 'offer an OGTT'. (2) The non-pregnant set applies unless pregnant is recorded TRUE: a 28-year-old woman never asked about pregnancy with HbA1c 6.6 twice is computed as diabetes 'met' on HbA1c, the test the pack blocks in pregnancy. (3) DM-CON-PREG-02's label omits the random-with-symptoms criterion that who_2013_diabetes_in_pregnancy carries.
findings.why: Breaches rule 8 (a district site must reach a safe next step) and rule 2 (not asked is being read as 'not pregnant'). Hyperglycaemia at 30 weeks is time-critical for mother and baby; most Ugandan antenatal care happens at HC III with a meter. A woman with a symptomatic glucose of 13 leaves with a routine suggestion.
findings.reviewerFix: Add a pregnancy district rule: pregnant AND any capillary or plasma glucose in the pack's diabetes range (fasting >= 7.0, or >= 11.1 otherwise) -> same_day referral to specialised antenatal care; pregnant AND fasting capillary >= 5.1 -> refer for laboratory confirmation. Put the question of accepting a plasma-calibrated meter for GDM to the CSO (FIGO 2015 discusses it; do not adopt a number without reading it). For a woman of reproductive age with pregnant not recorded, make the general set 'insufficient: pregnancy status needed' rather than applying it. Add both vignettes.
findings.done: DM-CON-PREG-03 and -04 give the meter-only antenatal site a referral rule. Unknown pregnancy in a woman who could be pregnant now makes the non-pregnant criteria set 'insufficient'. DMV-44 to DMV-46. Whether a meter may be used for gestational criteria is D-DM-28.

findings.finding: The display string of a target reads 'HbA1c below 8.0% during TB treatment'. A target is the thing most likely to be shown to the patient (agreed target, patient summary, printed plan). The item is tagged restricted class tb and its note says the reason is never shown on a patient-facing surface, but the reason is in the display text itself.
findings.why: Breaches rule 7. TB status leaks through the label of an ordinary diabetes target. The tag travels with the rule but cannot redact a string.
findings.reviewerFix: Change display to 'HbA1c below 8.0%' and hold the reason in a restricted, clinician-only field. Sweep every display/label/action of items tagged with a restricted class for the same pattern.
findings.done: Reason removed from the target's display; x.restrictedReason holds it. Every item that reads a restricted feature now carries x.neutralDisplay, and the build fails if one is missing.

findings.finding: The label says 'Known type 2 diabetes, HbA1c below 6.5%, off all glucose-lowering medicines for 3 months or more' but the predicates test only dm_status == known; type is never checked. Evaluator: person recorded as type 1 who has stopped insulin for 3 months, HbA1c 6.3, meter 15 -> remission 'met', and nothing else fires.
findings.why: Breaches rule 10 and is unsafe: a type 1 in the honeymoon period, a ketosis-prone patient, or anyone whose HbA1c reads falsely low (haemolysis, malaria, sickle trait, recent transfusion, all common here) and who has run out of insulin is offered the word 'remission'. The consensus definition is for type 2 only.
findings.reviewerFix: Add dm_type_recorded == type_2 to the criterion, and require a concurrent glucose below the diabetes range where HbA1c validity caveats exist. Never evaluate it when dm_type_recorded is type_1 or unclassified. Add the negative vignette.
findings.done: The criterion requires type 2 recorded; the set is 'not met' when a glucose in the diabetes range is on record. DMV-47.

findings.finding: Every 'due' rule is written as months_since_X >= N. For a person never tested or never screened the value is missing, so the rule is 'insufficient' and never fires. Evaluator: adult on ART, never had a glucose -> nothing fires; known diabetic never had an eye, kidney, foot or nerve check -> only education fires. The notes defer to Design B, but DM-SUS-RISK-NEVER covers only age-and-weight eligibility and DM-ACT-SCREEN-NEVER covers only eye, kidney and foot: never-tested people on ART, on antipsychotics, after pancreatitis or after GDM, and never-done HbA1c, sensation and lipid checks, are covered by nothing.
findings.why: The never-screened are common in Uganda and are the highest-risk group; the rules as written serve only people already in a recall system. This is the 'rule silenced because it depends on a value that is rarely recorded' trap.
findings.reviewerFix: Give each screening item an explicit 'never done' state the predicate can read (e.g. a boolean X_ever_done, or let the engine treat 'no dated result on record' as a recordable fact distinct from 'not asked'), and write each rule as ANY(never done | months >= N). Add a vignette per lane.
findings.done: Seven 'never done' features, each an explicit answer. Every due rule is 'never, or N months since'. DMV-48, DMV-49.

findings.finding: Meter criteria require capillary_glucose_context to match exactly. Evaluator: thin 24-year-old, weight loss, meter 22, context not recorded -> diagnosis 'insufficient'; with context 'two_hours_after_food' -> not diagnostic either (that option matches no criterion although a post-meal reading is a random glucose). Meanwhile DM-SUS-INCID-01 fires telling the clinician the value is 'diagnostic with symptoms'.
findings.why: A value of 22 exceeds every threshold in the table whatever the timing, and WHO defines random as any time regardless of meals. The system contradicts itself and withholds a diagnosis on the patient who most needs one, at the sites that have only a meter.
findings.reviewerFix: Add a criterion: capillary_glucose >= REF-DM-DX-OGTT2H-CAP (12.2, the highest meter threshold in the set) with symptoms, any or no context; and let who_hd_random_cap_symptoms accept context in [random, two_hours_after_food]. Add the vignette without a context.
findings.done: New criterion: any meter reading 12.2 or more with symptoms. The random criterion accepts 'after food'. DMV-50.

findings.finding: A single diabetes-range fasting glucose, HbA1c or 2-hour value without symptoms fires nothing. DMV-02 (fasting 7.4, no symptoms) expects 'fires: []' and passes; evaluator with HbA1c 7.1 alone also fires nothing. Only a RANDOM value of 11.1 or more has a 'repeat on another day, do not leave it' rule (DM-SUS-INCID-01).
findings.why: Rule 5 is honoured (no diagnosis) but the patient is dropped: WHO's instruction, quoted in the pack, is 'repeat the test ... as soon as practicable on a subsequent day'. The expected result of DMV-02 is clinically incomplete even though the build passes.
findings.reviewerFix: Add DM-SUS-INCID-02: any of fasting_pg >= 7.0, fasting capillary >= 7.0, hba1c >= 6.5 (no caveat in force), ogtt_2h_pg >= 11.1, with repeat_abnormal_result not recorded true -> 'One result in the diabetes range: repeat on another day' (soon). Change DMV-02 to expect it.
findings.done: DM-SUS-INCID-02. DMV-02 now expects it.

findings.finding: The rule can never fire. It needs dm_status != known, but dm_status has one option ('known'): when recorded it equals known (not met), when not recorded the predicate is 'insufficient'.
findings.why: A person collecting glibenclamide or insulin with no diabetes on the problem list is exactly who falls outside every 'established' rule (no screening, no hypo logic). The reconciliation rule meant to catch them is dead code.
findings.reviewerFix: Either add explicit options to dm_status (e.g. not_known) and require them, or write the rule as dm_status absent-or-not-known using a construct the grammar evaluates when the value is missing. Add a vignette.
findings.done: dm_status gains 'not_known'; Design B rule DM-SUS-RECON-02 covers the absent case. DMV-51.

findings.where: 30-classify.json DM-CLS-T1-01; 50-act.json DM-ACT-RX-01 contraindication contra_ketosis; vignette DMV-10
findings.finding: ketosis_at_presentation is a permanent historical fact used as a current trigger. Evaluator: ketosis-prone type 2, presented in ketosis 8 years ago, came off insulin and stayed well, clinician has recorded type 2, HbA1c 7.8 on no medicine -> DM-CLS-T1-01 fires SAME-DAY ('treat as insulin-deficient until shown otherwise', refer same day) at every visit for life, and DM-ACT-RX-01 is permanently 'contraindicated'. The rule also contradicts the pack's own ketosis_prone_type_2 classification. In DMV-10 the same rule is expected to fire on euglycaemic ketoacidosis from an SGLT2 inhibitor, which its own mimic list names.
findings.why: Breaches rule 9 (an urgent rule that fires forever is ignored) and blocks the usual maintenance step for a phenotype that is common in sub-Saharan Africa.
findings.reviewerFix: Split the rule: ketones 2+ or more NOW -> same_day (unchanged). ketosis_at_presentation alone -> routine type review, and suppress when insulin_stopped_without_relapse is present or a clinician has recorded the type since. Make contra_ketosis read current ketones only. Remove DM-CLS-T1-01 from DMV-10's expected list or reword it for the SGLT2 case.
findings.done: T1-01 reads ketones now only, and not on an SGLT2 inhibitor. New routine rule T1-03 for a past ketosis, silent once settled. RX-01's contraindication reads current ketones. DMV-52; DMV-10 corrected.

findings.where: 30-classify.json DM-CLS-T1-02, DM-CLS-ATYP-01 (urgency routine, runWhen established); 60-acute-route.json DM-ACU-ROUTE-01
findings.finding: The newly diagnosed lean young adult is under-called. (1) WHO HEARTS-D's same-day list, quoted in REF-DM-CLS-T1-SAMEDAY, includes 'clinical suspicion of type 1 diabetes in newly diagnosed patient'; the pack makes that same-day only when ketones are 2+ and leaves a 24-year-old with BMI 17, weight loss and glucose 22 (ketones negative or 1+) at 'routine'. (2) Classification rules run only once diabetes is 'established', so nothing says 'do not assume type 2' at the visit where the diagnosis is made. (3) HEARTS-D's severe stratum 'FPG >= 15 mmol/L and symptomatic -> test urine ketones' (REF-DM-ACU-FPG-SEVERE-SYMPT, used by no rule) is not implemented; the ketone prompt starts at 18.
findings.why: The classic fatal error in Uganda is the thin young adult labelled type 2, sent home on tablets and returning in ketoacidosis. Urine ketones lag and can be low early.
findings.reviewerFix: Make DM-CLS-T1-02 same_day when the diagnosis is new (years_since_diagnosis < 1 or diagnosed this encounter) and at least two features are present; run T1-01/T1-02/ATYP-01 as soon as a diagnostic criterion is met, not only after confirmation. Add a ketone-test rule for fasting glucose >= REF-DM-ACU-FPG-SEVERE-SYMPT with symptoms.
findings.done: Classification rules run as soon as a criterion is met. New same-day rule T1-04 for the newly diagnosed. New ketone rule at 15 mmol/L with symptoms (ROUTE-08). DMV-50.

findings.finding: C-peptide below 200 pmol/L 'supports' and 600 or more 'refutes' type 1 with no timing guard. The pack's own REF-DM-CLS-CPEP-TIMING says C-peptide is read only beyond 3 years from diagnosis and not within 2 weeks of a hyperglycaemic emergency; neither is in the predicates or the label. REF-DM-CLS-CPEP-LOW is marked recheck 'not_found', confidence low, needs CSO input (the 200 figure could not be read from the source figure), yet it drives a live criterion.
findings.why: Soon after ketoacidosis glucose toxicity suppresses C-peptide in ketosis-prone type 2, which would be 'supported' as type 1; a type 1 in the first years can exceed 600 and be 'refuted', which invites stopping insulin.
findings.reviewerFix: Add years_since_diagnosis >= 3 (REF-DM-CLS-CPEP-TIMING) to both criteria and say so in the labels; add a 'not within 2 weeks of a hyperglycaemic emergency' input or caveat. Hold t1_cpeptide_low out of the catalog until a person has read the figure.
findings.done: Both C-peptide criteria are held out of the live rules (x.heldOut) until a person reads the source figure.

findings.finding: Display says 'Very high glucose or HbA1c, or weight loss with symptoms: ADA says consider insulin whatever the current treatment'; predicates are dm_status == known AND any of HbA1c > 10, any glucose >= 16.7, or unexplained weight loss alone. It fires same-day on people already on insulin, on type 1, and on weight loss alone with no glucose criterion. The source (rec. 9.20) is for adults with TYPE 2 and names symptoms of hyperglycaemia or very high values.
findings.why: Rule 10 (display and predicates differ) and rule 9: glucose at or above 16.7 is routine in Ugandan clinics, so a same-day prompt fires on a large share of attendances, including a nonsensical 'consider insulin' on insulin users. Weight loss in a diabetic here is as often TB, HIV or cancer.
findings.reviewerFix: Require dm_type_recorded in [type_2, unclassified] and glucose_lowering_therapy != insulin; make the weight-loss arm require a concurrent glucose or HbA1c above target, and name TB, HIV and malignancy in the text. Make display and label identical.
findings.done: RX-04 is for type 2 or unclassified, not on insulin, and needs a glucose or HbA1c criterion. Weight loss has its own rule (DM-CLS-WTLOSS-01) naming TB, HIV and cancer.

findings.finding: The sulfonylurea step carries no contraindication or caution. Evaluator: eGFR 28 -> RX-02 'add a sulfonylurea' fires. It also fires at any age, with frailty, food insecurity, irregular meals or a previous severe low. RX-01 fires when eGFR was never measured (the contraindication is 'insufficient', so the step shows as clean) and tests a fixed 7.0 although its display says 'above target': a frail person on the accepted relaxed tier with HbA1c 7.4 is told they are above target.
findings.why: WHO's own text (REF-DM-RX-GLIB-AGE quote) warns against glibenclamide 'in patients for whom hypoglycaemia is a concern', and the ADA table quoted for glibenclamide_ckd says other sulfonylureas are started conservatively in kidney disease 'to avoid hypoglycemia'; the pack computes a hypoglycaemia risk band and then ignores it at the step that creates the risk. Missing kidney function is being read as 'no contraindication' (rule 2).
findings.reviewerFix: RX-02: add cautions shown with the step when hypoglycaemia_risk_ada is high or raised, egfr < 30, food_insecurity or meals_irregular present, age >= 75 or frailty present. RX-01: when egfr is not recorded, show 'kidney function not known' on the step; compare against the accepted target tier, not a fixed 7.0.
findings.done: RX-02 carries cautions. RX-01 reports 'kidney function not known' and is silent inside an accepted relaxed target. DMV-35, DMV-53.

findings.finding: The 'district pathway for the control axis' needs a laboratory. fasting_pg requires lab.glucose; a fasting METER reading is read by no control band, target or therapy step. Evaluator at a district site: known type 2, fasting meter 12.4, on metformin or on nothing -> only the two education steps fire; no band, no 'above target', DM-ACT-RX-01 unavailable. Urine protein 2+ on a strip also drives nothing in this pack.
findings.why: Rule 8. The pack accepts a fasting meter value for diagnosis (WHO: fasting capillary and venous plasma values are identical) but not for control, so the health centre that can diagnose cannot be told the patient is uncontrolled.
findings.reviewerFix: Let the control bands, tgt_fpg_surrogate and RX-01 also read capillary_glucose with context fasting (and two_hours_after_food for the post-meal band). Add a district vignette for control. Wire urine_protein_strip positive to 'abnormal, pending confirmation: refer for a laboratory ratio' if the live catalog does not.
findings.done: Two meter control tables, step RX-01B and a strip-positive step. DMV-53.

findings.finding: 'Kidney disease that does not fit diabetes: refer' (same_day) fires on egfr_fall_percent > 20 with no time window, no 'sustained', and no exclusion for a recent start of an ACE inhibitor, ARB or SGLT2 inhibitor. The source quote (KDIGO) is 'a sustained fall in GFR of >20%, or >30% in those initiating hemodynamically active therapies', and it is a referral criterion for CKD, not a sign of non-diabetic disease. ADA's clue is 'rapidly decreasing eGFR'.
findings.why: A 20% fall from baseline over ten years is ordinary diabetic kidney disease; the rule will eventually tell most patients with nephropathy that their disease 'does not fit diabetes' and demand a same-day referral that Uganda's few nephrology units cannot absorb. It also contradicts the creatinine-rise flag, which tolerates 30% after a RAS blocker.
findings.reviewerFix: Separate the two ideas: (a) non-diabetic clue = nephrotic picture, active sediment, rapidly rising albumin, haematuria, or a rapid fall (define the window with the CSO); (b) KDIGO referral for a sustained fall > 20% (routine, labelled as progression). Exclude the 4 weeks after starting or increasing a RAS blocker.
findings.done: CKD-01 keeps only the non-diabetic clues. Progression has its own routine step (REFER-EGFR-03) with KDIGO's 30% allowance. DMV-60.

findings.finding: Two flags are narrower than their own source. (1) The quote behind metformin_during_acute_illness (A4-64) says 'consider holding metformin AND SGLT2 inhibitors when oral intake cannot be maintained'; the flag covers metformin only. In DMV-10 (SGLT2 inhibitor, vomiting, ketones 3+) the therapy flag raised is about metformin and none concerns the SGLT2 inhibitor. The label also says 'acutely unwell' while the display says 'with poor intake', which is not tested. (2) The pregnancy red flag covers ACE inhibitors, ARBs and statins; a pregnant woman on a sulfonylurea, SGLT2 inhibitor, GLP-1 agonist, DPP-4 inhibitor or pioglitazone is flagged by nothing, although the pack's note cites WHO 2025 'metformin or insulin under specialist care'.
findings.why: The medicine that causes euglycaemic ketoacidosis is the one left unflagged during the illness that precipitates it.
findings.reviewerFix: Add an SGLT2 arm (or a sibling flag) to the acute-illness flag; align its display and label. Add an amber/red flag for pregnant AND glucose_lowering_therapy in [glibenclamide, gliclazide, glimepiride, sglt2_inhibitor, glp1_ra, dpp4_inhibitor, pioglitazone]: 'review today with the antenatal team'.
findings.done: Red flag for an SGLT2 inhibitor in acute illness; red flag for other glucose-lowering medicines in pregnancy. DMV-10, DMV-58.

findings.finding: Nothing in the catalog recognises a person who needs insulin and is not taking it. There is no feature for insulin omission and no rule on dm_type_recorded == type_1 with insulin absent from glucose_lowering_therapy. Evaluator: type 1 recorded, therapy 'none', meter 15 -> only education fires (and 'remission' is met, see above). The only safeguard is a draft exam-catalogue flag that depends on a medicine-adherence atom the pack itself says is unconfirmed.
findings.why: Stock-outs, cost and fasting make stopped insulin a regular event in Ugandan clinics, and insulin omission is one of the commonest precipitants of ketoacidosis. DM-ACT-EDU-04 teaches 'never stop insulin' to those who are on it and says nothing to those who have stopped.
findings.reviewerFix: Add: dm_type_recorded == type_1 (or ketosis-prone/insulin-deficient flag) AND glucose_lowering_therapy != insulin -> same_day 'Not on insulin: check glucose and ketones now, find out why' (no dose). Add an 'insulin stopped or missed' history item the NCD engine can read.
findings.done: ROUTE-09 (type 1 not on insulin) and ROUTE-10 (insulin stopped, missed or run out). DMV-47.

findings.where: 60-acute-route.json DM-ACU-ROUTE-01; feature capillary_glucose (unit mmol/L, no range); clerking FLAG-EX-GLU-KETONE-TEST
findings.finding: (1) Urgency: every glucose of 18 or more is 'immediate', with or without symptoms, while the exam catalogue raises the same trigger as 'caution'. Readings of 18 or more are common in Ugandan diabetes clinics; an interrupt on each will be dismissed by reflex (rule 9), and the two layers disagree. (2) Units and limits: glucose features take a bare number in mmol/L with no plausibility range. Many meters in circulation here read mg/dL; '126' typed into the field is diagnostic of everything and fires the immediate rule. A meter showing 'HI' or 'LO' cannot be recorded at all, so the two most dangerous readings fire nothing.
findings.why: A rule that cries wolf at 18 will not be read at 38; and the sickest patient's reading is unrecordable.
findings.reviewerFix: Make ROUTE-01 same_day when no symptom is recorded and immediate when any of vomiting, abdominal pain, deep breathing, dehydration, drowsiness is present; align the exam flag. Add a unit selector or a hard plausibility check on glucose entry, and explicit 'HI' / 'LO' options that the acute rules read.
findings.done: ROUTE-01 is same-day; the interrupt is rule 11. HI and LO are recordable and satisfy the rules. Unit entry (mmol/L or mg/dL) and a plausibility range are platform work: engine change EC-6.

findings.finding: The IDF 1-hour table (non-pregnant adults) has no 'when' and is applied in pregnancy. DMV-23 (26 weeks, 1-hour 9.2) is computed as 'Intermediate hyperglycaemia (IDF)' although 9.2 is below the WHO gestational 1-hour threshold of 10.0; a 1-hour of 10.5 in pregnancy would show 'intermediate' when it is diagnostic of GDM, and 11.6 would show 'Diabetes range (IDF); repeat to confirm'.
findings.why: Two contradictory readings of one number on the same screen, one of them from a standard that does not apply to her.
findings.reviewerFix: Give the table a not-pregnant condition (and an established == false condition), or add a pregnancy 1-hour table from who_2013_gdm. Assert in DMV-23 that no IDF band is shown.
findings.done: The IDF table is not read in pregnancy. DMV-23 asserts it.

findings.finding: Runs 'always' and proposes diagnosis.reclassify with flag drug_associated on a single glucose of 11.1 or more in anyone on steroids, including people with long-established diabetes. Evaluator: known type 2 for years, now on prednisolone, meter 15 -> 'Hyperglycaemia in a person on steroids: record it as medicine-associated'. The capillary arm ignores context.
findings.why: The display is an instruction to relabel, and the commonest steroid patient with a high glucose is a known diabetic whose control has worsened. A drug-associated label implies it will resolve when the steroid stops.
findings.reviewerFix: Run only when diabetes is not established (or was diagnosed after the steroid began); change the display to 'consider' and keep the label a clinician decision. For established diabetes on steroids fire a monitoring prompt instead (the source: monitor post-meal or random glucose).
findings.done: DRUG-01 runs only when diabetes is not established and no longer proposes a relabel. Known diabetes on steroids gets a monitoring prompt. DMV-56.

findings.finding: The 'raised glucose during acute illness may be transitory' and TB caveats are attached to random_pg only. At a district site the reading is capillary_glucose, and a fasting value is fasting_pg, so neither carries the caveat. An adult with severe malaria or pneumonia, meter 12.5 and 'thirst' is computed as diabetes with no warning shown on the value used.
findings.why: WHO (quoted): severe hyperglycaemia under acute stress 'should not in itself be regarded as diagnostic'. Fever and dehydration produce thirst, so the symptom gate does not protect. A lifelong label follows.
findings.reviewerFix: Attach both caveats to capillary_glucose, random_pg and fasting_pg. Consider making diagnosis 'pending re-test after recovery' when acute_illness_current is present and ketones are not raised.
findings.done: The illness and TB caveats attach to meter and fasting glucose too. They warn and do not block: whether to hold the diagnosis until recovery is D-DM-29.

findings.finding: Potassium 6.0 to 6.4 falls between the two rules. Evaluator: potassium 6.2 on an ACE inhibitor with eGFR 25 -> an amber flag whose action reads 'reduce or stop the ACE inhibitor or ARB only as a last resort'. The pack's own KDIGO quote (A6-60) says: 'Moderate K+ 6.0-6.4: clinically unwell or AKI - assess and treat in hospital; unexpected result - repeat within 24 hours'. The amber wording is KDIGO's advice for chronic hyperkalaemia above 5.5, applied to a level its other table sends to hospital.
findings.why: A reassuring 'last resort' message beside a potassium of 6.3 in a patient with an eGFR of 25.
findings.reviewerFix: Add a band 6.0 to below 6.5: same_day, 'KDIGO: repeat within 24 hours; if unwell or kidney function has fallen, assess in hospital' (route, no treatment). Cap the amber flag's text at below 6.0.
findings.done: ROUTE-16 for potassium 6.0 to 6.4. The amber flag stops below 6.0 and no longer reassures. DMV-54.

findings.finding: The rule requires weeks_since_antipsychotic_start >= 12 AND months_since_glucose_test >= 12. The source (quoted) says screen at baseline, repeat 12 to 16 weeks after starting, then annually. Anyone who had the baseline test the guideline requires has a glucose test within 12 months, so the 12-week re-test, the point of the rule and of its display, can never fire for them; and anyone never tested is silenced by the missing value.
findings.why: Olanzapine and clozapine can produce diabetes and ketoacidosis within months; the 12-week check is the one that catches it.
findings.reviewerFix: Fire when weeks_since_antipsychotic_start >= 12 and no glucose test has been done SINCE the start (needs a weeks-since-test or 'tested since start' input), plus the annual arm and a never-tested arm.
findings.done: Two rules: the 12-week re-test (no test since the start) and the yearly test. DMV-57.

findings.finding: 'Established cardiovascular disease: antiplatelet treatment is for secondary prevention' fires on cvd_established, which lumps heart attack, angina, stroke, TIA and peripheral artery disease. It does not separate haemorrhagic from ischaemic stroke, names no bleeding caution, and (having no 'on antiplatelet' input) fires at every visit including for people already taking one.
findings.why: Haemorrhagic stroke is a larger share of stroke in sub-Saharan Africa than in the populations behind the source, and CT is often unavailable, so 'stroke' in the record frequently means type unknown. A standing prompt toward antiplatelets for that group is unsafe; a prompt that never clears is ignored.
findings.reviewerFix: Add text 'not after haemorrhagic stroke or where the stroke type is unknown; check bleeding risk', add an on_antiplatelet input with 'absent' semantics like on_statin, and consider splitting stroke out of cvd_established.
findings.done: The prompt clears once the person is on an antiplatelet and is contraindicated after a bleeding or untyped stroke. The exclusion has no quoted source: for CSO signature.

findings.where: 50-act.json DM-ACT-RX-10, therapyFlags glibenclamide_age_60, hypoglycaemia_needing_help_on_treatment; feature hypo_worst_12m
findings.finding: RX-10's display says 'A low needing help, or repeated lows' but only needed_help is tested; hypo_worst_12m has no option for a measured level 2 low (below 3.0) or for frequency, though the quoted ADA text says 'one or more episodes of level 2 or 3 hypoglycemia should prompt reevaluation'. An elderly woman on glibenclamide with repeated self-treated lows gets no review prompt (only the age flag). WHO's glibenclamide warning 'in patients for whom hypoglycaemia is a concern' is implemented for age only: under 60 with lows, food insecurity or irregular meals, nothing fires.
findings.why: Rule 10, and the quoted threshold for action is not the one coded. Recurrent 'mild' lows on glibenclamide precede the fatal one.
findings.reviewerFix: Add options to hypo_worst_12m (or a second field) for a measured value below REF-DM-HYPO-L2 and for repeated lows; fire RX-10 on those too. Extend the glibenclamide flag: glibenclamide AND any of hypo_worst_12m != none, food_insecurity, meals_irregular.
findings.done: Two new answers (a reading below 3.0; repeated lows). RX-10, the flag and the risk model read them. Glibenclamide has a second flag for hypoglycaemia concern.

findings.where: 50-act.json DM-ACT-REFER-* (omissions against REF-DM-ACT-REFER-SAMEDAY); feature chest_pain_or_stroke_symptoms (read by no rule)
findings.finding: WHO HEARTS-D's same-day list is quoted in the dossier but only partly implemented. Not implemented in the catalog: 'symptoms of heart disease or stroke' (the feature chest_pain_or_stroke_symptoms exists and nothing reads it); 'hypoglycaemia unresolved by treatment'; 'critical limb ischaemia'; 'anuria'.
findings.why: Heart attack and stroke are leading causes of death in people with diabetes; the pack created the input for their symptoms and wired it to nothing.
findings.reviewerFix: Add same_day/immediate referral rules for chest_pain_or_stroke_symptoms present, and for the other listed items, or cite the catalogue that owns each and add a vignette showing it fires.
findings.done: ROUTE-17 (heart or stroke symptoms), REFER-LIMB-01, anuria in REFER-EGFR-01, REFER-BP-03, and 'not resolving' in ROUTE-06. DMV-59.

findings.finding: (1) Mild non-proliferative retinopathy is recalled at 24 months and moderate at 12, the far end of ICO's low-resource ranges ('1-2 yrs', '6-12 mos'). ADA, quoted in the same item, says that if any retinopathy is present examinations are 'at least annually', and the pack's own note says the ICO schedule applies only where diabetes is controlled; no interval reads control. (2) DM-ACT-REFER-EYE-01 is 'urgent' for moderate retinopathy, whose own note says 'at the next 6 to 12 month examination'.
findings.why: Most patients with retinopathy in Uganda are above target; giving them the longest permissible interval is the unsafe default. Calling moderate disease 'urgent' while severe and proliferative share the same word blunts the signal (rule 9).
findings.reviewerFix: Use the near end of each ICO range (12 and 6 months) unless control is at target, or state the control condition in the interval. Split the referral rule: severe, proliferative or centre-involving oedema = urgent; moderate = routine referral.
findings.done: Mild and moderate retinopathy use the near end of ICO's range unless control is confirmed at target. Referral split: urgent for sight-threatening disease, routine for moderate.

findings.finding: Labels that do not say what the predicates test (rule 10). RX-12: display 'Painful neuropathy', predicates test numbness/burning/tingling with a sign, so a painless numb foot gets a pain-medicine prompt. PANC-01: label 'fatty stools with recurrent upper abdominal pain', predicate is steatorrhoea alone (recurrent_abdominal_pain is unused), which fires on metformin diarrhoea. INCID-01: label 'Random glucose', but the capillary arm ignores context. NEURO-03: label omits 'known diabetes'; 'resting pulse' is any pulse. tgt_hba1c_older_healthy: display says 'healthy older adult', predicate is age 65 or over.
findings.why: Each tells the clinician something the engine did not check.
findings.reviewerFix: RX-12: add a pain input or reword to 'symptomatic neuropathy'. PANC-01: add recurrent_abdominal_pain to an ALL with steatorrhoea. INCID-01: test context == random or reword. NEURO-03 and the target: reword to match.
findings.done: Five labels reworded or predicates changed to match.

findings.finding: Boundary error against the quoted source. WHO: 'an FPG value of <=7.0 mmol/L and a postprandial PG value of <=9.0 mmol/L can serve as surrogates'. The bands end 'At target' below 7.0 and below 9.0 (the evaluator uses x < to), and RX-01 treats fasting >= 7.0 as above target, so exactly 7.0 and 9.0 are called above target.
findings.why: Contradiction with REF-DM-CTRL-FPG-SURROGATE ('at or below').
findings.reviewerFix: Make the upper edges inclusive for these two tables, and RX-01 fasting_pg > 7.0.
findings.done: RX-01 now uses 'above 7.0' for fasting glucose. The bands keep 'below' and say so: WHO disagrees with itself at exactly 7.0 and 9.0 (D-DM-13).

findings.finding: Action texts give a direction of dose change without a number: 'ADA says the amount should be reduced', 'reduce or stop the ACE inhibitor'.
findings.why: Rule 1 forbids titration anywhere. These are borderline; the CSO should rule.
findings.reviewerFix: Reword to 'review with the prescriber' and cite the source, or record an explicit CSO exception.
findings.done: Three flag actions reworded to 'review with the prescriber'. The reference text for metformin below 45 still paraphrases ADA: D-DM-31.

findings.finding: Rules with no stop condition or loose urgency. PREG-02 ('re-test 6 to 12 weeks after the birth') fires at any postpartum_weeks >= 6, for years, and after the test is done. PREG-01 keeps offering an OGTT after one is on record (DMV-23). RISK-01 and POP-TB-01 fire at every visit however recently the person was tested. PAED-01 is 'immediate' for weight loss alone in a child, which in Uganda is usually undernutrition, TB or HIV.
findings.why: Noise that trains people to dismiss the lane.
findings.reviewerFix: Add an upper bound and 'no glucose test since the birth' to PREG-02; suppress PREG-01 when an OGTT value is recorded; add a months_since_glucose_test arm to RISK-01 and TB-01; make PAED-01 same_day for weight loss alone and immediate for the polyuria/thirst/bed-wetting arm.
findings.done: Stop conditions added to PREG-01, PREG-02, RISK-01, TB-01; PAED-01 split by urgency. RISK-02 relies on the engine showing it once per episode.

findings.finding: Three live items rest on citations marked unverified: the Kampala dolutegravir signal, the Uganda HIV-chapter dolutegravir-metformin interaction, and 'eGFR is not valid in pregnancy' (quote field reads 'NOT FOUND in the pages opened'), which is also a diagnosis-blocking caveat. The dolutegravir-metformin action warns of 'hypoglycaemia', which metformin alone does not cause, and will fire on nearly every person with HIV and diabetes because dolutegravir is first line.
findings.why: A CSO cannot sign a rule whose source nobody read; a permanent amber flag on the standard regimen is noise.
findings.reviewerFix: Read the Uganda Consolidated HIV Guidelines and the Lancet HIV paper before release; mark these items needsCsoInput until then. Reword the interaction action to what the source says once read (no dose).
findings.done: The dolutegravir-metformin text now quotes UCG 2023, read verbatim at verification. The Kampala signal and the eGFR-in-pregnancy caveat are marked needsCsoInput; the pregnancy caveat no longer blocks.

findings.where: 50-act.json glibenclamide_age_60, DM-ACT-RX-02; feature could_conceive vs pregnant/prior_gdm/pcos
findings.finding: Uganda fit. The flag and the step say 'gliclazide preferred', while the pack's own EMHSLU note places gliclazide at tertiary level and glimepiride (with metformin) at primary care and records glibenclamide as deleted in 2023. could_conceive is tagged sexual_reproductive_health but pregnant, gestation_weeks, prior_gdm and pcos are not.
findings.why: A district clinician is advised to use a medicine they cannot get; restricted-class tagging is inconsistent (rule 7 intent).
findings.reviewerFix: Add the EMHSLU level of care to the flag text ('where gliclazide is not available at this level, see EMHSLU') once the list is read; ask the CSO whether pregnancy-related features belong to the restricted class.
findings.done: RX-02 and the glibenclamide flag point to the level of care. Which sulfonylurea at which level is D-DM-22; whether pregnancy features are a restricted class is D-DM-30.

findings.finding: The 34 vignettes do not contain: any low glucose; an HHS picture; a foot ulcer; metformin with eGFR below 30; a person off insulin; a never-screened or never-tested person; a pregnant woman at a district site; a known-diabetic child; a meter reading with no context; a remission negative (type 1); a control assessment at a district site. Each of these fails or is silent in the reference evaluator (see findings above). DMV-15 (19-year-old, BMI 17, on no treatment) expects only routine rules.
findings.why: The build passes because the dangerous patients are not in the test set.
findings.reviewerFix: Add one vignette per item with the corrected expectations; treat 'nothing fires' on any of them as a build error.
findings.done: 26 vignettes added (DMV-35 to DMV-60), one for each gap named. Each must fire something or the build fails.

findings.finding: Any recorded glucose of 3.9 mmol/L or more is offered as evidence AGAINST hypoglycaemia in a person with diabetes. The atom has no timing or treatment qualifier, and the briefing does not say which reading the vital atom takes when there are several (presumably the latest). The profile's own note says the atom 'holds only for a glucose taken while symptomatic and BEFORE treatment' and that 'the evidence text must say so', but nothing in the atom, the engine-change list or the text field delivers that.
findings.why: dx.hypoglycaemia_dm is must-not-miss and time-critical. The usual patient has already had sugar at home, at triage or in resus before the clerking glucose is taken, so the first recorded value is often normal. If the atom reads the latest value, then after treatment the 'for' mark (hypoglycaemia_level) disappears and an 'against' mark appears in the same column. A junior can then mark the diagnosis unlikely with a three-word reason and discharge a patient on glibenclamide or long-acting insulin, in whom the low recurs for many hours. This is the opposite of what the STOP report gap was meant to close.
findings.reviewerFix: Remove the atom from this amendment. Re-add it only with an engine change that lets the glucose vital carry 'taken before any sugar, glucose or glucagon was given' and 'taken while symptomatic', and make the atom true only when both are recorded yes (unknown otherwise). Put the caveat in the evidence text itself, not in the profile note. Apply the same timing rule to the dx.dka 'against' atom (blood ketones below REF-DX-KETONE-NORMAL), which also reads the latest value and can be normal after treatment at a referring unit.
findings.done: The 'against' glucose atom is removed from the hypoglycaemia profile; the note says why and what the vital must record before one can return.

findings.where: clerking-v2/07-exam.amendment.json, classifiers.add.dr_review; flag FLAG-EX-DR-SIGHT; clerking-v2/10-plan-care.v1.json CARE-DR-REFER
findings.finding: The 'Retinopathy: next step' classifier reads only dr_grade, macula=centre_involving and view=inadequate, first match wins. It therefore returns 'review_1_to_2_years' for mild retinopathy with (a) macula = non_centre (oedema or exudate, centre spared), (b) macula = cannot_assess, (c) visual acuity worse than 6/12 or visual symptoms, and (d) an undilated direct view. It returns nothing at all when the clinician ticks the existing option seen = not_visualised instead of the new view = inadequate. CARE-DR-REFER repeats the same three grade windows and also omits non-centre oedema and the acuity rule, although it cites REF-DM-EYE-REFER-VA.
findings.why: The pack's own dossier says otherwise: REF-DM-EYE-RECALL-DME-NCI (ICO: non-centre-involving oedema re-examined in 3 months, referral recommended where laser exists), REF-DM-EYE-REFER-VA (refer if acuity is worse than 6/12 or there are visual symptoms, whatever the grade), REF-DM-EYE-REFER-NOVIEW (refer if acuity or an adequate view cannot be obtained), REF-DM-EYE-CONTROLLED-ONLY (the schedule applies only where diabetes is controlled) and REF-DM-EYE-METHOD (dilated ophthalmoscopy or photography by a trained person). The dx.diabetic_retinopathy note itself says 'a normal undilated direct ophthalmoscopy misses most retinopathy' and 'vision worse than 6/12 or any visual symptom is referred whatever the grade'. A screen that tells a clerking doctor 'review in 1 to 2 years' for a patient with macular oedema or reduced acuity delays sight-saving treatment. REF-EX-DR-RECALL already holds dme_non_centre = 3 months but no rule reads it.
findings.reviewerFix: Rewrite the classifier in this order: (1) refer within 1 month: pdr or macula centre_involving; (2) refer within 3 months: severe_npdr; (3) refer: macula cannot_assess, view inadequate, seen includes not_visualised, or visual acuity worse than 6/12 in either eye, or sym.blurred_vision yes; (4) re-examine in 3 months: macula non_centre; (5) moderate; (6) mild only when method is dilated or photograph AND view adequate AND acuity recorded 6/12 or better in both eyes; otherwise result 'incomplete' (as iwgdf_risk does). Take every interval from REF-EX-DR-RECALL rather than from the result id. Show the 'applies only where diabetes is controlled' caveat in the result reason. Add non-centre oedema and the acuity rule to CARE-DR-REFER. Make FLAG-EX-DR-SIGHT fire on rule 3 as well. Decide with the CSO whether Uganda's 2016 guideline (refer every person with diabetes to a retina centre) or ICO is the default and model both, rather than leaving the Uganda rule in a note.
findings.done: dr_review reordered, most urgent first; it now reads macula 'cannot assess', an inadequate or absent view, acuity worse than 6/12 and blurred vision, and returns 'incomplete' instead of a reassuring interval. Three care items replace one. Which rule governs (Uganda 2016 'refer all' or ICO) is D-DM-14.

findings.where: clerking-v2/10-plan-care.v1.json, every item whose problems include dx.dm_type1, dx.dm_type_unknown or dx.dm_type2 (CARE-DM-TARGET, CARE-DM-BP, CARE-DM-EYE, CARE-DM-KIDNEY, CARE-DM-LIPIDS, CARE-DM-CVD-RISK, CARE-DM-HYPO-REVIEW, CARE-DM-REVIEW, CARE-DM-MEDS-REVIEW, CARE-DM-STATIN)
findings.finding: No item in the suggested-care list has an age gate, and no clerking file contains one. A child or a 14-year-old with dx.dm_type1 on the board is shown adult management content: 'treat towards below 130/80', 'agree an individual target', adult eye and kidney screening intervals, the adult cardiovascular risk chart and the adult review cadence.
findings.why: Pack rule 3 and briefing Part 4.1: under 16 is recognition, classification support and referral only, with no management content. Most diabetes in children is type 1, and the dx.dka note itself anticipates children. Adult blood-pressure and glycaemic targets and adult screening start times are wrong for children. If the adult desk never clerks anyone under 16 this must be stated and enforced by the engine, not assumed.
findings.reviewerFix: Add a 'when' with a signed age reference (16 years) to every management, target, screening-interval and recall item, and add one under-16 item for the three diabetes problems: 'Under 16: refer to the paediatric or diabetes team today' (kind refer). Add a vignette of a 12-year-old with dx.dm_type1 showing that only recognition, ketone testing, education and referral items appear. State in the pack whether the adult v2 desk can be opened for a patient under 16.
findings.done: Every care item carries min_age_ref unless it is a referral or an acute test; a new item refers under-16s today. The age is REF-DX-ADULT-AGE, for CSO signature.

findings.where: clerking-v2/09-diagnosis.amendment.json, profile dx.hhs, suggest_against[0] (classifier ketone_band = dka_range)
findings.finding: Ketones in the 'dka_range' band are offered as evidence AGAINST the hyperosmolar state, while the same profile's note says ketones in that range 'point to a mixed picture, which is common and more dangerous: keep both on the board'. The band also includes a urine strip of 2+ with no blood value.
findings.why: dx.hhs is must-not-miss and time-critical. Mixed ketoacidosis and hyperosmolar state is common; a urine strip of 2+ is frequent in a vomiting, starved hyperosmolar patient. The matrix would nudge a junior to mark the hyperosmolar state unlikely exactly when the note says not to. The atom and the note contradict each other.
findings.reviewerFix: Delete the 'against' atom. If the CSO wants the 2024 consensus exclusion shown, show ketone_band as neutral context on the HHS card with the text 'ketones raised: consider a mixed picture', never as an 'against' mark.
findings.done: No 'against' atom on the hyperosmolar profile.

findings.where: clerking-v2/09-diagnosis.amendment.json, profile dx.dm_type1, suggest_against[0] (res:obs.c_peptide >= REF-DX-CPEP-HIGH); REF-DX-CPEP-LOW; REF-DX-CPEP-HIGH
findings.finding: A random C-peptide at or above 600 pmol/L is evidence AGAINST type 1 with only min_trust as a condition. The REF text requires a concurrent glucose and a sample within 5 hours of eating, and the source applies the bands to people on insulin some years after diagnosis; none of that is in the atom, and there is no maximum age for the result. REF-DX-CPEP-LOW says a low value 'indicates type 1' without saying that a low value during a hyperglycaemic crisis or with a low concurrent glucose is not interpretable (the dossier rates this entry confidence 'low').
findings.why: dx.dm_type1 is set must-not-miss in this amendment because missing it leads to ketoacidosis. C-peptide is preserved early in type 1 and is raised by kidney impairment. An 'against' mark from an early or unpaired sample can lead to insulin being withdrawn.
findings.reviewerFix: Remove the 'against' atom, or make it conditional on atoms the engine can check (on insulin, year_diagnosed at least the source's interval ago, paired glucose recorded). Until then show C-peptide as a result on the card with the source's conditions in the evidence text. Fix the REF-DX-CPEP-LOW meaning to carry the source's conditions and its 'low' confidence.
findings.done: No C-peptide atom for or against type 1; both clerking references removed.

findings.where: clerking-v2/09-diagnosis.amendment.json, profile dx.hhs suggest_for (res:derived.osmolality_effective > REF-DX-OSM-HHS); REF-DX-OSM-HHS; wiring/cfc-addendum.proposal.json derived.osmolality_effective
findings.finding: The atom compares EFFECTIVE osmolality (2 x sodium + glucose, the concept proposed in the CFC addendum) with REF-DX-OSM-HHS, whose value 320 mOsm/kg is the TOTAL osmolality threshold (2 x sodium + glucose + urea, mirror of REF-DM-ACU-HHS-OSM-TOTAL). The atom text also names a third thing, 'derived.osmolality'.
findings.why: The dossier holds both thresholds: effective above 300 (REF-DM-ACU-HHS-OSM-EFF) or total above 320. An effective osmolality of 305 to 320 meets the criterion and would not be marked. Formula and threshold do not match.
findings.reviewerFix: Either compare derived.osmolality_effective with a new REF-DX-OSM-HHS-EFF (mirror of REF-DM-ACU-HHS-OSM-EFF), or propose derived.osmolality_total and keep 320. State the formula in the REF meaning and make the atom text name the same concept as the atom.
findings.done: Effective osmolality is read against the effective threshold (300), from the dossier.

findings.where: clerking-v2/09-diagnosis.amendment.json, profiles dx.dm_type_unknown and dx.dm_type2, suggest_against (res:obs.glucose(ogtt_2h) < REF-DX-GLU-2H-IGT); note on dx.dm_type_unknown
findings.finding: A 2-hour value below 7.8 mmol/L alone is offered as evidence against diabetes. It is not conditional on the fasting value of the same test, on HbA1c, or on the patient not taking glucose-lowering treatment. The note says 'only a normal 2-hour OGTT counts against'.
findings.why: A person with a fasting value of 7.0 or more and a 2-hour value below 7.8 still has a diabetes-range result (isolated fasting hyperglycaemia). A normal 2-hour value in someone on metformin or a sulfonylurea refutes nothing. The matrix would show 'against' beside a diabetes-range fasting result from the same test.
findings.reviewerFix: Make the 'against' atom an 'all': 2-hour below REF-DX-GLU-2H-IGT AND fasting value of the same test below REF-DX-GLU-FASTING-IFG AND medicine_group glucose_lowering recorded not taken. Correct the note to 'a normal OGTT (fasting and 2-hour) off treatment'.
findings.done: The single-test OGTT 'against' atom is removed from both profiles.

findings.where: clerking-v2/09-diagnosis.amendment.json, profile dx.dm_type2 suggest_for (cls:waist_risk, cls:bmi_who, pmh:diabetes, glucose and HbA1c atoms) compared with dx.dm_type1 suggest_for
findings.finding: Type 2 lists waist band, BMI band, family history, past diabetes of any type, capillary glucose, laboratory glucose and HbA1c as evidence. Type 1 lists none of the glucose, HbA1c or past-diabetes atoms. So for any person with known diabetes and a raised glucose the type 2 column fills with several suggested marks and the type 1 column stays empty, and build adds two more to type 2.
findings.why: Pack rule 6 and briefing Part 4.2: type is never inferred from build; return unclassified rather than infer from phenotype. Glucose and HbA1c establish diabetes, not its type. The dx.dm_type_unknown note says 'build alone does not decide it in Uganda' and the type 2 note says a third of Ugandan adults with non-autoimmune diabetes are lean. An evidence count that is built to be lopsided will steer juniors to type 2 in a young, overweight, ketosis-prone or type 1 patient.
findings.reviewerFix: Keep the diabetes-establishing atoms (glucose, HbA1c, past diabetes) on dx.dm_type_unknown only, or put the identical set on both type profiles. Remove waist and BMI bands from type 2 evidence, or show them as context that is never counted. Leave on each type profile only discriminating evidence: reported type, insulin from diagnosis, ketones, C-peptide and antibodies under their conditions.
findings.done: Type 2 no longer lists glucose, HbA1c, any-type past diabetes, or build bands.

findings.where: clerking-v2/09-diagnosis.amendment.json, profiles dx.dm_type_unknown, dx.dm_type2, dx.diabetes_in_pregnancy and rule DDX-RESULT-HBA1C (res:obs.hba1c >= REF-DX-HBA1C-DM); clerking-v2/00-engine-changes.json EC-1
findings.finding: The dx.dm_type_unknown note promises that 'the engine shows the HbA1c with its date and marks it not usable for diagnosis with the reason' in pregnancy, haemoglobin variants, haemolysis, recent malaria or transfusion, iron or B12 deficiency and low eGFR. EC-1 specifies no such behaviour. The atom has only min_trust 3, which admits a point-of-care HbA1c, has no maximum age (REF-DX-RESULT-AGE-HBA1C is defined and used by nothing) and reads no certification or method context.
findings.why: Iron deficiency, sickle trait, malaria and pregnancy are common in Uganda and move HbA1c in both directions. As written, an HbA1c of 6.5% or more in an iron-deficient or pregnant patient is a plain suggested 'for' mark, and the safeguard exists only as a sentence in a note. The CFC already carries 'certification' and 'method' for HbA1c.
findings.reviewerFix: Add the validity behaviour to EC-1 as a specified, tested rule: a list of signed caveat atoms per concept that turns the result to 'not usable for diagnosis' with the reason, or drop the sentence from the note. Require certification or laboratory method for the diagnostic atom. State how a restricted caveat (for example antiretroviral treatment) is shown without breaking the rule that no restricted fact is evidence on a standard diagnosis.
findings.done: EC-1 now specifies the HbA1c validity behaviour and the restricted-reason display. Certification of the method is a qualifier Phase 0 must map.

findings.where: clerking-v2/09-diagnosis.amendment.json, profiles dx.gestational_diabetes and dx.diabetes_in_pregnancy; rules DDX-RESULT-GLUCOSE-FASTING, DDX-RESULT-GLUCOSE-IFG; clerking-v2/10-plan-care.v1.json CARE-DKD-RASI, CARE-DM-STATIN, CARE-GDM-POSTPARTUM; clerking-v2/00-engine-changes.json
findings.finding: There is no pregnancy atom. The two pregnancy profiles say 'offered only in a pregnant patient' but nothing gates them and no differential rule suggests them. Their result atoms have no maximum age, so a value from before the pregnancy or from an earlier pregnancy counts. A pregnant woman with a fasting value of 5.1 to 6.0 gets no suggestion; at 6.1 to 6.9 she is offered 'intermediate hyperglycaemia'; at 7.0 or more she is offered dx.dm_type_unknown rather than the must-not-miss dx.diabetes_in_pregnancy. dx.diabetes_in_pregnancy lacks past diabetes and the symptomatic random value as evidence. The care items that prompt an ACE inhibitor, ARB or statin review cannot exclude pregnancy. The gap is noted only as '_reconcile: how pregnancy gates a profile' and is not in the engine-change list.
findings.why: Applying non-pregnant thresholds and labels to a pregnant woman is a clinical error in both directions. The record already holds pregnancy facts (pregnancy_episodes), so the engine can know.
findings.reviewerFix: Add EC-5: a 'pregnancy {state}' atom reading the current pregnancy episode, unknown when no episode is recorded. Gate both pregnancy profiles and a new DDX rule on it; bound the result atoms to the current episode; make the non-pregnant DDX result rules and dx.intermediate_hyperglycaemia require 'not pregnant' recorded, or show a 'pregnancy not recorded' caveat for women of reproductive age. Add 'not in pregnancy' to the CARE-DKD-RASI and CARE-DM-STATIN labels. Until EC-5 exists withhold both pregnancy profiles.
findings.done: Engine change EC-5 (pregnancy atom) is specified. Both pregnancy profiles and a new differential rule are gated on it and withheld until it exists; the statin, ACE inhibitor and ladder items exclude pregnancy.

findings.where: clerking-v2/09-diagnosis.amendment.json, every profile with _op 'amend' (dx.dm_type_unknown, dx.dm_type2, dx.dm_type1, dx.dka, dx.hhs, dx.hypoglycaemia_dm, dx.ckd) and ddx_rules.amend
findings.finding: 'amend' is not defined as replace or merge. Six profiles are written as complete objects; dx.ckd is written as a complete object holding only two evidence atoms, one ask, one test and one related diagnosis, with a note saying 'existing content is unchanged'. If the loader replaces, the signed dx.ckd profile loses all its present content; if it merges, the six diabetes profiles keep whatever atoms they hold today, which the author could not see (the briefing shows only dx.hypertension verbatim). The dx.ckd note adds 'a second named scale' but severity holds one scale id, and kdigo_albuminuria is attached to no profile. dx.dm_type1 is changed to must_not_miss true without being listed as a decision, and the new rules that suggest it (DDX-KETONES, DDX-RESULT-HBA1C, DDX-RESULT-GLUCOSE-FASTING) do not list it in must_not_miss_first.
findings.why: The live profiles are CSO-signed and every one of their 1,910 atoms is tested. An amendment that silently drops or keeps atoms cannot be reviewed for clinical sense, and a must-not-miss change alters the signing block for every note that carries the diagnosis.
findings.reviewerFix: Regenerate this file against the live catalogue JSON as an explicit diff per profile: atoms added, atoms removed with the reason, fields changed from and to. Express dx.ckd as 'suggest_for.add' and 'tests_to_decide.add' in the same style as ddx_rules.amend. List the must-not-miss change to dx.dm_type1 and the new must-not-miss dx.diabetes_in_pregnancy as numbered CSO decisions, and update must_not_miss_first in every rule that suggests them. Either propose the schema change for two named scales or drop the sentence.
findings.done: EC-8 defines amend as merge-only. The per-profile diff against the live catalogue is Phase 0 work; the change to must-not-miss on type 1 is D-DM-35.

findings.where: clerking-v2/10-plan-care.v1.json CARE-DM-CONFIRM; clerking-v2/09-diagnosis.amendment.json profile dx.dm_type2 and dx.dm_type1 notes
findings.finding: The 'repeat on another day' item is attached only to dx.dm_type_unknown and dx.hyperglycaemia_unconfirmed. A clinician who picks 'Type 2 diabetes' directly on one raised value in a person without symptoms gets no confirm item, and the dx.dm_type2 note does not carry the confirmation rule. The item opens test.glucose_fasting whatever the first test was, although its label says 'same test preferred', and it shows on dx.dm_type_unknown even when the diagnosis is already secure (symptoms with a value of 11.1 or more, or long-known diabetes).
findings.why: Pack rule 5: a single abnormal value must not diagnose a person without symptoms. The safeguard depends on which of three labels the clinician happens to choose.
findings.reviewerFix: Attach the item to all three diabetes problems with a 'when' that hides it once past diabetes is recorded yes; state the confirmation rule in the type 2 and type 1 notes; let the item open the same test as the first abnormal result.
findings.done: The confirm item attaches to all three diabetes problems and is a later-day task.

findings.where: clerking-v2/07-exam.amendment.json, classifiers.add.ketone_band (result dka_range) and flag FLAG-EX-KETONES-DKA; rule DDX-KETONES in 09-diagnosis.amendment.json
findings.finding: A urine ketone strip of 2+ or 3+ alone puts anyone in the band named 'dka_range' and raises an urgent flag: 'Ketones in the ketoacidosis range: check a venous gas or bicarbonate and get senior review now'. There is no glucose or diabetes condition. The pack's own acute rule acu_ketones (catalog/60-acute-route.json) requires glucose of 11.1 or more, or known diabetes, alongside the ketones. The urine branches name no reference entry, so the 2+ threshold cannot be withheld and is not signed (REF-DM-ACU-DKA-UKET exists in the dossier but has no REF-EX mirror). The exam composer prints classifier bands beside vitals (the briefing's example is 'BMI 21.1 (normal weight)'), so a fasting or vomiting non-diabetic could have a 'ketoacidosis range' band written into the note.
findings.why: Starvation, vomiting, hyperemesis, fasting and gastroenteritis commonly give 2+ urine ketones with a normal glucose. Urgent (red) is reserved for findings worth interrupting a clinician; this one would fire on many non-diabetic patients and teach staff to ignore it. A band name that is a diagnosis breaks 'findings, not interpretations'.
findings.reviewerFix: Rename the bands to findings (for example 'high', 'moderately raised', 'raised'). Keep urgent only for: blood ketones at or above REF-EX-KETONE-DKA, or urine 2+ or more, together with any of glucose at or above REF-EX-GLU-HIGH, past diabetes yes, medicine_group glucose_lowering, or Kussmaul breathing; otherwise caution with the text 'raised ketones: check glucose; consider starvation, vomiting, pregnancy and alcohol'. Add REF-EX-KETONE-URINE-DKA for the strip grade. At sites without a gas or bicarbonate the reason should end 'or refer', not assume a venous gas.
findings.done: Ketone bands are named as findings. Urgent only with diabetes, a raised glucose, a glucose-lowering medicine or Kussmaul breathing; caution otherwise.

findings.finding: Urgent flag 'Insulin stopped: risk of ketoacidosis. Check glucose and ketones now' on any medicine entry for insulin with adherence 'stopped'. It has no condition on type, on who stopped it, on when, on symptoms or on glucose. It relies on a 'medicine + adherence_any' atom the shared evaluator is not shown to have (acknowledged in its note, not in the engine-change list). It names only REF-DM ids, and it duplicates the history rule FLAG-MED-ADHERENCE in a second engine.
findings.why: A person with type 2 diabetes whose insulin was stopped by a doctor after a step-down, or a woman whose insulin stopped after delivery, would carry a red badge at every visit. The flag matters for type 1 or insulin from diagnosis, or with a raised glucose, vomiting or ketones.
findings.reviewerFix: Make it urgent only when insulin is 'stopped' AND any of: past_detail type = type_1, insulin_from_start = yes, glucose at or above REF-EX-GLU-HIGH, sym.vomiting yes, or ketone band raised; otherwise leave the existing caution from FLAG-MED-ADHERENCE. Add the atom to 00-engine-changes.json. Give the badge the same text as FLAG-MED-ADHERENCE so the two merge.
findings.done: Urgent only with type 1, insulin from diagnosis, a raised glucose, vomiting or ketones. The medicine-adherence atom is declared in EC-7.

findings.where: clerking-v2/07-exam.amendment.json, suggestion SUG-PMH-DIABETES, note ('Remove that branch [of SUG-POLYURIA] when this lands')
findings.finding: The note asks for the past-diabetes branch of the signed rule SUG-POLYURIA to be removed. SUG-POLYURIA offers hydration, breathing pattern and odour; SUG-PMH-DIABETES does not. After the change a known diabetic who is unwell without polyuria (vomiting, abdominal pain, drowsy) gets no chip for hydration, Kussmaul breathing or ketotic breath unless the glucose is 18 or more (SUG-GLU-KETONES).
findings.why: Those three examinations are how ketoacidosis is recognised at the bedside, and ketoacidosis occurs below 18 mmol/L. The change is also an edit to a signed rule hidden in a note rather than listed as an amendment. The 'why' text says 'eyes at every review', which contradicts the 24-month interval in REF-EX-DR-RECALL and CARE-DM-EYE.
findings.reviewerFix: Keep the SUG-POLYURIA branch, or add a rule: past diabetes yes AND any of sym.vomiting, sym.abdominal_pain, sym.confusion, sym.breathlessness yes, or glucose at or above REF-EX-GLU-HIGH, offering vs.ketones, ex.general.hydration, ex.respiratory.breathing_pattern and ex.general.odour. List any change to SUG-POLYURIA under an explicit 'suggestion_rules.amend'. Change the 'why' to 'eyes when due'.
findings.done: SUG-POLYURIA's branch is kept. A new suggestion covers 'diabetes and unwell'.

findings.where: clerking-v2/07-exam.amendment.json, medicine_groups.add (sglt2_inhibitor, insulin, sulfonylurea, systemic_steroid) and flags FLAG-EX-SGLT2-UNWELL, DDX-SGLT2-UNWELL, DDX-STEROID-GLUCOSE; clerking-v2/04-history.amendment.json symptoms.also_ask.add (sglt2_tablet)
findings.finding: The groups match generic name stems only. A medicine typed by brand, or a patient who knows only 'a tablet that makes sugar pass in the urine', is not in the group, so the urgent SGLT2 flag, its suggestion and its differential rule stay silent. The new also-ask item 'sglt2_tablet' on sym.polyuria is read by no rule. 'systemic_steroid' matches hydrocortisone cream, dexamethasone or prednisolone eye drops by stem, so the steroid rules fire on topical treatment. The flag covers only vomiting and abdominal pain, where the pack's acute rule acu_edka also lists deep rapid breathing and acute illness. The record already has drug class tags (sglt2_inhibitor, sulfonylurea, insulin, systemic_glucocorticoid) with different ids.
findings.why: Euglycaemic ketoacidosis has a normal glucose, so the medicine is the only cue. A safety flag that depends on spelling is silent when it matters, and a steroid rule that cannot tell route cries wolf.
findings.reviewerFix: Drive the groups from the medication statement's class tags where a drug code exists and fall back to stems only for free text; add the common brand stems as a signed list; let 'medicine_group' also be satisfied by the also-ask answer (or move that question into the medicines step as 'takes an SGLT2 inhibitor: yes, no, not sure'). Restrict 'systemic_steroid' to oral or injected routes. Add breathlessness, drowsiness and reduced eating or drinking to FLAG-EX-SGLT2-UNWELL so it matches acu_edka.
findings.done: Rules added: class tags first, route for steroids. The unused also-ask is removed. The SGLT2 flag reads breathing pattern. Signed brand stems are Phase 0.

findings.where: clerking-v2/07-exam.amendment.json REF-EX-GLU-KETONE-TEST, FLAG-EX-GLU-KETONE-TEST, SUG-GLU-KETONES; clerking-v2/09-diagnosis.amendment.json DDX-GLUCOSE-VERY-HIGH (REF-DX-GLU-HHS), dx.hhs suggest_for
findings.finding: All of these compare a numeric vs.glucose with 18 or 33.3 mmol/L. A bedside meter does not give a number at the top of its range; it shows 'HI'. vs.glucose is a number field (plausible 0.5 to 50) with no way to record 'meter reads HI', and the amendment proposes none.
findings.why: The hyperosmolar threshold sits at or above the ceiling of most meters, and district sites have only a meter. The sickest patients are the ones for whom every one of these rules has nothing to read, unless the clinician invents a number.
findings.reviewerFix: Add a 'reads HI' (and 'reads LO') qualifier to vs.glucose that stores no invented number and that the vital atom treats as at or above every upper threshold (and LO as below every lower one). Add it to the engine-change list and to the tests.
findings.done: Specified as engine change EC-6; the catalog side (HI and LO as recordable values) is done.

findings.where: clerking-v2/00-engine-changes.json (EC-1 to EC-4) against all amendment files
findings.finding: The amendments use engine features that the briefing does not show and that the engine-change list does not declare. History: applies_to 'past_history'; 'shown_when' on a history property; 'includes_any' in the history language; a per-condition 'composer' template.
