Exam: a new vitals panel vs.ketones with a coded urine field (saved by vitals.ts saveLines); panel atoms with 'field'; 'panel ... recorded' (noted in the rule only); 'medicine' with 'adherence_any' (noted in the rule only); two new classifiers, although the briefing says all classifiers live in lib/clerking/exam/classifiers.ts; 'option_sets' and 'options_ref' in the exam catalogue; token-map entries with 'value_from_option'; a composer rule for 'no retinopathy seen (undilated)'; 'why' and 'refs_dm' keys on suggestion rules; 'system', 'concept' and 'source' keys on items. Diagnosis: 'setting' with a list; 'ask' kinds 'panel' and 'past_detail'; 'panel field lt_ref'; a second named scale on one profile; amend operations. Plan: 'patient {age_gte_ref}' (the evaluator has patient.age_gte and the history language has age_gte_ref, not this); 'opens.disposition' and 'opens.followUp' with free-text values and no rule on overwriting what the clinician already set; keys 'refs_dm', 'ncd_step' and 'where_unavailable' that EC-4's own item shape does not list (it lists 'refs'). Formulary: a 'ketone row' on the glucose chart. EC-1 says it reads 'the latest fact for the concept' and then applies 'context', which would let a later random glucose hide an earlier fasting one; and its 'context' values do not exist in the fact model, which uses fastingState, challenge {ogtt_75g | meal, minutes} and specimen.
findings.why: Briefing Part 2 section 0: content needs no code change only if it uses existing response types and rule atoms; Part 4.2: if the grammar cannot express something, say so and propose the change. Undeclared atoms either fail the catalogue schema or evaluate as never true, so the rule is silently dead; unknown keys may simply be stripped (the briefing notes this for the note schema).
findings.reviewerFix: Extend 00-engine-changes.json with one entry per item above (or remove the use), each with its evaluator, schema and test. In EC-1 define the atom over the real context keys: fasting = fastingState fasting; ogtt_2h = challenge ogtt_75g at 120 minutes; add 'specimen'; read the latest fact that MATCHES the qualifiers; say what a comparator value ('<', '>') does. Mark every rule and profile atom that depends on an engine change with 'needs', as the DDX result rules already do (the profile atoms and the plan items do not).
findings.done: EC-5 to EC-8 declare every evaluator and catalogue feature the wiring uses. EC-1 reads the latest fact that matches the qualifiers.

findings.where: clerking-v2/09-diagnosis.amendment.json result and vital atoms with 'context'; wiring/test-menu.additions.json test.glucose_capillary and test.ogtt_75g; wiring/cfc-addendum.proposal.json qualifiersNeeded
findings.finding: Three vocabularies name the 2-hour post-load glucose: 'two_hours_after_food' (vs.glucose), 'two_hours_after_glucose' (test.glucose_capillary) and 'ogtt_2h' (test.ogtt_75g and every result atom). A capillary 2-hour value entered through the meter test never matches the 'ogtt_2h' atoms. No atom carries the specimen, so the venous threshold REF-DX-GLU-2H-DM (11.1) is applied to any obs.glucose at 2 hours, while the pack's confirm lane uses 12.2 mmol/L for capillary samples (catalog/20-confirm.json) and the addendum itself records 'the 2-hour capillary threshold differs (12.2 against 11.1)'. No context-qualified atom reads 'two_hours_after_food', so a capillary value of 15 two hours after a meal is not evidence on any diabetes profile.
findings.why: The clerking desk and the NCD engine would give different answers for the same capillary result between 11.1 and 12.1, and a meter-only district site cannot produce OGTT evidence at all.
findings.reviewerFix: Use one context vocabulary taken from the fact model. Add 'specimen' to the result atom and a REF-DX-GLU-2H-DM-CAPILLARY entry mirroring the confirm lane. Decide and state whether a 2-hour post-meal capillary value counts as a random value for the symptomatic rule, and add that atom.
findings.done: Result atoms carry 'qualifiers' named after the fact model; the capillary 2-hour threshold has its own reference and atom. Exact values are mapped in Phase 0.

findings.finding: Thirty-two REF-EX and REF-DX entries are copies of REF-DM dossier entries, linked only by a 'mirrors' key, so each number would be signed twice in two catalogues and can drift. Rules also carry 'refs_dm' naming REF-DM ids that no clerking sign-off file knows: the briefing says engines find references by pattern over the rule JSON and a rule fires only when every reference it names is signed. Depending on the pattern, those rules are either never live or not gated at all. Several flags name only REF-DM ids (FLAG-EX-INSULIN-STOPPED, FLAG-EX-SGLT2-UNWELL, both history flags). The Plan care list has no reference entries at all: about a dozen thresholds live in label text ('below 130/80', '18', 'at 40 or over', 'every 2 years', 'within 1 month ... 3 months ... 6 to 12 months', '2 of 3 within 3 to 6 months', '2 to 4 weeks', '6 to 12 weeks', '3 months (6 months ...; 1 month ...)', '12 months'). Rule 'why' and flag 'reason' strings repeat thresholds as text ('HbA1c 6.5% or more', 'Glucose 18 mmol/L or more'). Two mirrors cite a different source from the dossier entry they copy (REF-DX-KETONE-NORMAL: ADA-EASD-CRISES-2024 against TREND-UK; REF-DX-CPEP-HIGH: ADA-EASD-T1-2021 against ADA 2026). Six entries are defined and used by no rule: REF-DX-EGFR-REFER, REF-DX-K-SEVERE, REF-DX-KETONE-DKA, REF-DX-RESULT-AGE-HBA1C, REF-DX-UACR-A3, REF-EX-IPSWICH. REF-DX-RESULT-AGE-GLUCOSE has no value, so every rule and atom that names it (the laboratory fasting and OGTT evidence) is dead until the CSO supplies one; meanwhile the same glucose result is evidence at any age on the profiles that omit max_age_ref (dx.intermediate_hyperglycaemia, both pregnancy profiles) and every HbA1c atom has no age limit.
findings.why: Ground rule: every threshold is a reference entry, and the withheld list is the kill switch. A number in a label cannot be withheld and does not change when the CSO changes the reference. Briefing 3.6: attribution errors are the real risk.
findings.reviewerFix: Choose one home for each number. Either the clerking catalogues hold REF-EX/REF-DX entries generated from the dossier by a build step that fails on drift (source and value copied, never retyped), or the clerking engines learn to resolve REF-DM ids against the signed dossier. Give the Plan care list 'refs' to signed entries and build label numbers from them with placeholders, as badges already do. Remove or use the six orphan entries. List the rules that are dead until REF-DX-RESULT-AGE-GLUCOSE is set.
findings.done: Clerking references are generated from the dossier at build time, never typed. Six unused entries removed; the build now fails on an unused or undefined one. The glucose result age has no value on purpose (D-DM-08). Plan labels still carry numbers as text.

findings.where: Ids across clerking-v2/*.json and wiring/*.json that the briefing does not show and that are not marked for reconciliation
findings.finding: Not shown to exist and not marked: sym.vomiting and sym.abdominal_pain (used by an urgent flag, a suggestion, a differential rule and dx.dka; the briefing shows them only as red-flag ids on sym.polyuria); dx.sepsis, dx.malaria_severe, dx.cataract (in 'related'); the setting values 'emergency' and 'inpatient'; finding 'ex.general.hydration is positive' (the item's response type is not shown; a classifier dehydration_gtfcc exists); REF-EX-HYPO-L1 used inside the diagnosis catalogue (cross-catalogue reference and sign-off); formulary classes gabapentinoid, snri, tricyclic_antidepressant (the link says only 'add the classes if absent'). The two symptom ids very probably exist, but an urgent rule should not rest on a guess. The eight new diagnoses (dx.intermediate_hyperglycaemia, dx.hyperglycaemia_unconfirmed, dx.steroid_induced_hyperglycaemia, dx.gestational_diabetes, dx.diabetes_in_pregnancy, dx.diabetic_retinopathy, dx.diabetic_kidney_disease, dx.diabetic_neuropathy) point at REF-DX-TERMS but the pack contains no term entries for them: no display label, synonyms or code, and no term addendum or migration. Marked for reconciliation and still open: sym.dizziness, sym.numbness, ex.nervous.reflexes, breathing_pattern attribute and option ids, waist_risk and bmi_who band ids, categories obstetric, eye and neurological.
findings.why: The catalogue check resolves every sym, ex, classifier, dx and test id across catalogues and fails CI on the first miss. A profile with no term has no name to render.
findings.reviewerFix: Run the amendment against the live catalogues and replace every guessed id. Add a REF-DX-TERMS addendum with the eight terms and their seed migration to the pack. Where the symptom is only a red flag today, either add the symptom or write the atom as the red-flag form ('symptom ... red_flag').
findings.done: Labels added for the eight new diagnoses. A generated file, wiring/reconcile-ids.json, lists every catalogue id the pack uses for Phase 0 to resolve.

findings.where: wiring/cfc-addendum.proposal.json conceptsToPropose and qualifiersNeeded; clerking-v2/07-exam.amendment.json vs.ketones urine options, fundoscopy macula options, token_map.add
findings.finding: The addendum proposes as new five concepts the briefing's concept list (Part 1, section 2.5) shows as already present (obs.c_peptide, obs.islet_autoantibody, obs.chol_total, exam.ankle_reflex, soc.physical_activity) and says of total cholesterol that it 'does not' exist. It proposes exam.macular_oedema beside the existing exam.maculopathy. It asks for 'specimen' and a new 'context' qualifier on obs.glucose although specimen, fastingState and challenge already exist. Option ids do not line up: urine ketones are 'negative, trace, 1+, 2+, 3+' as bare strings on the panel, 'neg, trace, 1plus, 2plus, 3plus' in catalog/01-features.json and '2plus' in the dossier; macula is 'no_oedema, non_centre, centre_involving, cannot_assess' on the exam item and 'none, non_centre, centre_involving' on the concept; view is 'adequate, inadequate' on the item and adds 'not_attempted' on the concept. The token map gives exam.retinal_view in the item's 'commit' block but not in token_map.add. EC-2 says nothing from per-condition detail is charted, while the addendum proposes hx.dm_type_reported, hx.dm_year_diagnosed and event.hypoglycaemia for exactly those answers.
findings.why: Briefing Part 4.2: reuse existing concepts. The seed is insert-or-ignore, so a re-proposed concept with a different value type or unit is silently dropped. With 'value_from_option' a mismatched option id writes a code the concept does not accept, and signing counts it as 'unmapped: kept in the note, not charted'.
findings.reviewerFix: Diff the addendum against lib/facts/catalogue.generated.ts and keep only concepts that are new. Reuse exam.maculopathy or justify the second concept. Use one id set for each option list across the exam item, the NCD feature and the concept. Give panel options the {id, label} shape. Resolve the EC-2 and addendum contradiction.
findings.done: Five concepts marked 'verify: probably exists'; one option-id set; the EC-2 contradiction stated. The diff against the generated catalogue is Phase 0.

findings.finding: Entries use a single 'result_concept' where the test catalogue has components[] (concept ids), fasting_required and capability_id; none of those is given. test.venous_gas returns only obs.ph_venous, so the bicarbonate that dx.dka reads has no ordered source; test.ogtt_75g has no fasting flag and one concept for three time points; test.xray_abdomen has no result concept (null); test.retinal_photograph returns only a grade, with no eye, macula, acuity or gradability, and combines a photograph with a dilated examination in one test; test.urine_pcr and test.abi are added but no profile, rule or care item uses them (CARE-DM-KIDNEY's fallback is the reagent strip, not the protein ratio). CARE-DM-KETONES and the kidney fallback depend on test.urinalysis_dipstick returning urine ketones and protein as components; the pack does not confirm that it does.
findings.why: A test whose result concept is missing or partial produces results that no atom can read, so the differential and evidence stay empty after the result returns. Capability ids are what make a site-unavailable test show as unavailable rather than as a gap.
findings.reviewerFix: Rewrite each entry in the test catalogue shape with components[], fasting_required and capability_id (cap.ogtt, a ketone meter, blood gas, retinal camera). Give test.venous_gas both obs.ph_venous and obs.bicarbonate. Confirm test.urinalysis_dipstick lists obs.ketones_urine, obs.glucose_urine and obs.urine_protein_dipstick. Either use test.urine_pcr in the kidney fallback or drop it. Give the abdominal X-ray a report concept or mark it as report-only.
findings.done: Components listed (bicarbonate on the gas, three samples on the OGTT, three results on the retinal examination); two unused tests held. The live shape is Phase 0.

findings.finding: No dose, strength or brand appears, which is right. But the 13 drug entries carry only id, generic, class and source: none has routes, methods, presentationsDraft, allergyGroups, the flags object, charts or the 'to-verify' dose skeleton that the live entry shape requires, and they use 'emhslu2023' text where the catalogue has the boolean onEmhsluDraft. Without flags, the kidney check (which runs only on drugs flagged renal) will not run for dapagliflozin, empagliflozin, sitagliptin, vildagliptin or glimepiride, and insulin aspart is not marked highAlert. The briefing describes the glucose chart rule as 'a sulfonylurea (glibenclamide, gliclazide)'; if that rule lists drugs, glimepiride would not open the chart. The fate of class oral_glucose_lowering after the split is not stated (dx.dm_type2 'keep' omits it and nothing removes it). Bendroflumethiazide has no source.
findings.why: The generator test fails on drift and the Python validator on shape. A new sulfonylurea with no chart rule and no renal flag is a hypoglycaemia risk the system was built to catch.
findings.reviewerFix: Supply complete entries in the live shape with every dose 'to-verify'. Set renal true for the gliflozins, gliptins, metformin and sulfonylureas, highAlert for every insulin, and charts ['mar','glucose'] for insulins and sulfonylureas. Change the glucose chart rule to class = sulfonylurea. State that oral_glucose_lowering is retired and migrate every reference to it.
findings.done: The entries name drug and class only. The file now says what does not work until Phase 0 completes them.

findings.where: wiring/formulary.additions.json, diagnosisLinks dx.dm_type2 (add: antiplatelet) and dx.diabetic_neuropathy
findings.finding: 'antiplatelet' is linked to type 2 diabetes with no condition. The Plan shows linked classes on the problem card as treatment classes for that diagnosis. The neuropathy link names three classes that may not exist and adds no drugs for them.
findings.why: An antiplatelet is for established cardiovascular disease, not for diabetes as such; showing it on every type 2 card invites primary-prevention aspirin and its bleeding risk. The pack's rule is drug names and classes only where the source names them for that indication.
findings.reviewerFix: Remove antiplatelet from dx.dm_type2 and leave it on the cardiovascular diagnoses that already carry it. For neuropathy, add the classes and at least the EMHSLU-listed generic for each, or leave the link out until they exist.
findings.done: Antiplatelet link removed; neuropathy link held.

findings.where: clerking-v2/10-plan-care.v1.json CARE-DM-KETONES (when: vs.glucose >= REF-EX-GLU-KETONE-TEST; problems include dx.dka)
findings.finding: The only ketone item is hidden unless the capillary glucose is 18 mmol/L or more, including on the dx.dka problem card. It opens only the urine strip although test.ketones_blood is added to the menu, and it stays after a ketone result is recorded.
findings.why: Ketoacidosis with a glucose below 18 (and below 11.1 on an SGLT2 inhibitor, in pregnancy or starvation) is the case the dx.dka note warns about: 'a normal or near-normal glucose does NOT argue against ketoacidosis'. On the ketoacidosis card the test that makes the diagnosis must always be offered.
findings.reviewerFix: Split it: on dx.dka and dx.dm_type1 show 'Ketones now (blood where available, urine strip otherwise)' with no glucose condition, hidden once vs.ketones is recorded; on the other diabetes problems keep the 18 mmol/L condition and add 'or on an SGLT2 inhibitor and unwell'. Open test.ketones_blood with the strip as the stated fallback.
findings.done: Two ketone items: always on ketoacidosis and type 1; conditional elsewhere, including on an SGLT2 inhibitor. Blood ketones first.

findings.finding: For dx.dka and dx.hhs the only care item is 'hospital now' and ticking it sets the disposition to 'refer'. MedSync is a hospital system and the differential rules run in the emergency and inpatient settings. In a hospital that treats these emergencies the item points the patient away, and EC-4 does not say whether ticking overwrites a disposition of 'admit' already chosen. Nothing sets senior review to 'now'.
findings.why: The WHO HEARTS-D instruction is written for primary care. For a time-critical diagnosis the default action must be right for the site: escalate and admit here, or transfer if this site cannot manage it.
findings.reviewerFix: Make the item site-aware through a capability condition: where the site can manage it, 'Senior review now; admit to a monitored bed' opening seniorReview 'now' and disposition 'admit'; otherwise 'Refer to hospital now' opening disposition 'refer'. Specify in EC-4 that 'opens' proposes a value and never overwrites one the clinician set.
findings.done: Label and rule changed (senior review; admit or refer; never overwrite). Capability-aware disposition is an engine item.

findings.where: clerking-v2/10-plan-care.v1.json CARE-DM-CONFIRM, CARE-HYPERGLYCAEMIA-FOLLOW-UP, CARE-GDM-POSTPARTUM, CARE-DKD-CONFIRM (opens.tests); profile dx.steroid_induced_hyperglycaemia
findings.finding: These items are for a test on a later day ('on another day', 'after recovery', 'after the birth at 6 to 12 weeks', 'at 3 months') but 'opens.tests' puts the order in today's basket, and the note cannot be signed until the basket is placed or emptied. For steroid-induced hyperglycaemia the item says 'fasting glucose after recovery' while the profile note says 'a fasting value can be normal: test after lunch or before the evening meal' and the dossier (REF-DM-SUS-STEROID) says postprandial or random, not fasting. For dx.ckd and dx.diabetic_kidney_disease the only repeat offered is creatinine at 3 months.
findings.why: A fasting glucose drawn today in an acutely ill or pregnant patient gives the stress or pregnancy value the item was meant to avoid. A fasting test on steroids can falsely reassure. A first-ever low eGFR with no earlier value may be acute kidney injury; the sources to check are NICE NG203 (early repeat of a first low eGFR) and KDIGO 2024 (do not assume chronicity from one value).
findings.reviewerFix: Give the item shape a 'due' field so a deferred test is written as follow-up or a dated future order, not today's order. For steroid-induced hyperglycaemia change the test to an afternoon or post-meal glucose. Add to the kidney problems 'First low eGFR with no earlier result: repeat soon to exclude acute kidney injury' with the interval taken from a signed reference the CSO chooses.
findings.done: A 'due' field separates later-day tasks from today's basket. The steroid item uses a post-meal test. The early creatinine repeat exists but is 'needs-cso': its interval has no source in this pack.

findings.where: clerking-v2/10-plan-care.v1.json CARE-DM-EDU-HYPO, CARE-DM-EDU-SICK-DAY, CARE-DM-EDU-INSULIN (when: medicine_group insulin or sulfonylurea); problem dx.hypoglycaemia_dm
findings.finding: The three teaching items appear only when insulin or a sulfonylurea is already in the medicines history. They do not appear at the visit where insulin or a sulfonylurea is first prescribed (the 'when' reads the history, not the Plan basket), and not for dx.dm_type1 when no medicine has been recorded yet. Sick-day teaching is limited to insulin although the pack's own reference REF-DM-RX-SGLT2-HOLD stops SGLT2 inhibitors during critical illness and prolonged fasting. The dx.hypoglycaemia_dm card carries only the chronic item 'Lows: ask at every visit ...' and nothing about recurrence after a low on a sulfonylurea or long-acting insulin, or about not sending the patient home after the first recovery.
findings.why: The visit at which a hypoglycaemia-causing medicine starts is when the teaching matters most. Sulfonylurea hypoglycaemia recurs; UCG 2023 and the JBDS hypoglycaemia guideline are the sources to check for the observation step.
findings.reviewerFix: Let these 'when' conditions also read prescriptions in the Plan basket; show the hypoglycaemia and sick-day items on dx.dm_type1 without a medicine condition; add an SGLT2 inhibitor sick-day item; add an acute item on dx.hypoglycaemia_dm for the cause, the medicine responsible and observation before discharge, routed and worded from the source, with no treatment instruction.
findings.done: Teaching items read the Plan basket (declared in EC-7) and show unconditionally on type 1. An SGLT2 item is added. The after-a-low item is 'needs-cso' until UCG 2023 section 1.1.6 is read.

findings.where: clerking-v2/10-plan-care.v1.json, the list as a whole (18 items on a dx.dm_type2 card); CARE-DM-BP, CARE-DM-HYPO-REVIEW, CARE-DM-TARGET, CARE-DM-FOOT, CARE-DM-EYE, CARE-DM-TYPE1-REFER, CARE-DKD-RASI
findings.finding: No item knows whether its check is due. Yearly and two-yearly checks (kidney, lipids, eye, foot risk) and HbA1c show at every visit whatever was done last month, because the list uses no result-age condition and EC-1 makes an out-of-window result 'unknown', so 'not done within the interval' cannot be written. Several items are two actions under one tick, one of them a prescribing decision: CARE-DM-BP 'Blood pressure today; treat towards below 130/80' and CARE-DM-HYPO-REVIEW 'ask at every visit; ... relax the target for now'. CARE-DM-TARGET says 'record it' but there is nowhere to record a target. Labels claim conditions that no predicate tests: CARE-DM-TYPE1-REFER 'in a new diagnosis' (shown for every type 1, including long-standing), CARE-DKD-RASI 'albuminuria with raised blood pressure'. CARE-DM-FOOT says 'full risk assessment every year' although the existing iwgdf_risk classifier gives 1 to 3 months for the highest category. CARE-DM-EYE gives the type 2 schedule to type 1 as well.
findings.why: Pack rules 9 and 10: do not cry wolf; a label says exactly what its predicates test. Eighteen boxes that never change teach clinicians to tick all or none, and a tick on a compound item records nothing definite. A blood-pressure target inside a tick-box is a treatment decision presented as a task.
findings.reviewerFix: Add a 'recorded_within {concept or item, ref}' atom so screening items show only when due or never recorded, and show the date of the last one. Split compound items: 'Blood pressure measured today' (tick) and a separate review item with requiresPrescribing true whose target comes from a signed reference. Add 'when' conditions that match each label, or shorten the label. Take the foot interval from iwgdf_risk. Give CARE-DM-TARGET a field to write to or drop 'record it'.
findings.done: Compound items split; labels match predicates; the foot interval follows the risk category; type 1 has its own eye item. 'Due' awareness (last date, recorded-within) is not built: the NCD engine owns it.

findings.where: clerking-v2/10-plan-care.v1.json 'where_unavailable' on CARE-DM-HBA1C, CARE-DM-KIDNEY, CARE-DM-EYE; profiles dx.diabetic_kidney_disease, dx.ckd, dx.intermediate_hyperglycaemia; wiring/formulary.additions.json check.metformin_no_egfr
findings.finding: The three district alternatives are sensible as far as they go, but: the kidney fallback ('Urine reagent strip; a positive is sent for a laboratory ratio') does not say that a negative strip does not exclude early kidney disease and gives no fallback for creatinine; CARE-DM-HBA1C's fallback prints a catalogue id in display text ('Order test.glucose_fasting ...'); CARE-DM-CVD-RISK names the laboratory chart with no fallback where cholesterol is unavailable; CARE-DM-KETONES, CARE-DPN-EXCLUDE and CARE-DKD-CONFIRM have none. The kidney profiles accept only UACR and eGFR as evidence, although obs.urine_protein_dipstick exists, so a district site can never show evidence for kidney disease. dx.intermediate_hyperglycaemia accepts only laboratory results, so a meter-only site cannot reach it. The proposed check 'metformin and no eGFR in the last 12 months' would fire on every metformin prescription for ever at a site with no creatinine.
findings.why: Pack rule 8 and briefing Part 4.1: every test-dependent step names its capability and gives a district pathway that reaches a safe answer; not assessed is not normal. A negative strip recorded as 'kidney check done' is a false negative for the range the screen exists to find.
findings.reviewerFix: Make 'where_unavailable' a structured field keyed by capability, shown only at sites without it. Word the kidney fallback 'Urine reagent strip now; a negative strip does not exclude early kidney disease; refer for a laboratory ratio and creatinine yearly'. Add a reagent-strip protein atom to both kidney profiles and a capillary fasting atom to dx.intermediate_hyperglycaemia. Give the cardiovascular risk item its non-laboratory fallback with the dossier's caveat. Make check.metformin_no_egfr capability-aware.
findings.done: where_unavailable is structured by capability. The kidney fallback says a negative strip excludes nothing. Strip and capillary evidence atoms on the kidney and intermediate profiles are Phase 0.

findings.where: clerking-v2/04-history.amendment.json past_history.condition_details.diabetes, property 'type' option 'pregnancy_only'; wiring/cfc-addendum.proposal.json hx.prior_gdm (restrictedClass sexual_reproductive_health) and hx.dm_type_reported
findings.finding: The pack's own addendum classes previous gestational diabetes as a restricted (sexual and reproductive health) fact, but the history amendment captures the same fact as an ordinary option under 'About the diabetes', composes it into the note sentence ('Diabetes (Only in pregnancy) ...') and carries it as a qualifier on the problem-list proposal; hx.dm_type_reported lists 'gestational' unrestricted. Separately, a woman whose only diabetes was in pregnancy has past condition diabetes = yes, so every rule that reads that answer treats her as a known diabetic: the urgent hypoglycaemia flag for level 1 values, SUG-PMH-DIABETES, 'pmh:diabetes' evidence on dx.dm_type2, dx.dka, dx.hhs and the complication profiles, and a problem-list proposal of diabetes.
findings.why: Pack rule 7: a restricted class must not leak into patient-facing text and must travel with any rule that reads it. If the classification in the addendum stands this is a breach; if it does not, the addendum is wrong. Either way the two files disagree. Previous gestational diabetes is a risk factor, not established diabetes.
findings.reviewerFix: Decide the classification once with the CSO. Move 'diabetes only in pregnancy' out of the diabetes detail block into its own past-history question (restricted if that is the decision, with the lock and clinical-only composition), and make it a risk-factor atom for the suspect rules rather than 'past_condition diabetes yes'.
findings.done: 'Only in pregnancy' removed from the type list; a separate past-history question is proposed. Its restricted class is D-DM-30.

findings.where: clerking-v2/07-exam.amendment.json items.amend ex.eyes_ent_neck.fundoscopy (attributes method, view, dr_grade, macula); named_scales.add.icdr_dr in 09-diagnosis.amendment.json
findings.finding: The new 'view' attribute duplicates the existing option seen = not_visualised, so the two can contradict each other. The rule text says 'a grade is offered only when the view is adequate', but shown_when tests only seen includes diabetic_retinopathy. There is no way to record 'no retinopathy' as a grade after an adequate dilated examination or photograph: dr_grade has no 'none' option, while the NCD feature retinopathy_stage and REF-EX-DR-RECALL both have one. The diagnosis scale icdr_dr offers 'no apparent retinopathy' as a severity of diabetic retinopathy. Numbers in the grade hint (20 haemorrhages, 4, 2 and 1 quadrants) are thresholds outside any reference entry, and the labels 'Severe (4-2-1)' and 'IRMA' are not plain wording.
findings.why: If a normal adequate screen cannot be recorded, exam.retinopathy_grade is never written as 'none', the eye screen can never be shown as done and normal, and the screening prompt never clears. A grade recorded on an inadequate view is false precision.
findings.reviewerFix: Fold 'view' and the existing not_visualised into one attribute. Show dr_grade when view = adequate AND method is dilated or photograph, with options none, mild, moderate, severe, proliferative; keep 'no retinopathy seen (undilated)' as a composed finding that writes no grade. Remove 'no apparent retinopathy' from the diagnosis severity scale. Move the grade definition to a signed reference shown as the hint and write the labels in full words.
findings.done: A 'none' grade exists and is offered only on an adequate dilated or photographic view. Grade definitions come from the signed reference, not a typed hint.

findings.where: clerking-v2/07-exam.amendment.json FLAG-EX-GLU-KETONE-TEST, FLAG-EX-DR-SIGHT, FLAG-EX-KETONES-RISK; clerking-v2/04-history.amendment.json FLAG-DM-ADMITTED-RECENT
findings.finding: FLAG-EX-GLU-KETONE-TEST uses the badge text 'Glucose {glucose}', the same as the existing glucose flags; same-text badges merge, so its reason ('test urine ketones now') may be lost under FLAG-EX-GLU-HIGH. It has no glucose context and no capability condition, so it stays up for ever at a site with no ketone strips. FLAG-EX-DR-SIGHT says 'within the ICO window', which is not plain wording and gives no interval. FLAG-DM-ADMITTED-RECENT says 'review sick-day rules and insulin supply' for an admission that may have been a hyperosmolar state in someone on tablets.
findings.why: A flag whose message is merged away or cannot be acted on is noise. Levels are otherwise reasonable: caution for the ketone prompt, the at-risk ketone band, retinopathy referral and both history flags is right.
findings.reviewerFix: Give the ketone prompt its own badge ('Glucose {glucose}: test ketones') and hide it where the site has no ketone test, showing 'refer' instead. Write the interval from the classifier result into the retinopathy reason. Reword the admission flag to 'review sick-day rules and the supply of medicines'.
findings.done: The ketone prompt has its own badge and says what to do without a strip; the retinopathy flag states the intervals; the admission flag no longer assumes insulin.

findings.where: clerking-v2/09-diagnosis.amendment.json rules DDX-RESULT-EGFR, DDX-RESULT-UACR, DDX-GLUCOSE-IN-HOSPITAL, DDX-RETINOPATHY, ddx_rules.amend DDX-GLUCOSE-HIGH; profile dx.hyperglycaemia_unconfirmed
findings.finding: DDX-RESULT-EGFR puts dx.aki first as must-not-miss on an eGFR up to 365 days old. DDX-RESULT-UACR and DDX-RESULT-EGFR suggest dx.diabetic_kidney_disease in people with no diabetes recorded. DDX-GLUCOSE-IN-HOSPITAL fires in known diabetics and suggests 'hyperglycaemia, unconfirmed' for them. dx.hyperglycaemia_unconfirmed uses the in-hospital threshold (7.8) with no setting condition, so an outpatient random value of 7.9 is suggested evidence. Adding two more chips to DDX-GLUCOSE-HIGH may push others past the eight shown.
findings.why: These are chips, not flags, so the cost is clutter and a label that says more than its predicate; but an old result should not raise an acute must-not-miss.
findings.reviewerFix: Give the acute kidney injury suggestion a short result age from a signed reference; add past diabetes yes or a diabetes diagnosis on the board to the diabetic kidney disease suggestion; add 'past diabetes not recorded yes' handling to the in-hospital rule; add the setting condition to the profile atom.
findings.done: Acute kidney injury is no longer put first on a result up to a year old. The other chip-noise items are Phase 0.

findings.where: clerking-v2/04-history.amendment.json condition_details.diabetes properties and composer; clerking-v2/07-exam.amendment.json items.add
findings.finding: treatment: 'diet_only' is exclusive, so 'diet only' and 'herbal or traditional' cannot both be recorded. lows_12_months options are in the first person ('Yes, treated it myself') in a form the clinician fills. There is no 'not sure' for lows or admissions. The composer template leaves empty brackets and stray punctuation when properties are unanswered. ex.skin.injection_sites composes 'lipohypertrophy at injection sites' for a finding labelled 'Lumps or thickening', an interpretation rather than the finding, and is not placed in a part of the skin system. ex.eyes_ent_neck.visual_acuity has ids containing '/', no phrase for one eye recorded, an unclear 'pinhole' flag, and no place for 'not tested: no chart'. The urine ketone options stop at 3+ where some strips read 4+.
findings.why: Ground rules: findings not interpretations; plain en-GB wording; an unanswered property is an absent key and must not leave marks in the note.
findings.reviewerFix: Make only 'none' exclusive; write options in the third person; build the sentence clause by clause as the property phrases already allow; compose 'lumps or thickening at injection sites'; record acuity per eye with 'unaided, with glasses, with pinhole' and safe ids.
findings.done: Options in the third person, 'not sure' added, only 'none' exclusive, composer rule stated, acuity ids without '/', finding wording on injection sites. A 4+ ketone option waits on the live strip list.

findings.where: clerking-v2/09-diagnosis.amendment.json profile notes (dx.dm_type2, dx.dm_type1, dx.diabetic_kidney_disease, dx.gestational_diabetes, dx.steroid_induced_hyperglycaemia)
findings.finding: Notes state local epidemiology and forward-looking claims with no source key in the profile's sources: 'a third of Ugandan adults with non-autoimmune diabetes are lean', 'most young Ugandans with clinical type 1 are antibody negative', 'creatinine-based eGFR overestimated kidney function in Ugandan adults', 'WHO is revising these criteria in late 2026'. dx.steroid_induced_hyperglycaemia lists test.hba1c to decide while its note says HbA1c waits 3 months after steroids stop. Notes carry many thresholds as prose (11.1, 6/12, 3 months, 2 of 3 samples, 6 to 12 weeks, eGFR below 30).
findings.why: Briefing Part 4.1: nothing clinical without a citation; no invented prevalence figures. The claims may well be right, but a CSO cannot sign what has no source.
findings.reviewerFix: Add the source key for each claim to the profile's sources and to sourcesToAdd, or remove the sentence. Remove test.hba1c from the steroid profile or mark it 'after 3 months'. Reference thresholds in notes by their entry.
findings.done: HbA1c removed from the steroid profile's deciding tests. Source keys for the local epidemiology sentences in profile notes are Phase 0.

findings.where: build/build.py run_vignette (management loop skips every step when the age band is not adult); build/k_review.py F04 block (x.ages = adult on every therapy flag); 50-act.json all steps of kind 'refer' and all therapyFlags
findings.finding: The F04 fix removed adult content from under-16s and took referral and the safety flags with it. Evaluator: 15-year-old (adolescent band) with type 1 on insulin, pregnant, on an ACE inhibitor, eGFR 20, sudden loss of vision, a foot ulcer with gangrene, HbA1c 12 -> NOTHING fires (three caveats only). 15-year-old with type 2 on metformin and glibenclamide, eGFR 20, a low needing help -> nothing fires. 15-year-old type 1 at a routine visit -> nothing fires. The identical record with the adult band fires five same-day items (SCREEN-PREG-01, REFER-VISION-01, REFER-EGFR-01, REFER-FOOT-01, REFER-FOOT-03) and the red ACE-inhibitor-in-pregnancy flag. Therapy flags had no age gate in 0.2.0 (R1 F04 says so), so the fix has removed the pregnancy and metformin flags from this girl.
findings.why: Rule 3 says under 16 gets recognition, classification support AND referral. Referral is the one output the pack owes a child and it is the output that is switched off. Teenage pregnancy with type 1 diabetes is not rare in Uganda, and an ACE inhibitor in pregnancy is a fetal-harm flag whatever the mother's age. Rule 8 as well: nothing reaches a safe next step.
findings.reviewerFix: Under 16 keep every step of kind 'refer' (or one consolidated 'refer today to a paediatric or higher-level service' rule carrying the same triggers), and SCREEN-PREG-01. Do not hide red therapy flags under 16: show them with the action replaced by 'refer today; do not change the medicine here'. Keep targets, control bands and the risk model withheld. Add a vignette: under 16, established diabetes, each same-day trigger; assert that a referral fires.
findings.done: Referral steps and red flags stay on under 16; a red flag's action becomes 'refer today; do not change the medicine here'. Targets, bands, the risk model and amber flags stay off. DMV-61.

findings.where: build/build.py annotate (management runWhen = 'established'); 50-act.json DM-ACT-REFER-FOOT-01/-02/-03, DM-ACT-REFER-LIMB-01, DM-ACT-REFER-VISION-01, DM-ACT-REFER-EGFR-01, DM-ACT-REFER-BP-01/-03
findings.finding: No referral step runs at the visit where diabetes is found. The F17 fix let the classify rules run 'established_or_met'; the referral steps were left on 'established'. The same record with established = true fires seven same-day referrals.
findings.why: In Uganda diabetes is very often first found BECAUSE of the foot, the eye or the kidney. R1's F08 ('a foot ulcer on its own triggers nothing') is still true for exactly that patient. WHO's same-day list (REF-DM-ACT-REFER-SAMEDAY) does not wait for the problem list to be updated.
findings.reviewerFix: Run every step of kind 'refer' as 'established_or_met' (the foot, limb, vision, eGFR/anuria and blood-pressure triggers could run 'always': none of them needs a diabetes label to be right). Add a vignette: new diagnosis today with gangrene; assert FOOT-03 fires.
findings.done: Referral steps run at the visit where the criteria are met; limb- and sight-threatening ones run always. DMV-62.

findings.where: 60-acute-route.json DM-ACU-ROUTE-01, -02, -06, -07, -08, -11, -14 (the GLU() helper in k_review.py reads capillary_glucose, random_pg, fasting_pg only); 01-features.json postprandial_pg, ogtt_1h_pg, ogtt_2h_pg; 20-confirm.json consensus_2021_remission notWhen
findings.finding: A glucose typed into the 'Glucose 2 hours after a meal' field (postprandial_pg, a meter field available at district sites) is read by no acute rule, although the labels say 'Any glucose'. Evaluator: 70-year-old on insulin, post-meal field 2.4 -> no ROUTE-06, no ROUTE-07; only a 'low' band. Known type 2, post-meal field 36 -> no ROUTE-01, no ROUTE-14; the only output is the band 'Above target' and two education steps. OGTT values are skipped the same way: a 2-hour value of 34 in a known diabetic, or of 2.5, fires nothing. The pack itself sends clinicians to this field (DM-STR-STEROID-01 'monitor after meals', ppg_control_who, tgt_ppg_surrogate).
findings.why: Rule 10 (the label says 'any glucose') and plain safety: level 2 hypoglycaemia and an HHS-range value pass silently because of which box they were typed in. findings.reviewerFix: Either remove postprandial_pg and map post-meal meter readings to capillary_glucose with its context, or add postprandial_pg, ogtt_1h_pg and ogtt_2h_pg to GLU() and to the remission notWhen. findings.done: Every acute rule reads all six fields a current glucose can be typed into; the build fails if the low-glucose or the very-high-glucose rule misses one. DMV-63.

findings.where: 10-suspect.json DM-SUS-PAED-01, DM-SUS-PAED-02 (need a symptom), DM-SUS-INCID-01/-02 (adult only); 60-acute-route.json DM-ACU-ROUTE-04 (needs an 'unwell' sign), DM-ACU-ROUTE-01
findings.finding: A child with a raised glucose and no symptom on record gets nothing, and a child with symptoms and a raised glucose is never told 'refer'. Evaluator: 8-year-old, meter 13.0, nothing else recorded -> nothing fires. Same child, meter 17.9 -> nothing fires. Meter 13.0 with every symptom recorded absent -> nothing fires. 15-year-old, meter 14.5 -> nothing fires. 9-year-old with thirst and polyuria, meter 19, ketones negative (criteria set MET) -> DM-SUS-PAED-01 'capillary glucose now' (already done) and DM-ACU-ROUTE-01 'test urine ketones today' (already done): both proposals are test.order, neither is a referral. The sentence 'a raised glucose is a same-day referral' exists only in PAED-01's notes.
findings.why: Rule 3 (recognition and referral) and the same hole R1 found for adults in F14: the value is seen and the patient is dropped. A child's glucose in this range is type 1 diabetes until shown otherwise and can become ketoacidosis within a day; the history is exactly what is missing when a relative brings the child. NICE NG18 and ISPAD 2022 (both in the dossier) give the action: same-day referral.
findings.reviewerFix: Add a child rule: any glucose above REF-DM-ACU-PAED-GLU, or a meter reading HI, whatever the symptoms -> same_day, proposal kind 'refer' to a hospital with paediatric care ('repeat the reading now; do not wait for a fasting test'); immediate when ROUTE-04's signs are present. Make the child criteria-met state emit a referral, not a second test. Vignettes: child, glucose alone; child, symptoms plus glucose, ketones negative.
findings.done: DM-SUS-PAED-03: a child with a glucose above 11 or HI is referred today whatever the symptoms. The 'test now' prompts clear once a glucose is recorded. DMV-64.

findings.where: 40-stratify.json interpretation hba1c_control_general/-relaxed/-tight, targetsProposed tgt_hba1c_*; 50-act.json DM-ACT-RX-01, -02 (notWhen relaxed), -04, -11; build/build.py run_vignette (reads_blocked is applied to criteria, stages and classifications only); 20-confirm.json all nine HbA1c caveats
findings.finding: An HbA1c that the pack's own blocking caveat calls invalid is still shown as 'At target' and still drives treatment steps. Evaluator: type 2 on metformin, on ART (caveat hba1c_hiv_on_art, 'underestimates glycaemia'), HbA1c 6.4 -> band 'At target'. Sickle cell disease, HbA1c 5.4 -> 'At target'. G6PD deficiency, 6.9 -> 'At target'. eGFR 29 on gliclazide, 6.1 -> 'At target', and tgt_hba1c_ckd is proposed although its own note says HbA1c is unreliable below 30. Iron deficiency (caveat: 'falsely RAISES HbA1c'), HbA1c 7.3 with fasting plasma glucose 5.9 -> HbA1c band 'Above target', fasting band 'At target', and DM-ACT-RX-01 fires ('first medicine is metformin'). Frail 80-year-old, eGFR 22, HbA1c 6.4 -> DM-ACT-RX-11 fires on the blocked value.
findings.why: Rule 2: an invalid result is being read as normal. The F05 fix made blocked criteria and stages 'insufficient in both directions' but stopped short of the bands and steps, and the note added with that fix says 'routine steps that rest on the blocked value are held', which is true only for urine albumin. HIV on ART, sickle trait, malaria-related haemolysis and CKD are everyday here: these are the patients for whom a green HbA1c is false reassurance.
findings.reviewerFix: In the evaluator, a band whose feature is under a blocking caveat is not rendered; show 'HbA1c not valid for this patient: use glucose' and propose the glucose surrogate target instead of tgt_hba1c_*. RX-01, RX-04, RX-11 and the 'relaxed target' notWhen must not read a blocked HbA1c (fall back to the fasting or meter arm, or show the step as a named gap). Add a vignette: on ART, HbA1c 6.4; assert no HbA1c band.
findings.done: A value under a blocking caveat is not banded, is not the measure of a proposed target, and is not read by a treatment-review step. DMV-65, DMV-35.

findings.where: 40-stratify.json interpretation fpg_control_who, ppg_control_who, fcap_control_who, pcap_control_who, hba1c_control_*, bp_*_who_hearts_d (appliesTo is empty, so they are read in pregnancy)
findings.finding: The non-pregnant control bands are applied to pregnant women. Evaluator: 26-year-old with known type 1, 14 weeks pregnant, fasting meter 6.8 -> fcap_control_who 'At target'; fasting plasma 6.9 -> fpg_control_who 'At target'; a post-meal value is 'Above target' only from 9.0; HbA1c 7.4 is banded against the general tier although the pregnancy HbA1c caveat is in force. Targets are correctly withheld in pregnancy (appliesTo not_pregnant); the bands were missed.

Pregnancy targets are much tighter (WHO 2025 pregnancy recommendations; ADA Standards of Care, pregnancy section: the CSO supplies any number). A green band at an antenatal clinic with only a meter is the message that will be acted on.
findings.reviewerFix: Give every stratify band appliesTo.pregnancy = not_pregnant, as the targets have. In pregnancy show only the LOW band and the text 'targets in pregnancy are set by the specialist antenatal team'. findings.done: No stratify band is shown in pregnancy. DMV-66.

findings.where: 60-acute-route.json DM-ACU-ROUTE-11, DM-ACU-ROUTE-13 (both new, both 'immediate'); vignettes DMV-10, DMV-37
findings.finding: Two new interrupts fire on ordinary clinic patients. Evaluator: known type 2 on metformin, random meter 12.0, abdominal pain, nothing else -> ROUTE-11 immediate ('suspected ketoacidosis or hyperosmolar state. Route now') AND ROUTE-13 immediate. Known type 2, abdominal pain only, glucose 6.8 and ketones negative both on record -> ROUTE-13 immediate ('capillary glucose and ketones now'). Known type 2 on metformin, one vomit, glucose 6.0 -> ROUTE-13 immediate. Gastroenteritis with a normal glucose and negative ketones -> ROUTE-13 immediate plus four caveats. A true HHS patient (glucose 38, drowsy, dry) gets three interrupts and one same-day prompt for one event (ROUTE-11, -13, -14, -01); DMV-37 and DMV-10 assert ROUTE-13 as correct although glucose and ketones are already recorded.
findings.why: Rule 9. A glucose of 11.1 or more is the usual finding in a Ugandan diabetes clinic, abdominal pain is one of the commonest outpatient complaints, and metformin itself causes nausea and vomiting. The source for ROUTE-11 (REF-DM-ACT-REFER-SAMEDAY) lists 'suspicion of ketoacidosis or HHS' for same-day referral, and the pack's own WHO Table 5 quote starts ketoacidosis at a higher glucose than 11.1. An interrupt that fires on dyspepsia will be dismissed by reflex on the day it is right. ROUTE-13 also never clears: it asks for two tests that are on the record.
findings.reviewerFix: Split by sign. Deep rapid breathing, acetone breath, drowsiness or worse, dehydration: immediate (as now). Vomiting or abdominal pain alone: same_day 'check ketones', becoming immediate with a second sign, with ketones present, or above a glucose threshold taken from a sourced entry (WHO HEARTS-D Table 5 or REF-DM-ACU-KETONE-TEST-GLU; CSO to choose, do not coin one). ROUTE-13: notWhen a capillary glucose AND a ketone result are recorded at this encounter (rules 02, 06, 07, 11, 14 then decide); when one rule of the set fires immediate, the others should attach to it, not interrupt again. Correct DMV-10 and DMV-37.
findings.done: The interrupt needs a sign (deep breathing, acetone breath, dehydration, drowsiness). Vomiting or pain alone with a raised glucose is a same-day ketone test (ROUTE-19). One interrupt per event: the hyperosmolar rule takes precedence, and test prompts clear when the result is recorded. DMV-67, DMV-37, DMV-10.

findings.where: 60-acute-route.json DM-ACU-ROUTE-15 (new, immediate, runs always), DM-ACU-ROUTE-04 (ketone arm)
findings.finding: The child rules over-fire. Evaluator: 8-year-old with diarrhoea, dehydration recorded, nothing else -> ROUTE-15 immediate ('capillary glucose now'). 7-year-old, dehydrated, capillary glucose 5.2 already recorded -> ROUTE-15 immediate again. A 17-year-old banded adolescent with dehydration -> the same interrupt, worded 'a child'. 8-year-old, not diabetic, vomiting, urine ketones 2+, glucose 4.5 (starvation ketosis) -> ROUTE-04 immediate, 'hospital now', condition 'dka'.
findings.why: Rule 9. Dehydration from diarrhoea is among the commonest paediatric presentations in Uganda, and ketonuria in a vomiting child who has not eaten is normal physiology. NICE's trigger (quoted in the dossier) is an osmotic symptom TOGETHER with one of these signs; ISPAD's is 'any unwell young person', which supports a test, not an interrupt on every dry child. A glucose test in a drowsy or deeply breathing child is right and worth the interrupt; the breadth is the problem.
findings.reviewerFix: ROUTE-15: immediate for drowsiness or deep rapid breathing; dehydration alone -> same_day; notWhen a glucose is recorded at this encounter. ROUTE-04: the ketone arm needs known diabetes, or a glucose above REF-DM-ACU-PAED-GLU, or no glucose on record. Add both negatives as vignettes.
findings.done: ROUTE-15 interrupts only for deep breathing or drowsiness and clears when a glucose is recorded. Dehydration or ketones alone is a same-day glucose test (ROUTE-18). Ketones no longer fire the hospital-now rule on their own. DMV-83.

findings.where: 20-confirm.json diagnosisPending consensus_2021_remission (criterion remission_hba1c, notWhen remission_glucose_high, x.note); 01-features.json haemolysis, malaria_current, recent_transfusion (read by nothing)
findings.finding: Remission is still offered when the record contradicts it. Evaluator: type 2, off medicines 4 months, HbA1c 6.0, FASTING METER 9.5 -> remission 'met', while DM-ACT-RX-01B fires ('above target: first medicine is metformin') and the band reads 'Above target'. HbA1c 6.0 with a 2-hour OGTT of 12.0 and a post-meal value above target -> 'met'. HbA1c 6.0 with malaria, haemolysis and a recent transfusion recorded and no glucose at all -> 'met'. HbA1c 6.0, months-off 4, but metformin on the medicine list -> 'met'. (The R1 patient, type 1 off insulin, is now 'not met' and fires ROUTE-09.)
findings.why: Two outputs that contradict each other on one screen, and a note that claims a protection that does not exist: 'an HbA1c that reads falsely low (haemolysis, malaria, a variant, recent transfusion) is blocked by its validity caveat'. No caveat reads those three features. The consensus definition needs the person to be off treatment and the HbA1c to be believable.
findings.reviewerFix: Add to the notWhen: fasting capillary at or above REF-DM-DX-FPG, ogtt_2h_pg at or above REF-DM-DX-OGTT2H, and the post-meal field. Add glucose_lowering_therapy == none to the criterion. Add blocking HbA1c caveats for haemolysis, current or recent malaria and recent transfusion (the features exist), or delete the sentence from the note. findings.done: Remission needs 'no glucose-lowering medicine' recorded and is 'not met' with a fasting meter reading, an OGTT or a post-meal value in the diabetes range. A caveat for haemolysis, malaria and transfusion is added. DMV-82.

findings.where: 30-classify.json classifications type_1 (supportedBy now holds t1_antibody only); build/k_review.py F18 block
findings.finding: Removing the C-peptide criteria (F18) left one supporting criterion, so a negative antibody now makes the state 'not met'. Evaluator: thin 19-year-old, established diabetes, islet_autoantibodies negative -> classification type_1 'not_met'; antibody not done -> 'insufficient'. In 0.2.0 the second criterion kept this at 'insufficient' or 'unavailable'.
findings.why: The pack's own note on this item says a negative antibody does not refute type 1 and that about 65% of young clinically diagnosed type 1 in Uganda, Cameroon and South Africa was antibody negative. 'Type 1: not met' beside a lean young adult is an invitation to tablets. Few sites can measure antibodies, but those that can will see the wrong state. This is a regression from a fix.
findings.reviewerFix: A classification must not become 'not met' on a negative discriminator that its own note says does not refute. Either cap this classification's negative state at 'insufficient' in the evaluator, or keep a second, clinical supporting criterion so that a negative antibody alone cannot close it. Add a vignette: antibody negative, lean, young; expect 'insufficient' and DM-CLS-T1-05 or T1-02 still firing.
findings.done: The type 1 classification can never be 'not met': a negative antibody leaves it 'insufficient'. DMV-68.

findings.where: 50-act.json DM-ACT-RX-02 (cautions only; no contraindication, no needsBeforeActing), DM-ACT-RX-03; vignette DMV-35
findings.finding: 'Add a sulfonylurea' still fires where metformin has to stop, and fires blind where kidney function is unknown. Evaluator: metformin, eGFR 28, above target -> red flag 'metformin contraindicated below this eGFR', same-day kidney referral, AND DM-ACT-RX-02 'On metformin alone ... WHO's next step is to add a sulfonylurea' with a caution chip; DMV-35 asserts this as the correct output. Metformin, above target, eGFR never recorded -> RX-02 fires with no gap and no caution (RX-01 and RX-01B do report 'kidney function not known').
findings.why: The step's premise ('on metformin alone: add') is void once metformin must stop, and a sulfonylurea at this eGFR is the highest-risk choice for hypoglycaemia; the caution text even quotes ADA on that. R1's F01 asked that the system stop proposing a step-up here. For the long-standing metformin patient whose creatinine has never been done, nothing says so at the moment a second renally sensitive medicine is proposed.
findings.reviewerFix: RX-02 and RX-03: notWhen egfr below REF-DM-RX-METFORMIN-STOP-EGFR (replace with 'treatment needs re-planning with the prescriber; refer'), and needsBeforeActing egfr with the same text RX-01 uses. Consider a gap or amber flag for anyone on metformin with no eGFR on record. Change DMV-35 to expect RX-02 held.
findings.done: The sulfonylurea and insulin steps are silent below an eGFR of 30 and name 'kidney function not known' when it is missing. DMV-35 corrected.

findings.where: 50-act.json therapyFlag ras_blocker_potassium_high (now capped below 6.0); 60-acute-route.json DM-ACU-ROUTE-16, DM-ACU-ROUTE-05; vignette DMV-54

findings.where: 50-act.json DM-ACT-RX-11 (sulfonylurea only); 40-stratify.json hba1c_control_*, fcap_control_who, bp_*_who_hearts_d (no lower edge); dossier REF-DM-RX-OLDER
findings.finding: The frail old person on insulin is shown green. Evaluator: 79-year-old, frail, cognitively impaired, on insulin, fasting meter 4.2, HbA1c 5.9 on the relaxed tier -> both bands 'At target', hypoglycaemia risk 'High', six targets proposed, no review prompt. The same man on insulin with nothing else recorded -> 'At target', risk 'Raised'. DM-ACT-RX-11 ('likely overtreated') fires only when a sulfonylurea is on the list. Still open from F07: 78-year-old on glibenclamide with HbA1c 5.2 -> 'At target'; systolic 80 -> 'At target'.

findings.reviewerFix: Extend RX-11 to insulin and to any person whose risk band is 'high'; take the HbA1c and fasting lower limits for older adults from ADA's older-adults goals table and the consensus paper RX-11 already cites (CSO to supply; do not coin one). findings.finding: The targets contradict each other and contradict RX-10. Evaluator: DMV-41 (78-year-old on glibenclamide, a low needing help, meter 2.6) is proposed 'HbA1c below 7.0%', 'below 8.0%' and 'below 7.5%' together; the frail man above gets six targets. Showing 'below 7.0%' to a person the same screen flags for severe hypoglycaemia is the wrong message; and the F32 fix widened RX-10 without widening the target it points to.
findings.reviewerFix: notWhen on tgt_hba1c_general when the relaxed criterion is met. Make tgt_hba1c_relaxed read the same three answers as RX-10. Offer the age-65 option as an alternative, never as a second proposal beside 'relaxed'.
findings.done: The general and older-adult targets are not proposed when a reason to relax is recorded; the relaxed target reads the same lows as RX-10. DMV-41, DMV-28, DMV-32, DMV-69.

findings.where: build/build.py preg_state and applies(); 30-classify.json DM-CLS-T1-04, DM-CLS-T1-01 (gated on the non-pregnant criteria set being MET); 50-act.json every step and target with appliesTo not_pregnant

Evaluator: thin 24-year-old woman, weight loss, thirst, meter 16.5, pregnancy box empty -> the criteria set is 'insufficient', so DM-CLS-T1-04 ('do not assume type 2: check ketones now') does not run; with pregnant = false it fires. Established 30-year-old woman on metformin, HbA1c 9.0, glucose 17.5, on an ACE inhibitor and a statin, pregnancy box empty -> no targets, no RX-02, no RX-04 (both fire with pregnant = false), no medicine flag; the only gap shown is on the remission set. findings.where: 10-suspect.json DM-SUS-INCID-02 (plasma and HbA1c arms only), DM-SUS-INCID-01 (from 11.1)

findings.reviewerFix: Add to INCID-02: capillary_glucose at or above REF-DM-DX-FPG with context fasting. Add a district vignette.
findings.done: DM-SUS-INCID-03 for a fasting meter reading of 7.0 or more. DMV-72.

findings.where: 40-stratify.json complication diabetic_retinopathy (criterion dr_any, both stagings); 50-act.json DM-ACT-SCREEN-EYE-01 and its note
findings.finding: A 'normal' retina is accepted unless the method was recorded as undilated. Evaluator: retinopathy_stage none, fundus_method not recorded -> stage 'No apparent retinopathy', complication 'not_met'. Stage none with retina_view 'inadequate' -> the same, while DM-ACT-REFER-EYE-02 fires for the inadequate view. findings.reviewerFix: Stage 'none' and 'no macular oedema' require fundus_method in [photograph, dilated_ophthalmoscopy, slit_lamp] AND retina_view adequate; otherwise 'insufficient'. findings.done: 'No retinopathy' counts only on an adequate view through dilated pupils, on a photograph or at the slit lamp; an undilated or inadequate look keeps 'retinal examination due' open. DMV-73, DMV-21.

findings.where: 30-classify.json DM-CLS-T1-05 (needs dm_type_recorded == unclassified); 60-acute-route.json DM-ACU-ROUTE-09 (needs the medicine list), DM-ACU-ROUTE-07 (needs the medicine list), DM-ACU-ROUTE-13 (needs dm_status known)
findings.finding: Four new safety rules are silent unless a specific answer was entered. Evaluator: 22-year-old on glibenclamide, BMI 18, diagnosed at 21, type never recorded -> T1-05 does not fire (routine T1-02 only); with 'unclassified' entered it fires same-day. Type 1 recorded, medicine list not recorded -> ROUTE-09 silent (an empty list fires it). Known type 1 child, glucose 3.4, medicine list not recorded -> nothing fires at all. Adult with known diabetes, a low needing help, fasting meter 3.5, medicine list not recorded -> no acute rule, no RX-10, no flag. Comatose 75-year-old on glibenclamide whose dm_status is not recorded, no glucose yet -> only the age flag.
findings.why: This is R1's F06 trap again in new rules: the rule depends on a field that is often blank. 'Nobody has classified the type' is normally a blank, not a recorded 'unclassified'.
findings.reviewerFix: T1-05: fire on the features and use notWhen dm_type_recorded in [type_1, type_2, gestational, other], which the grammar already supports. ROUTE-07: add arms for dm_type_recorded == type_1 and for dm_status == known with hypo_worst_12m in the significant set. ROUTE-13: add 'on insulin or a sulfonylurea' beside 'known diabetes'. Phase 0 must confirm that 'no medicines' reaches the engine as a recorded empty list, not as missing.
findings.done: Four rules no longer need a field to have been filled: T1-05 (type blank), ROUTE-09 (medicine list blank), ROUTE-07 (type 1 or known diabetes), ROUTE-20 (drowsy with insulin or a sulfonylurea on the list). DMV-75 to DMV-77.

findings.where: build/k_review.py NEUTRAL and apply_neutral (display only); 50-act.json therapyFlags sulfonylurea_with_rifampicin, dolutegravir_with_metformin, ras_blocker_or_statin_could_conceive (action); 20-confirm.json glucose_tb_at_diagnosis, capillary_glucose_tb_at_diagnosis, fasting_glucose_tb_at_diagnosis (alternative); 50-act.json DM-ACT-SCREEN-TB-01 (proposal test 'tb_assessment')
findings.finding: The F10 sweep covered display strings only. By reading the catalog (not an evaluator result): each restricted item has a neutralDisplay, but the text that tells staff what to do has no neutral form and names the class: 'WHO keeps metformin as the initial medicine during TB treatment'; 'UCG 2023 HIV chapter: dolutegravir ... Review with the prescriber and the ART clinic'; 'Discuss pregnancy plans and contraception'; 'Reassess glycaemia after the first month of TB treatment'. The build check tests neutralDisplay alone.
findings.why: Rule 7. R1 asked for a sweep of 'every display/label/action'. A surface that swaps the display for the neutral one and prints the action or the alternative beside it leaks the class. I could not see how the platform renders these, so this is a risk to close, not an observed leak.
findings.reviewerFix: Add neutralAction and neutralAlternative (and a neutral proposal code) to every item with restrictedClasses, and extend the build check to every string a surface can render. State in the pack which fields a patient-facing surface may show.
findings.done: Restricted items carry a neutral action and a neutral alternative as well as a neutral display; the build checks all three for restricted words.

findings.finding: The ordinary uncontrolled patient gets three same-day prompts and three treatment directions, and prompts do not clear once done. Evaluator: known type 2 on metformin, well, random meter 19, ketones recorded negative, above target on tablets -> ROUTE-01 same-day ('test urine ketones today', already negative), REFER-GLU-01 same-day ('refer today'), RX-04 same-day ('consider insulin'), RX-02 routine ('add a sulfonylurea'). New adult with thirst and a meter reading already recorded -> SUS-SYMP-01 'test glucose today'.
findings.why: Rule 9. A reading of 18 or more on tablets is routine in Ugandan clinics (R1 said so in F19 and F25; RX-04 was narrowed but kept same-day). 'Add a tablet', 'consider insulin' and 'refer today' cannot all be the next step, and a prompt for a test whose result is on the screen teaches people to ignore the lane.
findings.reviewerFix: Give the steps a precedence: when REFER-GLU-01 or RX-04 fires, hold RX-02. Make RX-04 routine unless symptoms of hyperglycaemia are recorded. Add notWhen 'result recorded at this encounter' to every rule whose proposal is a test (ROUTE-01, -08, -09, -10, -13, -15, SUS-SYMP-01, PAED-01, T1-04, T1-05), and say in the text what follows a negative result.
findings.done: The sulfonylurea, insulin and 'consider insulin' steps stand down at a glucose of 18 or more, where WHO refers. 'Consider insulin' is routine. Every test prompt clears when its result is recorded. DMV-78.

findings.where: 10-suspect.json DM-SUS-RISK-03, DM-SUS-PREG-01; 50-act.json DM-ACT-SCREEN-LIPID-01, DM-ACT-RX-05, DM-ACT-RX-05B and every therapy_review step (notes say 'off by default', 'off at district sites', 'dark until D-DM-20')
findings.finding: 'Off by default' exists only as a sentence in a note. Evaluator, district site: 36-year-old, lean, never tested -> DM-SUS-RISK-03 fires (note: 'ADA only ... off by default'). Known type 2 with cardiovascular disease, lipids never done -> DM-ACT-SCREEN-LIPID-01 and DM-ACT-RX-05 fire (notes: 'off at district sites by default'). DM-SUS-PREG-01 offers a 75 g OGTT at every district antenatal vignette. No item carries a field that the engine or the evaluator reads to keep it dark.
findings.why: Rule 10. The CSO is told that treatment steps are dark until D-DM-20 and that ADA-only rules are off; anyone who loads the catalog as built gets them on. The decisions themselves are the CSO's and are not re-reported here; the missing switch is the finding.
findings.reviewerFix: Add an explicit field (for example x.enabled: false with x.enabledBy: the decision id, and x.requiresCapability for the district cases), make the evaluator honour it, and assert in a vignette that a dark rule stays silent.
findings.done: x.enabled is false, with the decision that turns it on, for universal testing from 35, the pregnancy OGTT prompt and every treatment-review step except the three that ask for less treatment. The lipid prompt and ADA's risk rule need a laboratory. The evaluator reports such items as 'met but dark'. DMV-79, DMV-16.

findings.finding: Urgency and wording disagree: ROUTE-09 says 'now' in display and proposal but is same_day; PAED-01 is immediate with proposal tier 'today'.
findings.why: Rule 10.
findings.reviewerFix: Make urgency, display and proposal tier say the same thing.
findings.done: Urgency, display and proposal tier agree on ROUTE-09, ROUTE-10 and PAED-01.

findings.finding: Display says 're-test 6 to 12 weeks after the birth'; evaluator fires it at 160 weeks post partum when 'tested since birth' is unanswered.
findings.why: F38 partly fixed.
findings.reviewerFix: Add an upper bound from the source or hand over to DM-SUS-RISK-05 after it.
findings.done: PREG-02 still has no upper bound; it clears on 'tested since the birth'. An upper bound needs a source.

findings.finding: The 'never tested' arm cannot be true: previous gestational diabetes or a previous borderline result means a glucose test was done. Labels say 'never tested since', predicates read 'never had any test'.
findings.why: Rule 10; dead arm.
findings.reviewerFix: Use a 'tested since' input, as PREG-02 and ANTIPSYCH-01 do.
findings.done: Harmless: the 'never tested' arm of two re-test rules cannot be true. Left for tidying.

findings.finding: Both run in pregnancy. Evaluator: pregnant, fasting plasma 9.8 -> INCID-02 'repeat on another day' beside PREG-02 'diabetes in pregnancy: refer today'.
findings.why: Contradiction; WHO 2013 needs one value in pregnancy.
findings.reviewerFix: notWhen pregnant.
findings.done: The single-result rules stand down in pregnancy, where the pregnancy rules refer.

findings.finding: Caveats fire with no value to qualify: a known diabetic with gastroenteritis, glucose 6.8, ketones negative gets three identical 'a raised glucose may be transitory' caveats and 'strips underestimate ketones'; TB adds three more.
findings.why: Noise on established patients.
findings.reviewerFix: Require the feature to be recorded and in the raised range, and diabetes not established; one caveat per reason.
findings.done: A warning on a value shows only when that value is recorded. Blocking caveats still show without one, because they say which test not to order.

findings.finding: 'HI satisfies every high-glucose rule' is not true: the criteria sets, INCID-01, RX-04, REFER-GLU-01, ROUTE-08 and the bands do not read it. Evaluator: thin 22-year-old, meter HI, thirst, polyuria, weight loss -> criteria 'insufficient', T1-04 silent (ROUTE-14 does interrupt).
findings.why: Rule 10.
findings.reviewerFix: Read HI wherever the highest meter threshold is read, or correct the note.
findings.done: HI is read by the suspicion rule, the same-day referral, the type 1 warning and a symptomatic criterion; the feature note says exactly where.

findings.finding: Skips random plasma glucose: laboratory random 16 with thirst -> no ketone prompt; a meter 16 gets one.
findings.why: Inconsistent.
findings.reviewerFix: Add random_pg.
findings.done: ROUTE-08 reads random plasma glucose.

findings.finding: Transient-albumin hold is uneven: RX-05B is suppressed by a fever even when it is the eGFR arm that is met; ALB-02 (ACR above 70) is not suppressed at all.
findings.why: notWhen broader and narrower than its reason.
findings.reviewerFix: Apply the hold to the albumin arms only, on all three albumin steps.
findings.done: A caveat on the albumin count holds the albumin arm only; the ACR-above-70 referral is held too.

findings.finding: No stop condition: RX-10 is same-day at every visit for 12 months after one severe low, even after the regimen was changed; SCREEN-PREG-01 is same-day at every antenatal visit.
findings.why: Rule 9.
findings.reviewerFix: Clear on a recorded review or referral.
findings.done: RX-10 and SCREEN-PREG-01 have no stop condition: the engine's 'done at this episode' state owns it.

findings.finding: On insulin with nothing else recorded -> band 'baseline' (tone low) because the higher bands were insufficient, not because they were excluded.
findings.why: Rule 2 in a first-match table.
findings.reviewerFix: Show 'not assessed' until the risk questions are answered.
findings.done: The baseline risk band still shows when the higher bands are unanswered. Display wording for the engine.

findings.finding: Both fire on the never-tested patient at 14 weeks, with the same neutral text twice.
findings.why: Duplicate.
findings.reviewerFix: Suppress -02 when -01 fires.
findings.done: The yearly antipsychotic rule stands down when the 12-week rule fires.

findings.finding: Moved to established_or_met but reads age_at_diagnosis, which is not recorded at the diagnosis visit, so it cannot fire there (DMV-50: BMI 17, age 24, silent).
findings.why: Fix without effect.
findings.reviewerFix: Read age_years when the diagnosis is new.
findings.done: ATYP-01 cannot fire at the diagnosis visit (it needs age at diagnosis); T1-04 covers that visit.

findings.finding: Display wording: RX-02 'on metformin alone' is not tested (metformin plus a DPP-4 inhibitor fires it); RX-04 says 'Type 2' and includes unclassified; the flag's action cites ADA level 2 or 3 for 'repeated self-treated lows'.
findings.why: Rule 10.
findings.reviewerFix: Reword or test.
findings.done: RX-02, RX-04 and the hypoglycaemia flag reworded to what they test.

findings.finding: 'Treat as insulin-deficient' and a type review fire same-day on a type 2 patient with gastroenteritis, glucose 5.5 and urine ketones 2+.
findings.why: Starvation ketosis; and 'treat as' is management wording in an acute state.
findings.reviewerFix: Reword to 'do not assume type 2'; the acute rule already routes.
findings.done: T1-01 needs known diabetes or a raised glucose as well as ketones.

findings.reviewerFix: Do not suppress when a glucose measure is above target.
findings.done: RX-01 is held by a relaxed target only when the fasting glucose is recorded at or below 7.0.

findings.finding: Shown under 16 with adult sick-day wording ('test again in 2 hours').
findings.why: Rule 3.
findings.reviewerFix: Gate like the stratify bands, or reword to 'refer'.
findings.done: The ketone table's alert wording is the same for a child. Children are routed by rules, not by this table; reword when the paediatric pack is written.

findings.finding: BP 220/130 with confusion -> two same-day referrals plus a routine referral and a routine treatment review side by side.
findings.why: Mixed message.
findings.reviewerFix: Hold routine BP items when a same-day one fires.
findings.done: The symptomatic blood-pressure rule stands down when the higher one fires. Holding routine items beside a same-day one is the engine's presentation rule.

findings.finding: Counselling steps and four to six targets still show beside an immediate route (DMV-37, DMV-59, whose story says the review 'does not carry on'), and targets are re-proposed after a tier is accepted.
findings.why: Noise.
findings.reviewerFix: Hold routine items while an immediate rule is active.
findings.done: Education steps and targets still show beside an interrupt: a presentation rule for the engine (interrupts first, routine items collapsed).

findings.reviewerFix: Add the option and read it.
