findings.finding: F12, F15 and F30 work only on an explicit answer: evaluator with the 'never' and 'not_known' answers left blank fires nothing.
findings.why: Partly fixed, as the log half-says.
findings.reviewerFix: Design B must supply these facts from the record; say so as a Phase 0 blocker.
findings.done: Three earlier fixes work only on an explicit answer, by design: 'not asked' is never 'never'. Design B's whole-record rules cover the absent case.

findings.finding: Blocking both ways discards a positive: proliferative disease seen without dilation -> complication 'insufficient', no stage (the urgent referral does fire).
findings.why: The caveat's direction is 'masks'.
findings.reviewerFix: Block the negative only for 'masks' caveats.
findings.done: A 'masks' caveat discredits a normal result only. DMV-74.

findings.finding: The decision text does not show the consequence: pregnant, fasting METER 9.8 -> 'urgent: send a laboratory glucose' at a site with no laboratory, while fasting plasma 9.8 is a same-day referral.
findings.why: The CSO should decide it knowingly.
findings.reviewerFix: State the fasting 7.0 to 11.0 meter case in the decision.
findings.done: DM-CON-PREG-05: a fasting meter reading of 7.0 or more in pregnancy is referred today. DMV-81. D-DM-28 states it.

findings.where: 60-acute-route.json DM-ACU-ROUTE-13 (H07/H18 rewrite: urgency set to same_day for every arm); DM-ACU-ROUTE-11 (needs a glucose)
findings.finding: The H07 split left Kussmaul breathing and acetone breath without an interrupt when no glucose is on record yet. Evaluator (own5/own4 P27): known type 1 on insulin, deep_rapid_breathing + acetone_breath, no glucose -> only DM-ACU-ROUTE-13 same_day 'capillary glucose today'; ROUTE-11 cannot fire (needs glucose >= 11.1 or HI), ROUTE-20 needs drowsiness. Same result at a district site (P27b).
findings.why: Deep rapid breathing with acetone on the breath in a person with type 1 is ketoacidosis until shown otherwise; ROUTE-11's own display says 'route now; do not wait for ketones'. 'Today' tells staff it can wait. R3 asked that these signs stay immediate. Breaches rule 4.
findings.reviewerFix: Split ROUTE-13: deep_rapid_breathing, acetone_breath (and drowsiness, already ROUTE-20) with known diabetes or insulin/sulfonylurea -> immediate 'glucose and ketones now; route', whatever the glucose; keep same_day only for vomiting, abdominal pain or dehydration alone. Add a vignette (known type 1, Kussmaul, no glucose -> immediate).
findings.done: DM-ACU-ROUTE-24 interrupts on Kussmaul breathing or acetone in known diabetes at any glucose; ROUTE-13 keeps only vomiting, pain and dehydration. DMV-84.

findings.where: 10-suspect.json DM-SUS-SYMP-01 and -02 notWhen 'sym*_done' (k_review.py 'found while reading the evaluator's output', H20): any=GLU_REC()+[REC('hba1c')]
findings.finding: A recorded HbA1c silences the symptomatic glucose test. Evaluator (P28): thin 22-year-old, BMI 19, polyuria + polydipsia + unexplained weight loss, hba1c 5.6 on record, no glucose -> NOTHING fires (SYMP-01 'suppressed'; criteria sets insufficient; T1-04 needs a glucose).
findings.why: HbA1c lags acute-onset (type 1) hyperglycaemia and is less reliable in this population (anaemia, haemoglobinopathy); the pack's own caveats say so. 'recorded' has no date, so an old HbA1c from the record would do the same under Design B. The classic young, thin, symptomatic patient - the one who presents next in DKA - gets no prompt. Breaches rules 2 and 4.
findings.reviewerFix: Remove REC('hba1c') from both notWhen lists; clear only on a glucose recorded at this encounter (see J19). Add a vignette: classic symptoms with a normal HbA1c on record -> SYMP-01 fires.
findings.done: HbA1c no longer silences the symptom rules. DMV-85.

findings.where: 60-acute-route.json DM-ACU-ROUTE-19 notWhen acu_mild_ketones_done, DM-ACU-ROUTE-03 notWhen acu_edka_done, DM-ACU-ROUTE-01 notWhen acu_glu18_done, DM-ACU-ROUTE-13 notWhen acu_known_unwell_done (H07, H20)
findings.finding: Test prompts now clear on ANY result, and nothing picks up a result that is not reassuring. Evaluator (h_crit3/own3): known type 1 on insulin, glucose 22, vomiting, bohb 2.4 -> nothing fires except the band bohb_bands 'at_risk' ('At risk of DKA: seek advice as soon as possible'). Known type 2, glucose 25, vomiting, urine ketones 1+ -> nothing fires. On an SGLT2 inhibitor, vomiting + abdominal pain, glucose 9.0, urine ketones trace -> nothing fires (ROUTE-03 suppressed; caveat urine_ketones_low_despite_picture shown; red flag sglt2_during_acute_illness silent because it reads acute_illness_current only). Known type 1 vomiting, glucose 7.0 -> nothing fires. Type 1, glucose 22, vomiting, urine ketones neg at a district site -> nothing.
findings.why: ROUTE-19's own display promises 'ketones of 2+ makes it an emergency'; the rule disappears as soon as a 1+ or trace is typed, and ROUTE-02 needs 2+/3.0. The pack's bohb_bands table calls 1.6 to 3.0 'at risk of DKA' yet no rule carries urgency; the pack's own caveat says urine strips underestimate ketones (worst on SGLT2). A vomiting person with type 1 is a sick-day emergency (the pack's EDU-04 tells the patient 'come in if vomiting'). Breaches rules 2 and 4; regression from the H07/H20 fixes.
findings.reviewerFix: A test prompt may clear only on a result the source calls reassuring: urine 'neg' or bohb in bohb_bands 'normal'. Add a same_day rule (immediate with a sign) for a known diabetic who is vomiting/in pain with urine ketones trace/1+ or bohb in the 'raised'/'at_risk' bands, thresholds from the REF behind bohb_bands; on an SGLT2 inhibitor clear ROUTE-03 only on a blood ketone below the 'raised' band. Add a type 1 + vomiting rule (whatever the glucose) from ADA/ISPAD sick-day guidance (CSO to sign the source). Let sglt2_during_acute_illness also read vomiting/abdominal pain. Vignettes for each case above.
findings.done: ROUTE-21 (ketones 0.6 to 1.5 or trace/1+), ROUTE-22 (1.6 to 2.9, urgent) and ROUTE-23 (type 1 or insulin, vomiting, ketones today) close the gap below 2+; the SGLT2 flag reads vomiting, pain and dehydration. A prompt now clears only on a normal ketone result. DMV-86 to DMV-89.

findings.where: build/build.py run_vignette gate('established_or_met') x preg_state (H02 x H15); 50-act.json DM-ACT-REFER-EGFR-01, -BP-01, -BP-03, -EYE-01/-02/-03, -ALB-*, -PVD-01, -CHOL-01, -GLU-01, SCREEN-PREG-01
findings.finding: The H02 fix does not work for women whose pregnancy box is blank (the default after H15). Evaluator (own5 P31): woman 50, new diagnosis (meter 16 + thirst), eGFR 20, BP 230/130 with symptoms, pregnancy not recorded -> who_hearts_d_2020 'insufficient' (gap 'pregnant'), so met_now is false and NO referral fires; the referrals are not even listed as withheld. Same record with pregnancy_possible = false (P31b) -> DM-ACT-REFER-BP-01 and DM-ACT-REFER-EGFR-01 same_day. DMV-62 passes only because the patient is male.
findings.why: eGFR below 30 and BP above 200/110 are WHO HEARTS-D same-day referrals that do not depend on pregnancy or on a diabetes label. Half of all new diagnoses (women, most of whom will not have the pregnancy question answered) lose them silently. Breaches rules 2 and 4.
findings.reviewerFix: Run the kidney, blood-pressure and eye referral steps 'always' (R3's original advice) or gate established_or_met on the non-pregnant criteria evaluated without the pregnancy hold; at minimum list them in 'withheld' with the 'pregnant' gap. Add DMV-62's twin with a woman, pregnancy blank.
findings.done: 'established_or_met' reads the non-pregnant set as if pregnancy were answered. DMV-90.

findings.finding: Fires on children who already have diabetes. Evaluator (h_crit H01d): 12-year-old, known type 1 on insulin, routine visit, meter 14 -> DM-SUS-PAED-03 same_day 'refer today as suspected diabetes, whatever the symptoms' (plus REFER-TARGET-02).
findings.why: Most children with type 1 have readings above 11 at clinic; every visit becomes a same-day referral labelled 'suspected diabetes'. The cited REF-DM-ACU-PAED-GLU is NICE's threshold for a child WITHOUT known diabetes, with symptoms. Rules 9 and 10.
findings.reviewerFix: notWhen dm_status == known or dm_type_recorded recorded. Vignette: known type 1 child, meter 14 -> PAED-03 silent.
findings.done: PAED-03 stands down for a child already diagnosed. DMV-91.

findings.finding: A child with known diabetes and one ordinary symptom interrupts whatever the results. Evaluator (P32): 12-year-old type 1, abdominal pain, glucose 6.0, bohb 0.3 -> ROUTE-04 immediate 'hospital now' (bohb band 'normal'). Same with urine ketones neg (H01e).
findings.why: H08 fixed the non-diabetic arm only. NICE NG18 (the rule's source) asks for blood ketones in a known-diabetic child who is unwell and sends to hospital on the ketone result or the clinical picture; a normal blood ketone and glucose with tummy ache is not 'hospital now'. The adult equivalent was fixed by H07. Rule 9.
findings.reviewerFix: For the KNOWN() arm with only vomiting or abdominal pain: same_day 'glucose and blood ketones now', escalating to immediate on deep breathing, dehydration, drowsiness, or bohb in the source's DKA/at-risk range (NICE NG18 rec 1.4.x; REF behind bohb_bands). Keep immediate when nothing is measured.
findings.done: ROUTE-04 no longer interrupts on known diabetes alone; ROUTE-25 interrupts on signs; ROUTE-23 asks for ketones on vomiting or pain. DMV-92.

findings.finding: Diabetic-foot referrals now fire on anyone. Evaluator (h_crit): adult with dm_status not_known and a foot ulcer -> FOOT-02 urgent 'refer to a higher level of care'; non-diabetic adult with a hot swollen foot -> CHARCOT-01 urgent 'offload and refer'; 8-year-old with a foot ulcer (e.g. jiggers) -> FOOT-02 urgent.
findings.why: Charcot neuroarthropathy needs neuropathy; in a non-diabetic a hot, swollen foot is cellulitis, gout, trauma or DVT, and 'offload' is the wrong instruction. A simple ulcer in a non-diabetic is not a diabetic-foot referral. The labels imply diabetes the predicates do not test. Rules 9 and 10.
findings.reviewerFix: Keep 'always' only for gangrene/deep infection (FOOT-03), limb ischaemia (LIMB-01) and sudden vision loss (VISION-01), worded without diabetes. FOOT-01, FOOT-02 and CHARCOT-01: established_or_met (after J04's fix) or a predicate on dm_status known / glucose-lowering medicine.
findings.done: FOOT-02 and CHARCOT-01 run only with diabetes established or met; gangrene, ischaemia and sight loss still run always. DMV-93.

findings.where: 60-acute-route.json DM-ACU-ROUTE-07 (H18 added KNOWN() to the atLeast; urgency immediate)
findings.finding: Any known diabetic below 3.9 is an interrupt, whatever the treatment. Evaluator (h_major3): known type 2 on metformin only, fasting meter 3.8, well -> ROUTE-07 immediate 'hypoglycaemia, and it can come back'.
findings.why: 'It can come back' is true of insulin and sulfonylureas, not metformin or diet. Level 1 in a person on no hypoglycaemia-causing medicine warrants a recheck, not an interrupt. Phase 0's P0-07 recommends interrupting only below 3.0 or with a sign; D-DM-24 covers only the exact edge. Rules 9 and 10 (display says 'with diabetes' as if the risk were the same).
findings.reviewerFix: Keep immediate for the insulin/sulfonylurea/type 1 arms; for the KNOWN()-only arm use same_day or urgent 'recheck; review cause' (below 3.0 ROUTE-06 already interrupts). Vignette: metformin only, 3.8 -> not immediate.
findings.done: ROUTE-07 interrupts only on insulin, a sulfonylurea or type 1; ROUTE-26 (same day) covers other diabetes. DMV-94.

findings.finding: H07's 'one interrupt per event' is not true. Evaluator: on insulin, glucose 2.4 -> ROUTE-06 immediate AND ROUTE-07 immediate (DMV-63, H03a; child with type 1 at 2.5 the same). DKA picture (glucose 25, Kussmaul, ketones 3+) -> ROUTE-02 immediate AND ROUTE-11 immediate (plus T1-01 same_day). DMV-63 asserts both interrupts as correct.
findings.why: Two interrupts for one event train staff to dismiss them; the disposition of H07 claims it is fixed. Rule 9.
findings.reviewerFix: ROUTE-07 notWhen ROUTE-06's criterion met; ROUTE-11 notWhen ROUTE-02's criterion met (or one 'parent' interrupt with attached items, as R3 proposed). Change DMV-63 to expect ROUTE-07 silent.
findings.done: ROUTE-07 stands down below 3.0 (ROUTE-06); ROUTE-11 stands down on ketones in the DKA range (ROUTE-02). DMV-63 now expects one interrupt.

findings.where: 40-stratify.json fpg_control_who, fcap_control_who, ppg_control_who, pcap_control_who, bp_*_who_hearts_d (H13 fixed_in_part)
findings.finding: The frail old person on insulin is still shown green. DMV-69 (fasting plasma 4.2) -> fpg_control_who 'at_target'. 78-year-old on glibenclamide, HbA1c 5.2, BP 80/50 -> BP bands 'at_target' (tone normal, 'Below the treatment threshold'); no rule notes the low pressure.

findings.where: build/build.py HELD_KINDS + SAFETY_REVIEWS; 50-act.json DM-ACT-RX-11 (H05 side effect)
findings.finding: The overtreatment prompt is silenced exactly where it matters most. Evaluator (h_crit2 H05e): 80-year-old, frail, on gliclazide, eGFR 22, HbA1c 6.4 -> RX-11 not fired (HbA1c blocked by hba1c_low_egfr; RX-11 is therapy_review so it reads the blocked value as insufficient); no gap, no caution. Hypoglycaemia risk 'high'.
findings.why: R3 asked for a fallback or a named gap. CKD G4 plus frailty plus a sulfonylurea is the highest hypoglycaemia risk in the pack; the step that asks for LESS treatment should not be held by a caveat that only makes HbA1c unreliable. EGFR-01 same-day referral mitigates in part.
findings.reviewerFix: Exempt SAFETY_REVIEWS (RX-10, RX-11, RX-11B) from HELD_KINDS, or give RX-11 an arm 'HbA1c not valid for this patient' (blocked) with the same text, and a needsBeforeActing gap. Vignette: this patient -> RX-11 fires.
findings.done: Steps that ask for less treatment read every value, even under a blocking caveat. DMV-95.

findings.where: 40-stratify.json targetsProposed tgt_hba1c_general, tgt_hba1c_relaxed, tgt_hba1c_older_healthy; interpretation hba1c_control_* (H14 fixed)
findings.finding: Targets still contradict the band and each other. Evaluator (h_major2 H36): glycaemic_target_tier 'relaxed' recorded, HbA1c 7.6 -> band hba1c_control_relaxed 'at_target' AND target tgt_hba1c_general 'HbA1c below 7.0%' proposed (relaxed target not proposed: it reads frailty/lows, not the agreed tier). P04: 72-year-old, tier general, HbA1c 7.3 -> band 'above_target' while tgt_hba1c_older_healthy 'below 7.5%' is proposed beside tgt_hba1c_general.
findings.why: The clinician sees 'at target' and 'target below 7.0%' on the same screen. An agreed tier is the strongest statement of the target and is ignored by the proposals.
findings.reviewerFix: tgt_hba1c_general and tgt_hba1c_older_healthy: notWhen glycaemic_target_tier in [relaxed, tight, avoid_symptoms]; tgt_hba1c_relaxed: also when tier == relaxed. Choose the band from the proposed target when no tier is recorded, or show the older-healthy option only as an alternative to the general one (not a second target).
findings.done: A target proposal stands down when a different tier is already agreed. DMV-96.

findings.finding: Partly fixed. Evaluator: retinopathy_stage none, retina_view 'not_attempted' -> nothing fires (H17a). DMV-73 (stage none, method and view not recorded) -> complication 'insufficient' and nothing prompts the examination; the vignette asserts this silence.
findings.why: R3 asked for the 'not_attempted' arm too. A 'no retinopathy' that the pack itself does not accept should leave the examination due, otherwise the eye check is silently skipped. Rule 2.
findings.reviewerFix: Add arms: retina_view == not_attempted; and retinopathy_stage recorded while the complication's notMetRequires is not met. Make DMV-73 expect SCREEN-EYE-01.
findings.done: 'Not attempted' now keeps the eye check due. A retina recorded with no method stays 'insufficient' (DMV-73); a 'method not recorded' prompt needs a not-recorded operator the four-state grammar forbids, so it is Design B's 'never done' logic.

findings.where: 50-act.json DM-ACT-REFER-GLU-01 (needs glucose_goal_unmet_on_oral); DM-ACT-RX-02/-03/-04 notWhen GLU18; 10-suspect.json DM-SUS-INCID-01
findings.finding: A glucose of 18 or more after a negative ketone test reaches no referral unless one optional box is ticked. Evaluator (own3 P21): known type 2 on metformin, meter 25, urine ketones neg, goal field blank -> NOTHING fires; RX-04 is 'suppressed' by the notWhen 'WHO refers... the referral rule applies', but the referral rule did not fire. P22: new adult at a district site, meter 25, asymptomatic, ketones neg -> only DM-SUS-INCID-01 routine 'repeat on another day'.
findings.why: The pack's own REF-DM-ACU-KETONE-TEST-GLU quotes WHO PEN: 'Refer to hospital all patients with plasma glucose levels >= 18 mmol/l'; HEARTS-D Fig. 1 treats FPG/RPG > 18 as severe 'regardless of symptoms'. A notWhen that defers to a rule that cannot fire is a logic error; the missing box is treated as 'not unmet' with no gap. Rules 2 and 8.
findings.reviewerFix: REFER-GLU-01: fire on glucose >= REF-DM-ACU-KETONE-TEST-GLU (or HI) after ketones are known, with glucose_goal_unmet_on_oral as a needsBeforeActing gap rather than a predicate, and run it for the newly found patient as well. CSO chooses between PEN ('refer all') and HEARTS-D section 4 ('no improvement after metformin and/or gliclazide'). RX-02/03/04's GLU18 notWhen must reference the same criterion.
findings.done: DM-ACT-REFER-GLU-02 (WHO PEN) refers glucose 18 or more without ketoacidosis the same day, switched by D-DM-38. DMV-97.

findings.finding: H06 removed the BP bands in pregnancy and nothing replaces them. Evaluator (own3 P19): 32-year-old, 30 weeks, fasting plasma 5.5 (WHO 2013 GDM met), BP 165/105 -> only DM-CON-PREG-01; no BP band, and the REFER-BP rules cannot run (not established, non-pregnant set not met). H06 test: pregnant type 1, BP 150/100 -> no BP signal.
findings.why: R3's H06 concerned glucose bands. A systolic of 160 or more in pregnancy is severe-range hypertension (pre-eclampsia risk, higher with diabetes); silencing the only BP display is a regression. Same-day antenatal referral (PREG-01, SCREEN-PREG-01) mitigates in part.
findings.reviewerFix: Exempt the BP bands from H06, or add a pregnancy BP rule (diabetes in pregnancy with BP at or above the severe threshold -> same day/immediate) with thresholds from WHO's 2011 pre-eclampsia recommendations or UCG 2023 chapter 16 (CSO to supply).
findings.done: ROUTE-27 (140/90 in pregnancy, same day, urine protein) and ROUTE-28 (160/110, interrupt) from UCG 2023 16.3.7. DMV-98.

findings.where: build/build.py run_vignette fire() / management loop; vignette DMV-71, DMV-82
findings.finding: Dark items leak out of the reference evaluator. Evaluator (DMV-82): RX-01B is dark yet appears in steps_fired, urgency {'DM-ACT-RX-01B': 'routine'} and gaps {'DM-ACT-RX-01B': ['egfr']}. DMV-71 / H15b: dark RX-02 and RX-04 are listed in 'withheld' (waiting for the pregnancy answer); DMV-71 asserts this.
findings.why: The evaluator is the parity reference for Phase 2. Ported as-is, a dark step would ask staff for an eGFR or a pregnancy answer to unlock advice that will never show, contradicting H21's 'dark' claim.
findings.reviewerFix: In run_vignette: return early for enabled == False before steps_fired, urgency, cautions, gaps; skip dark items in the withheld branch. Correct DMV-71 to expect RX-02 dark, not withheld.
findings.done: Dark items appear only as dark. DMV-71 now expects RX-02 dark, not withheld.

findings.finding: A district site has no next step for a fasting meter in the intermediate range. Evaluator (own P01): 45-year-old, district, fasting meter 6.4, no symptoms -> nothing fires; who_hearts_d_2020 and who_2006_intermediate 'unavailable'. (DM-SUS-INCID-03 starts at 7.0; EDU-10 needs a prior intermediate result already recorded.)
findings.why: D-DM-04's recommendation reads fasting meter values against WHO's surrogates, and the pack added INCID-03 for 7.0 and above; the 6.1 to 6.9 band (lifestyle advice and a yearly retest per WHO) is the commoner finding and gets silence. Rule 8.
findings.reviewerFix: Add a district rule: fasting capillary glucose >= the WHO 2006 IFG lower value (the REF already used by who_2006_intermediate) and below REF-DM-DX-FPG -> routine 'intermediate range on a meter: confirm with a laboratory glucose where possible; lifestyle; retest in a year', gated by D-DM-04.
findings.done: DM-SUS-INCID-04: fasting meter 6.1 to 6.9 asks for a repeat and an OGTT where possible. DMV-99.

findings.finding: A hypertensive emergency is handled as a same-day referral, the same as a headache. Evaluator (own2 P14): known type 2, BP 230/130, hypertensive_symptoms true -> DM-ACT-REFER-BP-01 same_day plus two education steps; nothing interrupts. P07: 182/112 with headache -> the same single same-day step.
findings.why: hypertensive_symptoms lumps headache with changed mental state, breathlessness and reduced urine, so the pack cannot tell urgency from encephalopathy or pulmonary oedema; the latter are acute danger (rule 4), and there is no 'confused' option to read (H41). WHO HEARTS-D lists all of them as same-day, so the CSO must choose.
findings.reviewerFix: Split the feature (headache/blurred vision vs changed mental state, breathlessness, chest pain, reduced urine output) and route severe BP with the second group to the acute lane; CSO to sign the source (UCG 2023 4.1.6 or the WHO hypertension guideline).
findings.done: DM-ACU-ROUTE-29 interrupts above 180/110 with drowsiness, chest pain or stroke signs (UCG 4.1.6.1); the urgency threshold is D-DM-39. DMV-100.

findings.where: 60-acute-route.json, 10-suspect.json: every notWhen built with op 'recorded' (GLU_REC, KET_REC) - ROUTE-01/-03/-08/-13/-15/-18/-19/-20, SUS-SYMP-01/-02, SUS-PAED-01
findings.finding: 'Recorded' has no time scope. By reading the catalog: the notWhen labels say 'already recorded' and the op is a bare 'recorded'; Phase 0 reports the live engine has no 'recorded' op at all. Under Design B's fact snapshots, a glucose from last month would satisfy it.
findings.why: ROUTE-20 is the only interrupt for a drowsy diabetic with no glucose; if a historic glucose clears it, the hypoglycaemic coma is missed. The same applies to every 'test now' prompt added by H07/H20.
findings.reviewerFix: Define the op as 'recorded at this encounter' (or within a window the CSO sets under D-DM-08) in the pack and in the engine-change spec (EC list); add a vignette with an old glucose and ROUTE-20 still firing.
findings.done: 'Recorded' is defined as recorded at this encounter; Design B carries the time scope.

findings.finding: Partly fixed. By reading the catalog: neutralDisplay/neutralAction/neutralAlternative now exist, but the proposal codes still name the restricted class; R3 asked for 'a neutral proposal code', and no statement of which fields a patient-facing surface may show was found.
findings.why: An order or education item is the part most likely to appear on a patient-facing list ('TB assessment', 'pregnancy planning'). Rule 7.
findings.reviewerFix: Neutral proposal codes (or a neutralProposal) for every restricted item, and extend the build check to proposal strings; state the patient-visible fields in the pack README.
findings.done: Proposals that name a restricted class carry a neutral proposal code.

findings.finding: Evaluator (P07): BP 182/112 with headache -> BP-01 'Blood pressure above 200/110: refer today' fires (diastolic arm); BP-03 is suppressed.
findings.why: The display reads as both numbers above; the patient's systolic is 182. Rule 10.
findings.reviewerFix: Display 'Systolic above 200 or diastolic above 110: refer today'.
findings.done: BP-01's display states both arms.

findings.finding: Not fixed. Evaluator (P29): known type 2 on metformin, vomiting, glucose 5.5, urine ketones 2+ -> T1-01 same_day 'treat as insulin-deficient' (KNOWN() satisfies the atLeast).
findings.why: R3's exact patient; starvation ketosis in gastroenteritis is not evidence about type.
findings.reviewerFix: Drop KNOWN() from the atLeast (ROUTE-02 already routes), or reword to 'do not assume type 2'.
findings.done: T1-01 needs a raised glucose or HI; known diabetes alone no longer suggests type 1.

findings.where: 50-act.json DM-ACT-REFER-TARGET-02 (agesOverride any; note 'type 1 and type 2 alike')
findings.finding: Evaluator: well 19-year-old type 1 (P08) and 12-year-old type 1 (H01d) with HbA1c above 7.5 -> 'refer for review of the insulin'.
findings.why: REF-DM-CTRL-INSULIN-REFER-HBA1C is HEARTS-D's protocol for type 2 on basal insulin; its use for type 1 and children is a pack inference with no needsCsoInput mark.
findings.reviewerFix: Mark needsCsoInput (D-DM-37) or limit to type 2; paediatric targets from ISPAD.
findings.done: REFER-TARGET-02 is for adults with type 2 diabetes.

findings.finding: Evaluator (P06a): on steroids, meter HI, no diabetes -> DRUG-01 silent (reads random_pg, capillary_glucose, postprandial_pg only).
findings.why: HI is the steroid patient's commonest extreme reading.
findings.reviewerFix: Add HI (and fasting_pg) to DRUG-01.
findings.done: DRUG-01 reads a meter HI.

findings.finding: Evaluator: 8-year-old girl (child band) with a foot ulcer -> seven criteria sets 'insufficient' with gap 'pregnant', including who_2013_gdm; every patient on a medicine shows consensus_2021_remission 'insufficient' with gap 'pregnant' though it is not met on the medicine alone.
findings.why: A pregnancy question for a child, and a pregnancy gap on a set already refuted, is noise.
findings.reviewerFix: Treat ageBand child as not_pregnant; evaluate a set's other criteria before adding the pregnancy gap. (Adult women of any age remain P0-02.)
findings.done: A child has pregnancy 'not possible'.

findings.where: 10-suspect.json DM-SUS-INCID-02 notWhen 'a second diabetes-range result on a later day is already recorded'
findings.finding: Evaluator (P05): HbA1c 6.6 twice with sickle cell disease -> diagnosis 'insufficient' (blocked), INCID-02 suppressed; only the caveat suggests glucose.
findings.why: The repeat clears the prompt even though the diagnostic set could not use it.
findings.reviewerFix: Do not suppress when the HbA1c is under a blocking caveat; propose a fasting glucose.
findings.done: Not changed: a blocked HbA1c still counts as the 'second result' that stops INCID-02. Engine presentation in Phase 3 must show the value as blocked.

findings.finding: Evaluator (P24): type 2, diarrhoea, dehydrated, glucose 12 -> ROUTE-11 immediate 'route now; do not wait for ketones'.
findings.why: A common gastroenteritis picture; at 11.1 to 17.9 with dehydration alone a ketone test first is proportionate (rule 9). R3 asked for dehydration to stay immediate, so CSO call.
findings.reviewerFix: Dehydration alone below REF-DM-ACU-KETONE-TEST-GLU: same_day ketone test; immediate with a second sign.
findings.done: Dehydration is a sign that justifies an interrupt (N13).

findings.finding: Evaluator (P23): comatose adult, nothing known -> nothing fires.
findings.why: A glucose in any unresponsive person is standard emergency care; the pack restricts it to known diabetes or insulin/sulfonylurea.
findings.reviewerFix: Consider a drowsy/comatose arm with no glucose on record whatever the history (CSO).
findings.done: An unresponsive person with nothing known belongs to triage's glucose-first rule, not the NCD engine (I4).

findings.finding: By reading: each reads dm_status == known or 'on tablets', so the established_or_met override can never fire at the newly-met visit.
findings.why: Dead configuration that looks like coverage.
findings.reviewerFix: Drop the override or replace dm_status known with the met criterion.
findings.done: Harmless dead overrides; left for tidying.

findings.finding: Evaluator: every diabetic, including obese type 2 on metformin, shows classification type_1 'insufficient'.
findings.why: Display noise.
findings.reviewerFix: Show the type 1 state only when a type-1 rule fires or a discriminator is recorded.
findings.done: Display: a classification shown on every diabetic. Engine presentation in Phase 3.

findings.finding: Evaluator: on insulin with a reading of 2.4 today (H03a) -> risk 'baseline'.
findings.why: The current low is not read by the risk model.
findings.reviewerFix: Read the current glucose below REF-DM-HYPO-L2 into the high band, or show 'not assessed'.
findings.done: Display: the baseline risk band beside a reading taken today. Engine presentation in Phase 3.

findings.where: 60-acute-route.json DM-ACU-ROUTE-21 notWhen acu_ketones_mid_up (J03) x DM-ACU-ROUTE-02 atLeast; DM-ACU-ROUTE-24 atLeast
findings.finding: Ketones in the DKA range reach nothing when the person is on insulin or an SGLT2 inhibitor (or has type 1 recorded) but 'known diabetes' is not ticked and the glucose is below 11.1. ROUTE-21's notWhen hands bohb >= 1.6 / urine 2+ to 'rules 22 and 02', but ROUTE-02's context is only known diabetes, HI or glucose >= 11.1 (no insulin, sulfonylurea, SGLT2 or type 1), and ROUTE-22 stops at 3.0. Evaluator (ketgrid.py, adv.py): insulin on the list, status blank, glucose 7, bohb 3.5 or urine 3+, with or without vomiting -> NOTHING. A13 insulin, vomiting, glucose 8, urine 3+ -> nothing (ROUTE-13 and ROUTE-23 suppressed). A12b SGLT2 inhibitor, vomiting, deep breathing, glucose 9, bohb 4.2 -> only the therapy flag sglt2_during_acute_illness (ROUTE-03 and ROUTE-21 suppressed; ROUTE-24 needs known diabetes or insulin/SU). Type 1 recorded, status blank, glucose 7, bohb 3.5 -> only ROUTE-09 same_day.
findings.why: Euglycaemic ketoacidosis on an SGLT2 inhibitor and partly treated DKA on insulin are exactly the low-glucose presentations. The pack elsewhere accepts the medicine list as evidence of diabetes (ROUTE-13, -20, -21, -22), so a hand-off to a rule with a narrower context silences the most dangerous result (rule 4).
findings.reviewerFix: Give ROUTE-02 the same context as ROUTE-21/22 (known diabetes, type 1 recorded, insulin, sulfonylurea, SGLT2 inhibitor, HI or glucose >= REF-DM-ACU-DKA-GLU), per the 2024 hyperglycaemic-crises consensus already behind REF-DM-ACU-DKA-BOHB (prior diabetes qualifies at any glucose). Add the SGLT2 inhibitor and type 1 to ROUTE-24's atLeast. Build check: every notWhen that says 'rule NN applies' must imply rule NN's criterion. Vignettes: SGLT2, status blank, glucose 9, bohb 4.2 -> ROUTE-02 immediate; insulin, glucose 8, urine 3+ -> ROUTE-02.
findings.done: ROUTE-02 and ROUTE-24 read type 1, insulin, a sulfonylurea and an SGLT2 inhibitor as diabetes at any glucose. DMV-101, DMV-102.

findings.where: 60-acute-route.json DM-ACU-ROUTE-03 notWhen acu_edka_done (unchanged by J03); vignette DMV-88
findings.finding: On an SGLT2 inhibitor with vomiting and abdominal pain, any urine strip still clears the interrupt; R4's fix ('clear ROUTE-03 only on a blood ketone below the raised band') was not applied. Evaluator: A11 SGLT2, vomiting + pain, glucose 9, urine ketones NEG -> only the therapy flag and caveat urine_ketones_low_despite_picture; nothing routes. A12 same with deep breathing and urine trace, status blank -> ROUTE-21 same_day only. DMV-88 (vomiting + pain, glucose 9, urine trace) asserts ROUTE-21 same_day as correct.
findings.why: The pack's own REF-DM-VAL-URINE-KETONE says strips underestimate ketonaemia early in DKA, and its caveat fires on these very patients. A negative or trace strip in SGLT2-associated ketoacidosis is not reassurance; the interrupt is downgraded or removed by the least reliable test.
findings.reviewerFix: ROUTE-03 notWhen: bohb < REF-DM-ACU-KETONE-LOW only. With only a urine result, keep the rule (immediate, or same_day 'blood ketones or blood gas now' if the CSO prefers, under D-DM-37), citing REF-DM-VAL-URINE-KETONE and the SGLT2 euglycaemic-DKA source already in ROUTE-03's citation. Change DMV-88 to expect ROUTE-03; add the urine-negative twin.
findings.done: ROUTE-03 stands down only on a blood ketone below 0.6; a strip never clears it. DMV-88 corrected; DMV-103.

findings.finding: Urgency is inverted: blood ketones 1.6-2.9 ('at risk of DKA', display 'contact the diabetes team now', proposal tier 'now') carry urgency 'urgent', which in this pack means within a window and not today (k_act.py note on EYE: "'urgent' here means inside those windows, not today"; CHARCOT 'urgent' = 1 working day), while the milder 0.6-1.5 band (ROUTE-21) is same_day. Vomiting never escalates. Evaluator: DMV-86 / J03a type 1, glucose 22, vomiting, bohb 2.4 -> ROUTE-22 urgent and DM-ACT-REFER-GLU-02 same_day 'Glucose 18 or more WITHOUT ketoacidosis'; nothing higher. ketgrid: known type 2, vomiting, bohb 2.0 or 2.9 -> ROUTE-22 urgent only; bohb 1.5 -> same_day. DMV-86 asserts 'urgent'.
findings.why: Any queue or worklist ordered by urgency puts the sicker patient behind the less sick one. ROUTE-23's own reference, REF-DM-ACU-SICKDAY-INSULIN, says 'seek urgent advice if ketones persist or the person is vomiting'; a vomiting person on insulin with bohb 2.4 is one step from DKA and the only reassuring-sounding text on screen says 'without ketoacidosis'.
findings.reviewerFix: ROUTE-22: urgency at least same_day (matching its 'now' tier); add an arm or companion rule: bohb >= REF-DM-ACU-KETONE-RISK (or urine 1+ in insulin/SGLT2 users) WITH vomiting -> immediate, sourced to REF-DM-ACU-SICKDAY-INSULIN / ISPAD sick-day guidance (CSO signature under D-DM-37). State the urgency order in the pack README. Fix DMV-86's expectation.
findings.done: ROUTE-22 is same day; ROUTE-30 interrupts on ketones 1.6 to 2.9 with vomiting. DMV-86 corrected.

findings.where: 60-acute-route.json DM-ACU-ROUTE-26 (new, J08) and DM-ACU-ROUTE-07 (KNOWN() arm removed); DM-ACU-ROUTE-20 notWhen
findings.finding: Regression from J08. (a) ROUTE-26 reads a blank medicine list as 'not on insulin or a sulfonylurea': its notWhen (ISU) is insufficient, so it does not suppress, and its display asserts the negative. Evaluator A09: known diabetes, medicine list blank, glucose 3.4 -> ROUTE-26 same_day 'not on insulin or a sulfonylurea: recheck today'; before J08 the KNOWN() arm of ROUTE-07 interrupted. (b) Altered consciousness is ignored: A10 known diabetes, list blank, DROWSY, glucose 3.5 -> ROUTE-26 same_day only (ROUTE-20 suppressed because a glucose is recorded); A10b metformin only, COMA, glucose 3.5 -> ROUTE-26 same_day only.
findings.why: Breaches rule 2 (missing data treated as negative) and rule 4. A low glucose with drowsiness or coma is level 3 hypoglycaemia by ADA's definition (altered mental state needing help), an emergency whatever the medicine list.
findings.reviewerFix: ROUTE-26: fire only when glucose_lowering_therapy is recorded and contains none of insulin/sulfonylureas (use '!=' predicates on a recorded list, so a blank list leaves ROUTE-07's immediate arm in force); restore KNOWN() to ROUTE-07 for a blank list. Add an arm to ROUTE-06 or a new immediate rule: any glucose < REF-DM-HYPO-L1 with mental_status drowsy/stupor/coma (ADA level 3 definition, the claim behind REF-DM-HYPO-L1/L2). Vignettes A09, A10, A10b.
findings.done: ROUTE-07 interrupts in known diabetes unless a recorded list excludes insulin and sulfonylureas and the type is recorded as not type 1; ROUTE-26 needs that recorded list; ROUTE-31 interrupts on a glucose below 3.9 with drowsiness. DMV-104, DMV-105.

findings.finding: A child on insulin who is vomiting is never asked for a glucose, and J06's 'keep immediate when nothing is measured' was not done. Evaluator: J06c 12-year-old type 1, abdominal pain, nothing measured -> only ROUTE-23 same_day 'check ketones today'. A14 10-year-old type 1, vomiting, urine ketones neg, NO glucose -> NOTHING (ROUTE-23 cleared by the strip; ROUTE-13 is adult-only; ROUTE-15/18 need deep breathing, drowsiness or dehydration). A15 10-year-old type 1, glucose 25, ketones neg -> NOTHING: PAED-03 silenced by J05, ROUTE-01 cleared, and REFER-GLU-02 (declared ages='any' in k_r4.py) is evaluated adult-only because annotate() overwrites ages with agesOverride or 'adult'.
findings.why: A vomiting child on insulin is at risk of both DKA and hypoglycaemia; the one-minute meter test is the first step in NICE NG18 (measure glucose and ketones when DKA is suspected in a child with known diabetes) and ISPAD sick-day guidance. Referral is permitted under 16 (rule 3), so silence is not a scope constraint.
findings.reviewerFix: Give ROUTE-13 a child arm (or extend ROUTE-23's proposal to glucose AND ketones, tier now for children) that clears only on a glucose recorded; per NICE NG18 rec 1.4 (REF behind ROUTE-04 notes) make it immediate when nothing is measured, as R4 asked. Set REFER-GLU-02 agesOverride 'any' (or add a child arm 'refer to the child's diabetes team today'). Vignettes J06c, A14, A15.
findings.done: ROUTE-32 asks for glucose and ketones now in a sick child with diabetes and no glucose; GLU-02 applies at any age. DMV-106.

findings.finding: Fires on ordinary clinic patients and ignores a normal blood ketone. Evaluator: R1b well type 2 on metformin, HbA1c 6.8, fasting meter 6.5, urine ketones TRACE on the clinic dipstick -> ROUTE-21 same_day 'recheck within 2 hours and contact the diabetes team today'. R1c same patient on an SGLT2 inhibitor -> same. A17 urine trace with bohb 0.3 -> ROUTE-21 still fires, although its note says it 'clears only on ... blood ketones below 0.6'.
findings.why: Trace ketonuria on a fasting morning urine and on SGLT2 inhibitors is common; the combi-strip used for protein and glucose reports it. Rule 9: a same-day 'contact the diabetes team' on a large share of well patients will be dismissed, and with it the real sick-day signal. The blood ketone is the better test; letting the strip override it contradicts the rule's own note.
findings.reviewerFix: Require illness for the urine arm (vomiting, abdominal pain, acute_illness_current) or a glucose >= REF-DM-ACU-KETONE-TEST-GLU; notWhen bohb < REF-DM-ACU-KETONE-LOW. Source: Trend UK / ISPAD bands are sick-day guidance (A9-50, A9-51). Add the well-patient vignette as max_fired.
findings.done: ROUTE-21 (urine) and ROUTE-21B (blood 0.6 to 1.5) need illness or a glucose of 18 or more and stand down on a normal blood ketone. DMV-107.

findings.finding: 'Without ketoacidosis' is claimed but only 'urine below 2+ OR bohb below 3.0' is tested. Evaluator: A18 glucose 20, urine neg, bohb 3.5 -> ROUTE-02 immediate AND GLU-02 same_day 'without ketoacidosis'. A19 glucose 20, urine 1+, deep breathing -> ROUTE-11 immediate AND GLU-02 'without ketoacidosis'. DMV-86 bohb 2.4 + vomiting -> GLU-02 'without ketoacidosis' beside ROUTE-22.
findings.why: Rule 10. A same-day 'no ketoacidosis' message next to an interrupt for ketoacidosis contradicts it, and DKA is a clinical/biochemical diagnosis (pH, bicarbonate) the predicates do not test.
findings.reviewerFix: notWhen ROUTE-02's criterion (any urine 2+ or bohb >= REF-DM-ACU-DKA-BOHB), bohb >= REF-DM-ACU-KETONE-RISK, and SIGNS(); display 'Glucose 18 or more with a ketone result below 2+'.
findings.done: GLU-02 stands down on ketones of 1.6 or more, 2+, any sign, pregnancy or an inpatient; reworded. DMV-108.

findings.where: 60-acute-route.json DM-ACU-ROUTE-29 vs -17 and -28; DM-ACU-ROUTE-25 vs -04 and -15; DM-ACU-ROUTE-01 in children
findings.finding: New rules bring back double interrupts for one event. Evaluator: A04 BP 230/130 + chest pain -> ROUTE-17 immediate AND ROUTE-29 immediate. A05 pregnant 170/115, drowsy -> ROUTE-28 immediate AND ROUTE-29 immediate. A06 15-year-old type 1, Kussmaul, no glucose -> ROUTE-15 immediate AND ROUTE-25 immediate. A06b same with glucose 22 -> ROUTE-04 immediate AND ROUTE-25 immediate, plus ROUTE-01 same_day 'test urine ketones today' for a child already being routed. A01c / A19 -> ROUTE-11 immediate plus ROUTE-21 same_day.
findings.why: Rule 9 and J09's stated principle (one interrupt per event); the clinician receives two interrupts with different wording for one patient.
findings.reviewerFix: ROUTE-29 notWhen ROUTE-17's criterion and ROUTE-28's criterion; ROUTE-25 notWhen ROUTE-04's criterion; ROUTE-15 notWhen ROUTE-25's; ROUTE-01, -21, -22 notWhen any interrupting rule's criterion. Add a build check that no vignette yields two 'immediate' items from the same condition family.
findings.done: ROUTE-29 yields to 17 and 28; ROUTE-15 yields to 25 in known diabetes; ROUTE-25 yields to 04 above 11; ROUTE-01 stands down when an interrupt applies. DMV-109.

findings.finding: J06 removed dm_status from the criterion but the display still reads '... with symptoms of diabetes, a raised glucose, ketones or known diabetes: hospital now' and when.label ends 'known diabetes'; there is no ketone predicate at all. Evaluator: J06a known type 1 child with abdominal pain -> ROUTE-04 not met, contrary to the label.
findings.why: Rule 10. A clinician reading the rule list believes a child with known diabetes and vomiting is interrupted; the pack now gives a same-day ketone test instead (and nothing at all once a strip is negative, K05).
findings.reviewerFix: Relabel to the predicates (symptoms, glucose above 11 or HI), or restore the arms the label names with the escalation R4 proposed.
findings.done: ROUTE-04's label says what it tests.

findings.finding: J18 is partly fixed. ROUTE-29 reads only drowsiness or chest pain/stroke signs; UCG-HTN-03 (the rule's own claim) lists hypertensive encephalopathy (severe headache, confusion, seizures, visual disturbance), pulmonary oedema and acute kidney failure. hypertensive_symptoms, which DM-ACT-REFER-BP-03's display says covers breathlessness, confusion and little urine, still never routes. Evaluator: J18a / DMV-90 known type 2, BP 230/130, hypertensive_symptoms true -> REFER-BP-01 same_day only. A03 185/112 headache -> BP-01 same_day only.
findings.why: The feature the clinician is most likely to tick for pulmonary oedema or encephalopathy is the one that does not interrupt; UCG treats these as emergencies.
findings.reviewerFix: Split hypertensive_symptoms per UCG-HTN-03's list (confusion/seizures/visual disturbance, breathlessness, reduced urine output vs headache alone) and add the organ-damage items to ROUTE-29's atLeast. The urgency without organ damage stays D-DM-39.
findings.done: New finding 'hypertensive_organ_damage' (UCG 4.1.6.1's list) interrupts with BP above 180/110; ordinary headache stays an urgency (D-DM-39). DMV-110.

findings.finding: (a) At 12 weeks the rule says 'assess for pre-eclampsia' and assigns condition pre_eclampsia (A02: 12 weeks, 142/92 -> ROUTE-27 same_day; A02b known chronic hypertension -> same). gestation_weeks is recorded but unused. (b) Postpartum is not covered: A02c 2 weeks postpartum, 165/112, headache, prior GDM -> nothing. (c) The prompt never clears: B03 pregnant 142/92 with urine protein NEG recorded -> ROUTE-27 still 'assess ... today (urine protein)'.
findings.why: UCG-CHTN-01: BP >140/90 before 20 weeks is chronic hypertension; UCG-PE-04: pre-eclampsia is usually diagnosed after 20 weeks and can present 4-6 weeks postpartum. Mislabelling at 12 weeks is rule 10; missing postpartum severe hypertension is a recognised maternal-death pathway in a woman the pack is already following (DM-SUS-PREG-02).
findings.reviewerFix: Label by gestation (chronic hypertension in pregnancy below 20 weeks, still referred for specialised antenatal care; pre-eclampsia assessment from 20 weeks) using gestation_weeks and UCG-CHTN-01/PE-04. Add a postpartum arm on postpartum_weeks within UCG-PE-04's window for the severe threshold. ROUTE-27: once urine_protein_strip is recorded, change to the result (refer if 1+ or more, UCG-PE-01/03) rather than repeating the test request.
findings.done: ROUTE-27/28 cover 6 weeks postpartum (UCG-PE-04), name chronic hypertension before 20 weeks, and ROUTE-27 clears on a negative urine. DMV-111.

findings.finding: No pregnancy stop: A16 pregnant 26 weeks, fasting meter 6.3 -> INCID-04 routine 'repeat fasting on another day, and offer a 2-hour OGTT' beside DM-CON-PREG-04 urgent 'send a laboratory glucose'. INCID-01 and INCID-03 both carry notWhen pregnant; INCID-04 does not.
findings.why: In pregnancy a fasting value of 6.3 is in the WHO 2013 gestational range; 'repeat on another day' contradicts the pregnancy rule and could delay care.
findings.reviewerFix: Add notWhen pregnant (as INCID-03's sus_fmeter_preg).
findings.done: INCID-04 stands down in pregnancy.

findings.where: 40-stratify.json targets tgt_hba1c_relaxed, tgt_hba1c_general, tgt_hba1c_older_healthy (J12); vignette DMV-96
findings.finding: J12 is partly fixed. (a) With a relaxed tier agreed, no HbA1c target is proposed at all: J12a / DMV-96 tier relaxed, HbA1c 7.6 -> targets fpg/ppg/bp only; R4 asked for tgt_hba1c_relaxed to apply when tier == relaxed, and DMV-96 asserts only the absences, locking in the gap. (b) With no tier recorded an older adult still gets two HbA1c targets: J12c 72-year-old, HbA1c 7.3 -> tgt_hba1c_general AND tgt_hba1c_older_healthy; J10b and DMV-100 the same.
findings.why: The agreed target is the one thing the clinician needs on screen; two different numbers side by side is the contradiction R4 reported.
findings.reviewerFix: Add 'glycaemic_target_tier == relaxed' as an arm of tgt_hba1c_relaxed's when; when no tier is recorded, show older-healthy as an alternative to the general target (one target), per R4 J12. DMV-96: expect tgt_hba1c_relaxed.
findings.done: An agreed relaxed tier proposes the relaxed target; from 65 only the older-adult target is proposed. DMV-96 corrected; DMV-112.

findings.finding: The J11 fix reads an HbA1c the pack has declared invalid and states a conclusion from it. Evaluator: B01 80-year-old, frail, gliclazide, recent transfusion (caveat hba1c_red_cell_turnover), HbA1c 6.4, fasting plasma 14 -> RX-11 fires 'HbA1c below 7.0%: likely overtreated'. B01b eGFR 22, HbA1c 6.4, meter 16 -> same.
findings.why: These caveats make HbA1c falsely low; the display tells the clinician the patient is overtreated while the glucose says otherwise (rule 10). R4 offered the safer alternative: an arm stating the HbA1c is not valid, with a gap.
findings.reviewerFix: Drop the blanket exemption; give RX-11 an arm for 'HbA1c blocked by a caveat' whose display says the HbA1c cannot be used and asks for glucose or hypoglycaemia history (needsBeforeActing), and keep the existing arm on a valid HbA1c only.
findings.done: RX-11 no longer reads an invalid HbA1c; it shows the HbA1c as a named gap instead. DMV-95 corrected.

findings.finding: Fires on gestational diabetes. Evaluator: R3 routine pregnant woman with GDM on diet (dm_status known, dm_type_recorded gestational, fasting meter 5.0) -> SCREEN-PREG-01 same_day 'Pregnant with PRE-EXISTING diabetes: retinal and kidney assessment now'. The criterion is only dm_status known & pregnant.
findings.why: Rule 10 and rule 9: the mandated routine GDM visit gets a same-day referral for an eye and kidney work-up that applies to pre-existing diabetes (WHO 2025 recs cited by the step), not GDM.
findings.reviewerFix: Add notWhen dm_type_recorded == gestational (or require dm_type_recorded in type_1/type_2/other).
findings.done: SCREEN-PREG-01 stands down for gestational diabetes. DMV-113.

findings.where: k_r4.py RECORDED_RULE (J19); catalog 10-suspect.json and 60-acute-route.json ('op': 'recorded', 52 uses); clerking-v2/00-engine-changes.json
findings.finding: J19 is not fixed. The definition 'recorded means at this encounter' is a Python string that nothing reads or emits: grep finds it only in k_r4.py and the review logs; no catalog file, Design B manifest, README or engine-change entry carries it, and the engine-change spec still lists '{panel, recorded}' with no time scope.
findings.why: Every 'already recorded' stop (SYMP-01/02 after J02, ROUTE-01/03/13/15/18/19/20/23, PAED-01) can be satisfied by an old value, silencing the coma, ketone and symptom prompts.
findings.reviewerFix: Emit the definition into the catalog grammar (00-capabilities-sections.json or the README) and as an EC entry in 00-engine-changes.json with the window decided under D-DM-08; add a vignette field for value age so the evaluator can test it.
findings.done: 'Recorded at this encounter' is emitted in catalog/00 (semantics) and on the engine changes that use it.

findings.finding: J20 is partly fixed. neutralProposal exists only in the pack's x for DM-ACT-SCREEN-TB-01 and DM-ACT-EDU-08; the Design B manifest the engine consumes still carries proposal test 'tb_assessment' and topic 'pregnancy_planning' (grep: 2 hits, 0 neutralProposal), because designb_rules copies x.proposal only. No build check scans proposal strings; the README does not state which fields a patient-facing surface may show.
findings.why: Rule 7: the restricted class rides into the engine's proposal code unchanged.
findings.reviewerFix: Export neutralProposal in designb_rules; extend annotate()'s leak check to proposal values; add the patient-visible-fields statement to the README.
findings.done: neutralProposal is exported to the Design B manifest; the build fails on a restricted proposal with no neutral code; the semantics block says which fields a patient may see.

findings.finding: Display 'Ketones now in a person with diabetes' but the criterion no longer tests diabetes. Evaluator (ketgrid): no diabetes, glucose 14, urine 3+ -> T1-01 same_day.
findings.why: Rule 10.
findings.reviewerFix: Display 'Ketones 2+ with a glucose of 11.1 or more: treat as insulin-deficient until shown otherwise'.
findings.done: T1-01's display no longer says 'in a person with diabetes'.

findings.finding: Switched on (enabled True, enabledBy D-DM-38) while D-DM-38 is unsigned; every other decision-gated item is dark until signed. Evaluator: DMV-97 fires.
findings.why: Governance consistency.
findings.reviewerFix: Leave it on only if the CSO accepts D-DM-38 at signature; otherwise dark like the rest.
findings.done: GLU-02 is dark until D-DM-38 is signed. DMV-97 now expects it dark.

findings.finding: Dehydration arm interrupts 'suspected ketoacidosis' with ketones measured normal. Evaluator B02: child type 1 with diarrhoea, dehydrated, glucose 7, bohb 0.2 -> ROUTE-25 immediate.
findings.why: Rule 9; the J06 complaint in a new form.
findings.reviewerFix: notWhen bohb < REF-DM-ACU-KETONE-LOW and glucose recorded below REF-DM-ACU-PAED-GLU for the dehydration-only arm (same_day instead).
findings.done: Dehydration in a child with diabetes is a sign (N13); a normal ketone does not exclude a falling glucose or sepsis.

findings.finding: 'Never stop insulin' is management advice shown for children (ageBands None). Evaluator: J06c 12-year-old -> ROUTE-23 fires with that text.
findings.why: Letter of rule 3 (under 16: recognition and referral only).
findings.reviewerFix: For child bands, display the referral/test only; keep the sick-day sentence for adults.
findings.done: 'Never stop insulin' moved from ROUTE-23's display to its note.

findings.finding: Acetone on the breath alone interrupts at a normal glucose. Evaluator B10: type 2 on metformin, acetone breath, glucose 8 -> ROUTE-24 immediate 'suspected ketoacidosis'.
findings.why: A subjective, often unreliable sign; rule 9.
findings.reviewerFix: Immediate on deep rapid breathing; acetone breath alone -> same_day ketone test (CSO, D-DM-37).
findings.done: Acetone on the breath is a sign that justifies an interrupt (N13).

findings.finding: DMV-92 is a 10-year-old banded 'adolescent'; DMV-98 is titled 'with gestational diabetes' but records no glucose.
findings.why: Vignettes should test what they say.
findings.reviewerFix: Band DMV-92 'child'; add the GDM glucose to DMV-98 or retitle.
findings.done: DMV-92 is banded 'child'; DMV-98 retitled.

findings.finding: The 'child' band is treated as never pregnant; the pack does not state the band's upper age (none found in tools/build), so whether girls of 10-12 fall in it was not verifiable.
findings.why: Adolescent pregnancy is common in Uganda; the exemption must stop below menarche.
findings.reviewerFix: State the child band's upper age beside preg_state (D-DM-32 source).
findings.done: The 'child' bands are stated in the semantics block.

findings.finding: Duplicate same-day referrals: B07 pregnant, meter 19, ketones neg -> CON-PREG-03 and GLU-02; B06 inpatient on steroids, 19 -> GLU-02 'WHO PEN refers all such patients to hospital' for a person already in hospital.
findings.why: Rule 9 noise.
findings.reviewerFix: GLU-02 notWhen pregnant and notWhen care_setting == inpatient.
findings.done: GLU-02 stands down in pregnancy and for inpatients.

findings.where: 60-acute-route.json DM-ACU-ROUTE-21 and DM-ACU-ROUTE-21B (K06 rewrite); DM-ACU-ROUTE-19, -01 stop conditions
findings.finding: Regression from K06. The rewrite dropped 'any glucose 11.1 or more / HI' from ROUTE-21's diabetes context (ROUTE-21B was built the same way), while ROUTE-19 ('raised glucose with vomiting: test ketones') and ROUTE-01 still stand down as soon as any ketone result exists. A person not yet known to have diabetes, with a high glucose, vomiting and intermediate ketones, now reaches nothing. Evaluator: L-A1 new adult, district, meter 28, vomiting, urine ketones 1+ -> only DM-SUS-INCID-01 routine ('repeat on another day'), caveat urine_ketones_low_despite_picture; before the K fixes (base_r4) -> ROUTE-21 same_day + REFER-GLU-02 same_day. Grid: adult, no diabetes info, vomiting, glucose 15 or 28 x urine trace / 1+ / bohb 1.0 -> 6 of 6 cells silent (all fired same_day before K06).
findings.why: New-onset ketosis-prone diabetes and type 1 presenting in adulthood are common in Uganda; vomiting with ketonuria and a glucose of 28 is the early DKA picture. Rule 4 and rule 8: the only text on screen tells the clinician to repeat the test another day. ROUTE-02/22/30 already accept a raised glucose as diabetes context; 21/21B are the odd ones out.
findings.reviewerFix: Give ROUTE-21 and ROUTE-21B the same context list as ROUTE-02/22/30 (DM_CONTEXT: known, type 1, insulin, sulfonylurea, SGLT2, HI, or glucose >= REF-DM-ACU-DKA-GLU). Add vignette L-A1 (expect ROUTE-21 same_day). Add the build check R5 asked for under K01: every stop condition that names another rule must imply that rule's criterion for the same patient (it would have caught this and L02).
findings.done: ROUTE-21/21B/22/30/02 read one context (diabetes, a raised glucose or HI). Enforced by the grid check.

findings.where: 60-acute-route.json DM-ACU-ROUTE-01 notWhen acu_glu18_signs (K08) vs DM-ACU-ROUTE-04 / -25 sign lists
findings.finding: Regression from K08. ROUTE-01 ('glucose 18 or more: test ketones today') now stands down on deep breathing, ACETONE BREATH, dehydration or drowsiness because 'an interrupting rule applies'. For children no interrupting rule reads acetone: ROUTE-04's list is vomiting, pain, deep breathing, dehydration, drowsiness; ROUTE-25's is deep breathing, dehydration, drowsiness; ROUTE-24 (which reads acetone) is adult-only. Evaluator: L-C12 8-year-old, known type 1 on insulin, meter 20, acetone on the breath -> NOTHING (base_r4: ROUTE-01 same_day). L-C12b 8-year-old, no diabetes info, meter 20, acetone -> PAED-03 same_day only (base_r4: + ROUTE-01).
findings.why: Ketotic breath with a glucose of 20 in a child with type 1 is ketoacidosis until shown otherwise (NICE NG18 lists it among DKA features). The K08 stop silenced the one prompt that was left. Rule 4.
findings.reviewerFix: Add acetone_breath to ROUTE-04's and ROUTE-25's sign lists (NICE NG18, the source behind REF-DM-ACU-PAED-DKA), or limit ROUTE-01's stop to the signs that an interrupt for the same age band actually reads. Vignette L-C12.
findings.done: Acetone interrupts in children (ROUTE-04, ROUTE-25). DMV-114.

findings.finding: Severe pre-eclampsia below 160/110 is never routed, and a negative strip silences it. UCG-PE-02 (the pack's own research row) defines severe pre-eclampsia as 160/110 with proteinuria 'OR any degree of hypertension with evidence of organ dysfunction'; UCG-HTN-03 lists eclampsia/pre-eclampsia as a hypertensive emergency. The new hypertensive_organ_damage finding (K10) is read only by ROUTE-29, which needs >180/110 and is now stopped by 'pregnant' (K08); ROUTE-28 reads BP only; ROUTE-27 is cleared by a negative urine protein (K11). Evaluator: L-B5 pregnant 34 weeks, 150/100, hypertensive_organ_damage (seizures / visual loss / confusion) -> ROUTE-27 same_day 'urine protein today'. L-B7 same with urine protein neg -> NOTHING. L-B5x 34 weeks, 150/100, drowsy -> ROUTE-27 same_day only.
findings.why: Seizures, visual loss or a falling conscious level in a hypertensive pregnant woman is eclampsia or imminent eclampsia: a maternal-death emergency at any BP above 140/90. Rule 4; the source the pack cites says so.
findings.reviewerFix: Add an immediate arm to ROUTE-28 (or a new rule): pregnant or within REF-DM-PREG-PE-POSTPARTUM weeks postpartum, BP >= REF-DM-PREG-BP-SBP/DBP, with hypertensive_organ_damage or mental_status drowsy or worse, sourced to UCG-PE-02 and UCG-HTN-03. ROUTE-27's 'protein negative' stop must not apply when organ damage or drowsiness is recorded. Vignettes L-B5, L-B7, L-B5x.
findings.done: ROUTE-28B (organ damage) and ROUTE-28C (drowsy with 140/90) interrupt in pregnancy and 6 weeks postpartum (UCG-PE-02). DMV-115.

findings.finding: The rules still disagree on who 'has diabetes'. K01 made type 1 recorded, insulin and SGLT2 count as diabetes in ROUTE-02/22/24/30 and K05 built ROUTE-32 on known/type 1/insulin, but ROUTE-25 (child, signs) reads only dm_status == known and ROUTE-20 (drowsy, no glucose) reads known/insulin/SU. Evaluator: L-C1 8-year-old, insulin on the list, status blank, deep rapid breathing, glucose 7 -> NOTHING. L-C2 8-year-old, type 1 recorded, status blank, drowsy, glucose 7 -> ROUTE-09 same_day only. Grid: child and adolescent, insulin-listed or type-1-recorded with status blank, Kussmaul, glucose 7, any ketone below 3.0 -> 28 cells with no interrupt (12 with nothing at all). Adult type 1 recorded, status blank, drowsy, no glucose -> ROUTE-09 same_day (7 cells); L-S3 SGLT2 listed, status blank, drowsy, no glucose -> nothing.
findings.why: A child on insulin with Kussmaul breathing has ketoacidosis until shown otherwise whatever the glucose (NICE NG18: in known diabetes suspect DKA even with a normal glucose; partially treated DKA). Relatives often bring the insulin pen while the status box stays blank. Rule 4.
findings.reviewerFix: Define one diabetes-context list in k_review (known, type 1 recorded, insulin, sulfonylurea, SGLT2 inhibitor) and use it in ROUTE-13, -20, -23, -25, -32 and ROUTE-07's context, as K01 did for 02/22/24/30. Vignettes L-C1, L-C2, L-S3.
findings.done: One 'has diabetes' list (DM_ANY) used by every acute rule. DMV-116.

findings.finding: Inverse escalation: the sicker insulin or SGLT2 user gets less. ROUTE-23 ('on insulin, vomiting: ketones today') stands down on dehydration or drowsiness because 'an interrupting rule applies', but below a glucose of 11.1 no interrupt reads either sign (ROUTE-11 needs 11.1; ROUTE-24 reads only deep breathing and acetone). ROUTE-03 (SGLT2) reads vomiting, pain, deep breathing and acute illness, but not drowsiness or dehydration. Evaluator: L-A6 type 1 on insulin, vomiting, glucose 7 -> ROUTE-23 same_day; L-A4 same + dehydrated -> NOTHING; L-A5 same + drowsy -> NOTHING (identical before the K fixes). L-S1 type 2 on an SGLT2 inhibitor, drowsy, glucose 8 -> NOTHING (only routine steps).
findings.why: Drowsiness and dehydration are late features of ketoacidosis; at a near-normal glucose they are exactly the euglycaemic and partly treated DKA the pack's notes describe (2024 hyperglycaemic-crises consensus behind REF-DM-ACU-DKA-BOHB: prior diabetes qualifies at any glucose). Rule 4.
findings.reviewerFix: ROUTE-23's sign stop: deep breathing and acetone only (what ROUTE-24 reads). Add dehydration and drowsiness to ROUTE-24's sign list for insulin/SGLT2/type 1 users at any glucose (or a new interrupt 'glucose below 11.1 with these signs: ketones now'), and add dehydration and drowsiness to ROUTE-03's 'any', sourced to the consensus and REF-DM-ACU-SICKDAY-INSULIN; CSO signature under D-DM-37. Vignettes L-A4, L-A5, L-S1.
findings.done: ROUTE-24 and ROUTE-03 interrupt on dehydration or drowsiness; ROUTE-23 no longer stands down on them. DMV-117.

findings.where: 60-acute-route.json DM-ACU-ROUTE-23 notWhen acu_insulin_sick_done, DM-ACU-ROUTE-32 notWhen acu_paed_known_sick_done
findings.finding: K02's principle (a urine strip never stands down a ketone prompt) was applied to the SGLT2 rule only. A vomiting child on insulin with a normal glucose and one negative strip reaches nothing. Evaluator: L-C4 8-year-old type 1 on insulin, vomiting, glucose 7, urine ketones neg -> only caveat urine_ketones_low_despite_picture; L-C4b without the strip -> ROUTE-23 same_day.
findings.why: REF-DM-VAL-URINE-KETONE (strips underestimate early) applies to insulin deficiency as much as to SGLT2. ISPAD sick-day guidance: a vomiting child with diabetes needs blood ketones and contact with the diabetes team. Referral is in scope under rule 3.
findings.reviewerFix: ROUTE-23: clear on bohb < REF-DM-ACU-KETONE-LOW only (as K02 did for ROUTE-03); with a urine result only, keep it (same_day). Vignette L-C4.
findings.done: For type 1 and insulin (ROUTE-23) and SGLT2 (ROUTE-03) only a blood ketone clears the prompt. WHO PEN's glucose-18 strip test (ROUTE-01/08/19) still clears on a negative strip, as the source says.

findings.finding: The K fixes added 290 double-interrupt cells to the grid (1,155 cells with two or more 'immediate' items; 865 existed before; up to 5 immediates in one cell). New pairs and their cause: ROUTE-03 with 24/11/14/30/25/04/32 (K02 narrowed 03's stop to rule 02 only; K01 put SGLT2 in 24) - L-S2 SGLT2, Kussmaul, glucose 8 -> 03 + 24; K02d SGLT2, vomiting, bohb 2.0 -> 03 + 30. ROUTE-30 with 04/32/07/14 (no stops) - child type 1, vomiting, glucose 14, bohb 2.0 -> 04 + 30. ROUTE-31 with 07: A10 / L-H1 known diabetes, blank list, drowsy, 3.5 -> 07 + 31, because 31's stop is labelled 'or known diabetes without a medicine list that excludes them' but does not test dm_status (rule 10 too). ROUTE-28 + 29: L-B4 3 weeks postpartum, 200/120, organ damage -> both (29's K08 stop reads 'pregnant' only; K11 extended 28 to postpartum). ROUTE-32 with 02/14/04. Pre-existing pairs still present: 02+04 (96 cells), 04+14 (child HI), 20+25 and 07+25 (70 each), 02+14.
findings.why: Rule 9 and the pack's own 'one interrupt per event' principle (J09, K08).
findings.reviewerFix: ROUTE-03 notWhen the criteria of 11, 14, 24, 30 (and 04/25/32 for children); ROUTE-30 notWhen 04, 25, 32; ROUTE-31's r07 stop: add KNOWN() so it matches its label; ROUTE-29 notWhen postpartum_weeks <= REF-DM-PREG-PE-POSTPARTUM; ROUTE-32 notWhen ketones 2+ / bohb >= 3.0. Turn the grid (phase-1/r6/grid.py) into a build check: no cell may carry two 'immediate' items from the same condition family.
findings.done: One interrupt per event, folded by ACUTE_ORDER in the evaluator; the build fails on two displayed interrupts anywhere in the grid.

findings.finding: A meter reading of HI or LO is not 'a glucose on record': GLU_REC lists the numeric fields only. Rules then say 'no glucose on record: capillary glucose now' right after the meter has read HI or LO. Evaluator: L-C11 14-year-old type 1, vomiting, meter HI -> ROUTE-04, -14 and -32 immediate ('no glucose on record'), plus ROUTE-01 and -23 same_day (five items). Adult on insulin, drowsy, meter LO -> ROUTE-06 + ROUTE-20 'no glucose on record: capillary glucose now'. Adult type 2, vomiting, meter HI -> ROUTE-13 'no glucose on record' + ROUTE-14. ROUTE-32 (new, K05) inherits it.
findings.why: Rule 10 (the display contradicts the record) and rule 9; at a meter-only site HI/LO is the reading.
findings.reviewerFix: Add P('glucose_meter_extreme','recorded') to GLU_REC. Vignette L-C11 (expect one interrupt).
findings.done: A meter HI or LO counts as a glucose on record in every stop condition.

findings.where: 40-stratify.json tgt_hba1c_general notWhen tgt_general_older (K13); tgt_hba1c_older_healthy notWhen tier_not_any
findings.finding: Regression from K13: an older adult whose clinician has agreed the GENERAL tier gets no HbA1c target at all. tgt_hba1c_general now stands down at 65 or over, and the older-adult target stands down whenever any tier is agreed. Evaluator: 72-year-old type 2, tier 'general', HbA1c 7.3 -> targets fpg/ppg/bp only (base_r4: tgt_hba1c_general). Also (pre-existing): tier 'tight' or 'avoid_symptoms' -> no HbA1c target at any age.
findings.why: The agreed target is the one the clinician needs on screen (R5 K13's own reason); the agreed tier now erases it.

Grid7b: 722 cells where a pregnancy-unknown interrupt is shown over a folded measured emergency (02, 14, 17, 11, 24, 29, 30, 03).

Naming eclampsia in a 48-year-old with a hyperosmolar state or a stroke sends her down the wrong pathway (obstetric triage, magnesium) while the time-critical one is a folded line. The display claims a fact (pregnant) the record does not hold: rule 10.

Add an order invariant to the build: no pregnancy-unknown interrupt above a measured emergency. Vignettes O1, O2, O6.
findings.done: A rule met only through unknown pregnancy ranks after every rule met on recorded facts, and is worded as a question. Build invariant. DMV-124.

findings.where: build.py designb_rules (line 574: appliesTo.pregnancy = 'pregnant' if any predicate reads 'pregnant'); designb/pack-manifest.draft.json rows DM-ACU-ROUTE-27, 27B, 27C, 28, 28B, 28C
findings.finding: The Design B manifest declares appliesTo {pregnancy: 'pregnant'} for all six pregnancy BP rules, and carries no pregnancyUnknownCounts flag (0 occurrences). The catalog criteria have a postpartum arm (pregnant OR postpartum_weeks <= 6) and rely on pregnancyUnknownCounts for the unanswered case. Observed: manifest row DM-ACU-ROUTE-28B 'appliesTo': {'ageBands': None, 'pregnancy': 'pregnant'}; same for 27, 27B, 27C, 28, 28C; the catalog 60-acute-route.json entries carry pregnancyUnknownCounts: true and no appliesTo.
findings.why: appliesTo.pregnancy is the field an engine uses to decide whether a rule runs (it withholds not_pregnant items today). An engine honouring the manifest will not run these rules for a postpartum woman (pregnant=false, postpartum 2 weeks) or for a woman whose pregnancy is unanswered, which undoes L03, L13 and L15 in the artefact Phase 2 deploys; the reference evaluator never reads rule appliesTo, so the build cannot see it.
findings.reviewerFix: Derive appliesTo from the criterion: a rule with a postpartum arm is 'any' (or a new value 'pregnant_or_postpartum'); emit pregnancyUnknownCounts in the manifest row; add a build assertion that each manifest row's appliesTo admits every vignette on which the catalog rule fires (DMV-111, DMV-119 would fail today).
findings.done: The manifest derives appliesTo from the criterion (postpartum and unknown arms → 'any'), and carries pregnancyUnknownCounts, unknownDisplay and interruptRank.

findings.where: 60-acute-route.json DM-ACU-ROUTE-28C (and missing rule); DM-ACU-ROUTE-15 ageBands child/adolescent only

findings.finding: 27B tells the clinician 'gestational or chronic hypertension. Review the blood-pressure plan today and aim below 140/90' whenever the strip is negative or trace, whatever else is recorded. A negative strip does not exclude pre-eclampsia (UCG-PE-02: 'any degree of hypertension with evidence of organ dysfunction'). Labelling her 'gestational hypertension, review the plan' is rule 10 and could delay referral of imminent eclampsia.

Add a rule: pregnant or postpartum (unknown counts), BP >= REF-DM-PREG-BP-SBP/DBP, hypertensive_symptoms present -> refer to hospital today (UCG-CHTN-03), or interrupt if the CSO reads UCG 2023 16.3.7's symptom list that way; quote that list into the research table first. findings.finding: The dehydration and acetone arms interrupt for any diabetes, including metformin-only or diet-only, and do not stand down on a normal blood ketone.
