findings.where: build.py pregnancyUnknownCounts on DM-ACU-ROUTE-27 and -28; DMV-119
findings.finding: Every woman whose pregnancy is unrecorded gets a pregnancy BP action. Evaluator: O5 woman 45, known type 2, 145/92, routine visit -> ROUTE-27 same_day 'urine protein today'; O4 same at 165/100, no symptoms -> ROUTE-28 immediate 'Pregnant ... acute severe hypertension. Route now'; DMV-119 asserts the interrupt for 170/115. A man with the same readings gets nothing acute (165/100) or a same-day referral (above 200/110).
findings.why: Hypertension is common in women attending a diabetes clinic, and the pregnancy question is often not asked at routine visits; the result is a same-day order on most hypertensive women and interrupts on many (rule 9). The question that resolves it takes seconds.
findings.reviewerFix: When the rule fires only through unknown pregnancy, issue one prompt 'Pregnancy not recorded: ask now' (urgency of the underlying rule only once the answer is yes), and put the choice to the CSO under D-DM-36. Vignettes O4, O5.
findings.done: Same-day pregnancy BP rules wait for the pregnancy answer; only the interrupts treat it as possible.

findings.where: 40-stratify.json tgt_hba1c_tight (k_r6.py: notWhen [], label 'good health, low risk of lows')
findings.finding: The tight target copies none of the general target's stops. Evaluator: tier 'tight', glibenclamide, a low needing help in the last year, HbA1c 6.9 -> targets include tgt_hba1c_tight (below 6.5%) while DM-ACT-RX-10 fires 'relax the target for now' and the hypoglycaemia flags fire; without the tier the same patient gets tgt_hba1c_relaxed. Tier 'tight' with eGFR 40 -> tgt_hba1c_tight and tgt_hba1c_ckd (6.5 to 8.0) together.
findings.why: REF-DM-CTRL-HBA1C-TIGHT's own quote (ADA Rec 6.4) limits the lower goal to people with 'low treatment risks (e.g., hypoglycemia)'; the label promises that and the predicates do not test it (rule 10). A 6.5% goal beside a recent severe low on a sulfonylurea points toward more treatment.
findings.reviewerFix: Give tgt_hba1c_tight the same relaxed-reason stop as tgt_hba1c_general (frailty, cognitive impairment, hypo_worst_12m, hypo_awareness_score), so the relaxed target supersedes; decide whether tight supersedes tgt_hba1c_ckd. Vignette: tight + needed-help low -> tgt_hba1c_relaxed.
findings.done: The tight target stands down on any reason to relax and on insulin or a sulfonylurea (ADA Rec 6.4).

findings.where: 60-acute-route.json DM-ACU-ROUTE-23 (display, proposal test.ketones) at district sites
findings.finding: At a district site (no lab.ketones_blood) ROUTE-23 asks for 'blood ketones today', and only a blood ketone clears it. Evaluator: L-C4 8-year-old type 1, vomiting, glucose 7, urine ketones negative, district -> ROUTE-23 same_day; C1 abdominal pain, glucose 6, district -> same. No referral or contact instruction is given.
findings.why: Rule 8: the district clinician gets a test they cannot do and no reachable next step.
findings.reviewerFix: Site-aware display or a second arm: where blood ketones are unavailable, 'contact the diabetes team today / refer today to a site that can measure blood ketones' (ISPAD sick-day guidance, the source already in ROUTE-23's notes).
findings.done: ROUTE-23 runs where blood ketones exist; ROUTE-23D is the district strip pathway with a repeat. DMV-129.

findings.finding: 28B never tests blood pressure, though its label says 'beside a raised pressure' and its display 'severe pre-eclampsia'. Evaluator: pregnant 30 weeks, organ-damage box ticked, BP 118/76 -> ROUTE-28B immediate 'severe pre-eclampsia'; woman 44, known type 2, pregnancy blank, organ-damage box, BP 118/76 -> ROUTE-28B immediate with the gap 'pregnant'.
findings.why: UCG-PE-02 requires 'any degree of hypertension'; a normotensive woman with pulmonary oedema or confusion needs routing, but not under that name (rule 10). The organ-damage box is also used outside pregnancy.
findings.reviewerFix: Add BP >= REF-DM-PREG-BP-SBP or DBP to 28B; with BP not recorded, fire and name 'bp_systolic' as the gap (seizures in pregnancy must not wait for a cuff).
findings.done: 28B needs 140/90 or more beside the organ-damage signs.

findings.finding: ROUTE-34 fires when ketones were never measured and says 'with ketones below the danger range: tablets cannot be kept down'. Evaluator: type 2, vomiting, glucose 28, no ketone result -> ROUTE-34 same_day beside ROUTE-01 and -19; adult type 1 on insulin, vomiting, glucose 24, urine negative -> ROUTE-23 + ROUTE-34 'tablets'; L-C11 14-year-old type 1 on insulin -> ROUTE-34 'tablets' under the ROUTE-04 interrupt; SGLT2, vomiting, glucose 35, no ketones -> ROUTE-34 beside ROUTE-01, -19 and the interrupt.
findings.why: A missing ketone result is shown as a reassuring one (rule 2, rule 10); 'tablets' is wrong for insulin users and children. Harm is limited because ROUTE-01/19 ask for ketones in the same output.
findings.reviewerFix: Require a ketone result in ROUTE-34's criterion (urine neg/trace/1+ or a blood ketone below REF-DM-ACU-KETONE-LOW), and word the display by therapy ('oral medicines or insulin plan cannot be kept to'). Stand it down under any interrupt.
findings.done: ROUTE-34's display no longer asserts ketones or tablets.

findings.where: k_grid.floor rows for vomiting with a high glucose; DM-ACU-ROUTE-34 scope (vomiting only)
findings.finding: The floor treats type 1 and type 2 the same when vomiting with a high glucose: same_day. Evaluator: adult type 1 on insulin, vomiting, glucose 24, urine negative -> same_day only (23, 34); C2 child type 1, vomiting, glucose 25, urine negative, district -> ROUTE-04 interrupt (children are covered). G4 75-year-old type 2, glucose 30, ketones negative, acutely ill (no vomiting, no dehydration ticked) -> nothing acute (GLU-02 dark).
findings.why: Vomiting in type 1 on insulin is the sick-day red flag in ISPAD 2022 and the JBDS sick-day guidance, and urine strips under-read early ketonaemia (REF-DM-VAL-URINE-KETONE). ROUTE-34's own rationale ('the hyperosmolar state can develop without ketones', independent of D-DM-38) applies equally to an older adult with an infection; reading vomiting only is narrower than the reason given.
findings.reviewerFix: Put two rows to the CSO under D-DM-41: type 1 or insulin, vomiting, glucose >= REF-DM-ACU-KETONE-TEST-GLU, no blood ketone -> immediate or hospital today per ISPAD 2022 / JBDS sick-day text (quote it into the research table first); and extend ROUTE-34's 'any' to acute_illness_current for older adults, sourced to the JBDS HHS guideline.
findings.done: ROUTE-34B covers acute illness with glucose 18 or more. Whether vomiting on insulin with a negative strip should interrupt is D-DM-42.

findings.finding: Pregnancy does not change any ketone rule. Evaluator: P11 pregnant with type 1, vomiting, glucose 9, blood ketones 1.0 -> ROUTE-21B same_day 'recheck within 2 hours'; P11c pregnant with type 1, abdominal pain, glucose 9, blood ketones 2.0 -> ROUTE-22 same_day.
findings.why: Ketoacidosis in pregnancy develops faster and at lower glucose, and threatens the fetus; the pack has no source on it.
findings.reviewerFix: Add the JBDS-IP guideline on DKA in pregnancy (2017) and the relevant UCG 2023 chapter 16 text to the research table, and let the CSO decide whether pregnancy raises 21B/22 to same-day-with-obstetrics or immediate. No threshold from memory.
findings.done: Pregnancy-specific ketone routing needs JBDS-IP text: D-DM-42.

findings.finding: The interrupt order exists only in build.py/k_r6.py: catalog/00 says 'the first in ACUTE_ORDER' but no file under catalog/, designb/ or clerking-v2/ contains the list or a per-rule rank (grep: 0). The Design B manifest still carries no time scope ('at this encounter': 0; L17), no supersedes, no fold.
findings.why: Phase 2 ports the catalog; it cannot reproduce the fold, so the one-interrupt behaviour that the grid enforces is not shipped.
findings.reviewerFix: Emit x.acuteRank on every immediate rule (and the order list in catalog/00), carry acuteRank, supersedes and recordedScope into the manifest, and assert in the build that the shipped order equals ACUTE_ORDER.
findings.done: acuteOrder, interruptRank, supersedes and the recorded scope are in the semantics block and the manifest.

findings.finding: Display still 'vomiting, in pain or breathing deeply ... even if glucose is normal' after L05 added dehydration and drowsiness; L-S1 (drowsy) and the glucose-35 patient see it.
findings.why: Rule 10.
findings.reviewerFix: Display from the label; drop 'even if glucose is normal' when a glucose >= REF-DM-ACU-DKA-GLU is recorded.
findings.done: ROUTE-03 display.

findings.finding: Still 'capillary glucose and ketones now' when ketones are recorded (L-C10, urine 3+); L22 changed the proposal only.
findings.why: Rule 10.
findings.reviewerFix: Display 'capillary glucose now'.
findings.done: ROUTE-32 display.

findings.finding: Metformin listed, type blank, 3.6 (L-H12) -> 'if the medicines are not known'; the medicines are known, the type is not.
findings.why: Rule 10 (L11c partly fixed).
findings.reviewerFix: Say 'or the type is not recorded'.
findings.done: ROUTE-07 display.

findings.finding: Hypoglycaemic patients at 3.0 to 3.9 still carry a folded 'suspected ketoacidosis. Route now' (L-C3, L-H1, L-A3).
findings.why: L12 partly fixed; misleading reason under the hypo interrupt.
findings.reviewerFix: Stand 24/25 down below REF-DM-HYPO-L1 as R6 proposed.
findings.done: Folded behind the hypoglycaemia interrupt, which heads; the folded reason is kept visible on purpose.

findings.where: acute lane, same-day items under an interrupt
findings.finding: 30,886 of 82,160 grid7 cells show same-day items beside an interrupt (01, 19, 23, 34, 27, DM-ACT-REFER-BP-01): L-C11 has 01, 23, 34 under ROUTE-04; DMV-100/O2 show BP-01 'same-day referral' under the interrupt.
findings.why: 'Today' beside 'now' (L21 partly fixed).
findings.reviewerFix: Fold same-day acute items into the interrupt as well, or stand them down when an interrupt is met.
findings.done: Presentation: same-day items collapse under an interrupt on the surface (Phase 3).

findings.finding: DMV-119: gap 'pregnant' is recorded for ROUTE-27 although ROUTE-27 is suppressed (stops on >=160/110); the gap is appended before notWhen is applied.
findings.why: Gap list overstates.
findings.reviewerFix: Append the gap only when the rule fires.
findings.done: A gap is recorded only when the rule fires.

findings.finding: Still lists 'blurred vision'; UCG-HTN-03 puts visual disturbance (and severe headache) under hypertensive encephalopathy.
findings.why: L10 partly fixed.
findings.reviewerFix: Move visual disturbance to hypertensive_organ_damage, per UCG 2023 4.1.6.1.
findings.done: Blurred vision moved to the organ-damage finding.

findings.finding: No grid row or vignette supplies pregnancy_possible; a 72-year-old woman without it gets ROUTE-28C and every target withheld (O3). The pack does not state the age band the platform must use.
findings.why: Behaviour depends on an unstated platform parameter.
findings.reviewerFix: State the band in catalog/00 (CSO), and give the older-women and adolescent vignettes pregnancy_possible explicitly.
findings.done: The semantics block says pregnancy_possible is the platform's answer (D-DM-36).

findings.finding: Still 'Diabetes (or on insulin or a sulfonylurea)' after the DM_ANY change.
findings.why: Rule 10 drift.
findings.reviewerFix: Display from the label.
findings.done: ROUTE-13 and ROUTE-20 displays.

findings.finding: eGFR 40 -> two HbA1c targets at once (general 7.0 + CKD 6.5-8.0; tight 6.5 + CKD).
findings.why: Two goals for one measure.
findings.reviewerFix: Decide supersedes for the CKD target.
findings.done: The CKD target supersedes the general, tight and older targets.

findings.finding: Q13 regressed. 28B now needs BP >= 140/90 and is insufficient when BP is not recorded, and nothing replaces it. Evaluator: pregnant 30 weeks, hypertensive_organ_damage (seizure/confusion/crackles), alert, BP not recorded -> fired {} (referral and district alike); 2 weeks postpartum, organ damage, BP not recorded -> {}; pregnant 30 weeks, organ damage, BP 120/80 -> {}; pregnant with type 2, organ damage, no BP -> only DM-ACT-SCREEN-PREG-01 same_day. r8/grid8.py: 18 'organ damage, BP not recorded' cells below an interrupt (16 with nothing at all) and 8 'pregnant/postpartum organ damage at 120/80' cells with nothing.
findings.why: R7 Q13's own fix said 'with BP not recorded, fire and name bp_systolic as the gap (seizures in pregnancy must not wait for a cuff)' and that a normotensive woman with pulmonary oedema or confusion 'needs routing, but not under that name'. Before 0.3.4 she was routed; now she is silent. Rule 2 (missing BP read as normal) and rule 4. The women's grid has no organ-damage-without-BP row, so the build cannot see it.
findings.reviewerFix: Treat a missing BP on 28B as possible (same mechanism as pregnancyUnknownCounts) and name bp_systolic as the gap, or add a 28E 'pregnant or within REF-DM-PREG-PE-POSTPARTUM weeks, organ-damage signs, BP not recorded: BP now, route now' ranked with 28B. For organ damage with a measured normal BP, route under a neutral display ('pregnant or recently delivered with seizures, confusion or breathlessness: route now') sourced to UCG 2023 16.3.7 eclampsia text once quoted into the research table. Add organ x {BP none, 120/80} rows to women_floor (immediate).
findings.done: ROUTE-28E routes organ-damage signs in pregnancy or postpartum with no BP recorded. Organ damage is defined beside a raised pressure, so 120/80 is not that finding. Women's grid row. DMV-130.

findings.finding: 28D is an interrupt but was left out of PREG_INTERRUPTS, so it has no pregnancyUnknownCounts. Evaluator: woman 30, pregnancy unanswered, drowsy, capillary glucose 6, BP not recorded -> fired {}; same with pregnant=false and postpartum_weeks blank -> {}. With no glucose recorded ROUTE-15 catches her (P7d -> ROUTE-15), which is why k_grid (no glucose dimension for women) reports 0 silent. Manifest row DM-ACU-ROUTE-28D: pregnancyUnknownCounts false.
findings.why: The Q01/Q05 logic the pack adopted (an unanswered pregnancy or birth question is 'possible' for interrupts) stops at the one interrupt whose job is the drowsy woman with no BP. A drowsy recently delivered woman is eclampsia until a BP says otherwise (UCG-PE-02, UCG-PE-04). Rule 2.
findings.reviewerFix: Add DM-ACU-ROUTE-28D to PREG_INTERRUPTS (pregnancyUnknownCounts, unknownDisplay, ranked last when metViaUnknown). Add a glucose-recorded dimension to the women's grid with floor 'drowsy, BP not recorded -> immediate' for every POSSIBLE pregnancy state.
findings.done: 28D (and 28E, 27D) treat unanswered pregnancy or postpartum as possible. DMV-131.

findings.where: k_r7 ACUTE_ORDER (15 at rank 22, 28D at 23); DMV-126
findings.finding: For a drowsy pregnant woman with neither glucose nor BP, ROUTE-15 heads and 28D is folded. Evaluator: DMV-126 -> interrupt DM-ACU-ROUTE-15 'Deep breathing or drowsiness, with no glucose on record: capillary glucose now'; 28D 'blood pressure and glucose now' folded. DMV-126 asserts only that 28D fires.
findings.why: The R7 Q03 principle the pack accepted: the header is what the team acts on. The header for a drowsy woman at 34 weeks names neither BP nor eclampsia, although 28D already asks for the glucose too.
findings.reviewerFix: Give ROUTE-15 a notWhen 'pregnant or within REF-DM-PREG-PE-POSTPARTUM weeks (rule 28D owns her)', or rank 28D before 15; make DMV-126 assert interrupt == DM-ACU-ROUTE-28D.
findings.done: 28D ranks before 15. DMV-126 corrected by the order.

findings.finding: Q09 removed the acetone/dehydration interrupt for non-insulin diabetes and nothing took its place, and a blank medicine list counts as 'not on insulin'. Evaluator: known type 2, medicine list blank, acetone on the breath, nothing measured -> only DM-ACT-EDU-01/02; type 2 on metformin, acetone, no glucose, no ketones -> {}; same with blood ketones 1.0 -> only the bohb band 'raised'; type 2 on metformin, acetone, glucose 7, urine ketones 1+ -> {}. r8/grid8m.py over the k_grid men: 120 adult acetone cells (ketones not measured-normal, glucose none or 7) with no same-day or immediate item, 40 of them with the medicine list blank.
findings.why: R7 Q09 asked to keep the interrupt for type 1/insulin/SGLT2 AND 'send the rest to ROUTE-13-style same day'; the second half was not done. ROUTE-13 does not read acetone and stands down once any glucose is recorded; ROUTE-21/21B do not read acetone. A blank list may hide insulin (rule 2); ketosis-prone 'type 2' is common in sub-Saharan Africa (the pack's own ketosis_prone_type_2 classification).
findings.reviewerFix: 24B: treat an unrecorded glucose_lowering_therapy as possibly insulin (fire, name the gap), as pregnancyUnknownCounts does for pregnancy. Add acetone_breath to ROUTE-13's any and to the illness arm of ROUTE-21/21B; let ROUTE-13 run with a glucose recorded when no ketone is recorded ('ketones today'). Floor: acetone or dehydration in diabetes with ketones not measured or above REF-DM-ACU-KETONE-LOW -> same_day; blank list + acetone -> immediate.
findings.done: 24B interrupts on acetone or dehydration unless a recorded list excludes insulin and SGLT2 and the type is not type 1; ROUTE-13B asks for ketones the same day in other diabetes. Men's grid rows. DMV-132.

findings.where: 50-act.json therapyFlag metformin_during_acute_illness; acute lane sick-day path; DMV-128
findings.finding: A person with diabetes who is vomiting or dehydrated with a normal glucose and normal ketones gets nothing. Evaluator: DMV-128 (66, metformin, dehydrated, glucose 7, bohb 0.2) -> only EDU-01/02; type 2 on metformin, vomiting, glucose 8 -> only EDU-01/02; child of 8 with type 1 on insulin, dehydrated, glucose 7, bohb 0.2 -> fired {}. metformin_during_acute_illness reads only acute_illness_current; the SGLT2 flag reads vomiting, abdominal pain and dehydration.
findings.why: The metformin flag's own source (ADA: hold 'when the person cannot eat and drink or acute kidney injury is a concern') describes exactly these patients; the flag misses its patient. For the child, ISPAD 2022 ch.13 (REF-DM-ACU-SICKDAY-INSULIN) asks for review when a child on insulin is unwell. DMV-128 asserts only that 24/24B stay silent, so the build is green on a fully silent sick day.
findings.reviewerFix: Extend metformin_during_acute_illness to any[acute_illness_current, vomiting, dehydration] (as sglt2_during_acute_illness). Add a same-day sick-day review for diabetes with vomiting or dehydration when glucose and ketones are recorded and not in a danger range (child with diabetes: same day, ISPAD 2022 ch.13). Make DMV-128 expect the flag.
findings.done: The metformin sick-day flag reads vomiting and dehydration; ROUTE-25C gives a child with normal ketones a same-day review.

findings.where: 40-stratify.json interpretation hba1c_control_general/_relaxed/_tight (when: glycaemic_target_tier); targets tgt_hba1c_tight/_ckd; designb DM-STR-CTRL-01, DM-ACT-TARGET-01 params
findings.finding: Q11 is fixed in the target list but not in the control band, which still reads the agreed tier. Evaluator: tier tight, glibenclamide, low needing help, HbA1c 6.9 -> no HbA1c target shown, DM-ACT-RX-10 'relax the target for now', and band hba1c_control_tight 'above_target'; tier tight, insulin, HbA1c 6.8 -> no HbA1c target, band 'above_target'; tier general, glibenclamide, low needing help, HbA1c 7.3 -> no HbA1c target, RX-10 fires, band hba1c_control_general 'above_target'; tier general, eGFR 45, HbA1c 7.5 -> target tgt_hba1c_ckd (6.5 to 8.0) but band 'above_target'. Written (not evaluated): DM-STR-CTRL-01 carries only general and relaxed params and reports 'against the general target' when no tier is agreed; DM-ACT-TARGET-01 has no tight or CKD param.
findings.why: An 'Above target' label on a person with a recent severe low on a sulfonylurea or insulin points to more treatment, the opposite of RX-10 on the same screen and of the ADA Rec 6.4 limit Q11 cited (REF-DM-CTRL-HBA1C-TIGHT). Rule 10: the band's label is judged against a target the pack has just withdrawn.
findings.reviewerFix: Compute the control band against the target actually proposed after notWhen and supersedes (key the bands to target ids, not to glycaemic_target_tier); when an agreed tier is stood down by a relax reason, band against REF-DM-CTRL-HBA1C-RELAXED; give DM-STR-CTRL-01 and DM-ACT-TARGET-01 the tight, CKD and older params. Vignettes for the four patients.
findings.done: Control bands are read only against the target proposed (forTarget); older and CKD bands added; the general target stands down on insulin or a sulfonylurea with a significant low. DMV-133.

findings.where: 10-suspect.json DM-SUS-INCID-01..04 and DM-SUS-PAED-01/03 (ageBands); confirm lane in children
findings.finding: A child or young adolescent with a diabetes-range glucose below 11.1 or an HbA1c in range gets no recognition or referral. Evaluator: child 12, fasting plasma glucose 8.0 -> fired {}; child 12, HbA1c 7.2 -> {}; adolescent 15, fasting 9.0 with polyuria -> who_hearts_d_2020 'met' and fired {} (PAED-01 stands down once a glucose is recorded; PAED-03 needs above 11; INCID rules are adult-only; newly-met steps are adult-only).
findings.why: Rule 3 allows recognition and referral under 16, and the pack withholds both. ISPAD 2022 uses the same diagnostic thresholds in children; a symptomatic adolescent meeting the criteria needs same-day referral (REF-DM-SUS-PAED-SAMEDAY). Delay in type 1 is the path to DKA.
findings.reviewerFix: Add a child/adolescent rule: diabetes criteria met, or any fasting plasma glucose >= REF-DM-DX-FPG, HbA1c >= REF-DM-DX-HBA1C, or any glucose >= REF-DM-DX-RANDOM -> refer the same day to the paediatric or diabetes team (REF-DM-SUS-PAED-SAMEDAY), whatever the symptoms. Add child bands with fasting 8 / HbA1c 7 to the vignettes.
findings.done: DM-SUS-PAED-04 refers a child with a diabetes-range fasting, 2-hour or HbA1c value the same day. DMV-134.

findings.where: DM-ACU-ROUTE-27/27B/27C/27D (pregnancyUnknownCounts removed by Q10, 27D added without it); women grid
findings.finding: When pregnancy is unanswered, or 'not pregnant' is recorded with the weeks since birth blank, raised BP with pre-eclampsia symptoms produces nothing and nothing asks the question. Evaluator: woman 30, pregnant=false, postpartum blank, 150/100, hypertensive_symptoms -> fired {}; pregnancy unanswered, same -> {}; pregnant=false, postpartum blank, 150/100 -> {}. With postpartum_weeks 2 the same woman gets 27D 'refer to hospital today'. r8/grid8.py: 8 'headache at 145/95, pregnancy or birth unanswered' cells with nothing. k_grid.women_floor has no row for headache.
findings.why: Q10 made the same-day pregnancy rules 'wait for the answer' but no item asks for it; R7 Q10 asked for one prompt 'pregnancy not recorded: ask now'. A woman 2 weeks after delivery truthfully answers 'not pregnant' (UCG-PE-04: pre-eclampsia up to 4-6 weeks postpartum; UCG-PE-03: any pre-eclampsia is referred). Rule 2.
findings.reviewerFix: Add one same-day item: female, pregnancy_possible not false, BP >= REF-DM-PREG-BP-SBP/DBP, and pregnant or postpartum_weeks unrecorded -> 'Ask now: pregnant, or a birth in the last 6 weeks?' naming the gap; or give 27D pregnancyUnknownCounts with unknownDisplay. Add headache rows to women_floor (same_day for every POSSIBLE state).
findings.done: 27D (headache or vomiting with 140/90) treats unanswered pregnancy or postpartum as possible. Women's grid row.

findings.finding: 27D refers a pregnant woman with BP >= 140/90 and headache or vomiting 'to hospital today' (same_day), while its own note says 'UCG 2023 16.3.7 lists headache, new blurred vision, epigastric pain and vomiting among the features of severe pre-eclampsia'. No research-table row quotes that list (UCG rows mentioning headache: only UCG-HTN-03). Evaluator: DMV-127 (34 weeks, 150/100, headache, protein negative) -> 27D same_day only; P4 same.
findings.why: If the note is right, she has severe pre-eclampsia by the pack's own source (UCG-PE-02 'any degree of hypertension with evidence of organ dysfunction'), which the pack routes as an interrupt (28B); if it is not quoted, the note asserts a source sentence nobody has read (rule 10). R7 Q06 asked for the list to be quoted first and the urgency put to the CSO; no D-DM item carries it.
findings.reviewerFix: Quote the UCG 2023 16.3.7 severe-features text into the research table; open a D-DM item (or extend D-DM-41) for the urgency of 27D; until signed, display 'refer to hospital now' rather than 'today'.
findings.done: 27D is an interrupt, cited to UCG 16.3.7's severe features (UCG-PE-05) and 4.1.6.1.

findings.where: DM_ANY not used outside the acute lane: management (DM-ACT-*), targets, stratify bands, DM-STR-* rules
findings.finding: An established patient with a recorded type and medicine but a blank status box gets no screening, no targets and no pregnancy referral. Evaluator: woman 28, pregnant 10 weeks, type 1 on insulin, dm_status blank, established -> DM-ACT-SCREEN-PREG-01 silent, no targets, no HbA1c/eye/kidney/foot items; only EDU-03/04/05. k_grid's own profiles ins_nostatus and T1_nostatus model this record.
findings.why: The shared list exists because one box is ticked without another (L04, Q02). Act, targets and bands still read dm_status == known only, so the missing box is read as 'no diabetes' (rule 2). The pregnant woman with type 1 misses 'specialised antenatal care' (same_day).
findings.reviewerFix: Replace `dm_status == known` with k_r7.DM_ANY in management, targets, interpretation bands and DM-STR/DM-CLS rules (keep the gestational notWhen on SCREEN-PREG-01). Vignette: the pregnant type 1 above -> SCREEN-PREG-01 same_day.
findings.done: Steps and targets read the shared diabetes list instead of the status box alone.

findings.where: Evaluator: rules and refer/test steps do not apply blocking caveats (build.py run_vignette: rules use ev_crit unguarded; HELD_KINDS = therapy_review only)
findings.finding: Values the pack has declared invalid still drive referrals, tests and wording. Evaluator: type 2 on insulin, iron deficiency (manufactures), HbA1c 8.0 -> DM-ACT-REFER-TARGET-02 'refer for review of the insulin'; same with a transfusion in the last 3 months, HbA1c 8.2 -> same; new patient, sickle cell disease, HbA1c 6.6, polyuria -> DM-SUS-INCID-02 'with symptoms it is diagnostic' while who_hd_hba1c_symptoms is blocked; known diabetes with sickle cell disease, 8 months since HbA1c -> DM-ACT-TEST-HBA1C-01 'HbA1c is due', though the caveat says 'monitor with glucose readings'.
findings.why: The brief's semantics: a blocking caveat makes every criterion that reads its feature insufficient. A falsely high HbA1c sending an insulin user for intensification risks hypoglycaemia; telling the clinician a blocked value 'is diagnostic' is rule 10.
findings.reviewerFix: Apply guarded() to rules and to refer/test steps (not only therapy_review); give DM-ACT-TEST-HBA1C-01 a notWhen 'HbA1c blocked for this patient' with the WHO HEARTS-D surrogate (fasting/post-meal glucose, the tgt_fpg_surrogate quote) as the proposal; INCID-02 display variant when HbA1c is blocked.
findings.done: Blocking caveats act by direction on every non-acute rule and step, with the value named as a gap; an HbA1c test step proposes the alternative when HbA1c is blocked. DMV-135.

findings.finding: 'No probable neuropathy' is reported without any sensory test. Evaluator: known type 2, foot_numbness_burning false, ankle_reflexes normal, no monofilament/vibration/pinprick/Ipswich -> complications.peripheral_neuropathy_probable 'not_met'. diabetic_retinopathy has notMetRequires (adequate graded exam); neuropathy has none.
findings.why: Rule 2: an examination never done is reported as normal. Loss of protective sensation is the foot-risk driver; ADA/IWGDF define it by sensory testing, not by symptoms and reflexes.
findings.reviewerFix: Add notMetRequires: a recorded monofilament_10g or ipswich_sites_missed (or vibration) result, per REF-DM-FOOT-LOPS-RULE and D-DM-18; otherwise 'insufficient' with the gap named.
findings.done: Neuropathy is never 'not met' without a sensory test.

findings.finding: The band is 'baseline' when every risk factor is unrecorded, and for a young type 1 on insulin. Evaluator: type 2 on insulin, hypo history, awareness score and eGFR not recorded -> risk 'baseline'; type 1 aged 25 on insulin, no lows -> 'baseline'. The model's `requires` list (hypo_worst_12m, hypo_awareness_score, egfr, age_years) is ignored by the evaluator.
findings.why: Rule 2: 'high' and 'raised' are insufficient, so first-match falls through to the catch-all. ADA Table 6.5 (the model's own quote) lists intensive insulin therapy as a major risk factor; the applicabilityNote itself says younger people with type 1 are at very high risk.
findings.reviewerFix: Enforce `requires` (no band, named gaps, until hypo_worst_12m at least is recorded); add an intensive-insulin/type 1 arm per ADA Table 6.5 to the CSO's D-DM-16 item.
findings.done: The hypoglycaemia model needs the medicine list. ADA's 'intensive insulin' factor is a source addition for D-DM-42.

findings.finding: The chart band is shown outside the chart's applicability. Evaluator: established cardiovascular disease, chart value 8% -> risk '5_to_10'; age 30, chart 3% -> 'lt5'. The applicabilityNote says 'Ages 40 to 74 only. Not for people with established cardiovascular disease, who are high risk by definition'; no predicate tests either.
findings.why: Rule 10: a person after a stroke or MI shown as 5-10% risk invites under-treatment; the note is prose an engine will not read.
findings.reviewerFix: Add a model-level notWhen (cvd_established present; age_years < 40 or > 74) and, for cvd_established, a 'high by definition' display (WHO HEARTS / the model's own note).
findings.done: The CVD chart needs all its inputs and does not run with established CVD; its age range needs WHO's chart text (D-DM-40).

findings.finding: (a) A lean child labelled type 2 gets no classification prompt: child 9, type 2 recorded, BMI 18 -> fired {}. (b) ATYP-01 cannot fire at the visit it is meant for: new lean 25-year-old, polyuria, capillary 15, BMI 17 -> WHO 'met', T1-04 fires, ATYP-01 silent (age_at_diagnosis unrecorded); next visit, established, age_at_diagnosis still blank -> T1-02 and ATYP-01 both insufficient, fired only EDU-01/02.
findings.why: Rule 3 allows classification support under 16, and in children type 2 without obesity is the label most likely to be wrong (ISPAD 2022). At diagnosis, age now is the age at diagnosis; reading only a field that is filled later makes established_or_met dead on 'met' (rule 10).
findings.reviewerFix: Child/adolescent rule: type 2 recorded, or diabetes not on insulin -> refer for type review (ISPAD 2022 classification chapter). ATYP-01, T1-02, MODY-01: when newly_met, read age_years in place of age_at_diagnosis, or name age_at_diagnosis as a gap.
findings.done: Classification prompts in a lean child recorded as type 2 and age at diagnosis: Design B owns the timing.

findings.finding: HbA1c is blocked for every sickle-trait carrier, with no feature that can lift the block, although its own alternative reads 'unless the laboratory confirms its method is free of interference'. Evaluator (design): blocksDiagnosis true, direction unpredictable, when ALL[sickle_cell_trait present]; no notWhen.
findings.why: NGSP's interference list (the source A11-26 already cited by DM-CON-VALID-03) shows most current methods unaffected by HbAS; with trait common in Uganda this removes HbA1c from a large share of patients wherever trait is recorded (a caveat that blocks wrongly).
findings.reviewerFix: Add a feature 'HbA1c method certified free of HbS interference (NGSP list)' and a notWhen on the caveat; CSO to confirm with the referral laboratories' methods.
findings.done: The variant caveats lift when the laboratory documents a variant-free method (NGSP).

findings.finding: Fires without an ACE inhibitor or ARB. Evaluator: type 2 on metformin, ras_blocker 'none', creatinine_rise_percent_4w 35 -> flag 'Creatinine up by more than 30% after starting an ACE inhibitor or ARB'.
findings.why: Rule 10: the predicate tests only the rise; the label and action are about a RAS blocker the patient is not taking.
findings.reviewerFix: Add ras_blocker in [acei, arb, both] (or ras_or_sglt2_started_recently present) to the criterion; route an unexplained 30% rise to the AKI pathway instead (KDIGO 2022).
findings.done: The creatinine-rise flag needs an ACE inhibitor or ARB.

findings.finding: Q10 partly fixed: the same-day rules wait, but a woman with pregnancy unanswered and asymptomatic BP 165/100 still gets an interrupt. Evaluator: woman 45, known type 2, 165/100 -> interrupt DM-ACU-ROUTE-28 via 'pregnant', display 'Pregnancy or a recent birth is not recorded: ask now. If pregnant or within 6 weeks of birth: pregnant or within 6 weeks of birth, with blood pressure 160/110 ...'.
findings.why: Rule 9: severe asymptomatic hypertension is common in women attending a diabetes clinic and the question resolves it in seconds; R7 Q10 asked that the underlying urgency apply only once the answer is yes. (The age band for pregnancy_possible is D-DM-36 and not re-reported.)
findings.reviewerFix: When met only via unknown and no organ-damage/drowsy arm is met, issue the 'ask now' as a same-day prompt with the gap, escalating to the interrupt once answered yes; keep 28B/28C/28D interrupting on unknown.
findings.done: Rule 28 on the unknown path is same day with the question, not an interrupt.

findings.where: decisions D-DM-41 question and recommended text; k_grid.floor

Kussmaul breathing or acetone in diabetes', which k_grid.floor no longer encodes for metformin, sulfonylurea or blank-list profiles (see T04). findings.where: Under-16 items beyond recognition and referral: DM-STR-STEROID-01, DM-STR-NEURO-01, DM-CLS-PANC-02, therapy flags with ages 'any'
findings.finding: Evaluator: child 12, type 1 on insulin and metformin, numb feet, on steroids -> DM-STR-NEURO-01 (test order, vitamin B12) and DM-STR-STEROID-01 'monitor after meals' (monitoring.propose); adolescent 13, type 1, low needing help -> hypoglycaemia_needing_help_on_treatment 're-evaluation of the plan, with a review of the medicine'.

findings.done: 'Adult' is 16 and over by numeric age in the evaluator.

findings.why: Rule 10.

findings.finding: Immediate but absent from acuteOrder, so it has no interruptRank in the manifest; secondary enuresis alone interrupts (child 8, bed-wetting only -> interrupt DM-SUS-PAED-01).

findings.reviewerFix: Add to ACUTE_ORDER after the measured rules; CSO to confirm immediate vs same_day for enuresis alone (NICE NG18 / ISPAD 2022).
findings.done: PAED-01 has a rank, as a measure-now request.

findings.finding: Still 'headache, blurred vision or vomiting' after Q24 moved blurred vision to organ damage.
findings.why: Rule 10 drift.
findings.reviewerFix: Display from the feature labels.
findings.done: BP-03 display.

findings.finding: prior_gdm with postpartum_weeks 260 -> 'Gestational diabetes in the pregnancy just ended: re-test 6 to 12 weeks after the birth' beside RISK-05.

findings.reviewerFix: Bound postpartum_weeks to the 6-12 week window (REF already cited) and leave later years to RISK-05.
findings.done: Postpartum timing beyond 6 weeks is Design B's episode logic.

findings.reviewerFix: 'insulin not recorded'.
findings.done: T1-05's label speaks of a recorded list; a blank list does not fire it.

findings.why: Rule 10, duplicate same-day items.

findings.finding: Now runs at all ages but is cited only to ISPAD's paediatric limited-resource chapter; the adult notWhen also cites REF-DM-SUS-PAED-MIMIC.

findings.reviewerFix: Cite the adult arm under D-DM-37 item 1.

findings.reviewerFix: Fire at TB diagnosis whatever the last test, per the WHO 2025 TB comorbidities handbook text already in the research table.

findings.finding: A single eGFR 45 -> 'eGFR 30 to 59: routine referral'; the CKD target is applied during AKI (egfr_not_steady_state does not reach targets).

findings.where: 60-acute-route.json DM-ACU-ROUTE-13B (notWhen acu_dm_acetone_test_done), DM-ACU-ROUTE-21 (notWhen on acetone/dehydration), DM-ACU-ROUTE-21/21B (any[] lacks acetone), DM-ACU-ROUTE-24B (stop acu_t1_acetone_list_clear); k_grid.floor; T04
findings.finding: T04 is only partly fixed. Diabetes on metformin or a sulfonylurea (type 2, 'unclassified', or gestational) with acetone on the breath or dehydration and ANY recorded ketone result other than normal blood ketones gets no same-day or immediate item. Evaluator: T2 metformin, acetone, bohb 1.0 -> only EDU-01/02 (R8's own patient, unchanged); T2 metformin, acetone, glucose 7, urine 1+ -> only EDU-01/02 (R8's own patient, unchanged); same with urine neg or trace -> only EDU-01/02, with caveat urine_ketones_low_despite_picture shown; T2 metformin, dehydrated, glucose 7, urine 1+ -> EDU + metformin flag only; T2 metformin+gliclazide, acetone, bohb 1.2 -> EDU only; 'unclassified' on metformin, acetone, glucose 10, urine 1+ -> EDU only; pregnant 30 weeks with gestational diabetes on metformin, acetone, glucose 8, urine 1+ -> EDU only. r9/grid9.py: 160 adult and older-adult cells (both sites, T2_metf and T2_SU) with acetone or dehydration and urine neg/trace/1+ or blood 1.0/1.4 have nothing at same-day or above. Mechanism: 13B stands down on any ketone record; 21 stands down on acetone or dehydration ('an interrupting rule applies'), but 24B no longer interrupts for these patients; 21 and 21B do not read acetone. The same patient with the TYPE left blank gets the 24B interrupt (U13), so recording 'type 2' moves him from an interrupt to silence.
findings.why: R8 T04's fix asked for same day when ketones are 'not measured or above REF-DM-ACU-KETONE-LOW'; only 'not measured' was built (k_grid.floor: ket == 'none'). The pack's own caveat says a low urine strip with acetone or vomiting can mask ketoacidosis and that the alternative is blood ketones or a gas, 'if neither is available, treat the clinical picture and refer', yet nothing refers. Ketosis-prone and unclassified diabetes are common in Uganda. Rules 2, 4, 8.
findings.reviewerFix: 13B: stand down only on blood ketones below REF-DM-ACU-KETONE-LOW (BOHB_NORMAL), not on any urine result. 21: drop acetone/dehydration from its notWhen when 24B is not met (or reuse 24B's own stop as the notWhen), and add acetone_breath to the any[] of 21 and 21B. 24B's stop: count only dm_type_recorded == type_2 as excluding type 1 ('unclassified' means the type is not settled; the pack's CLS-T1-03). Floor row: diabetes with acetone or dehydration and ketones other than blood below 0.6 -> same_day, at both sites.
findings.done: 13B stands down only on blood ketones below 0.6; rules 21/21B read acetone and no longer hand acetone to 24B; 'unclassified' no longer excludes type 1. Floor rows. DMV-136.

findings.where: 60-acute-route.json DM-ACU-ROUTE-23D (k_r8 T29 notWhen acu_insulin_sick_district_done); D-DM-42 interim text; k_grid.floor
findings.finding: Regression from T29. On insulin or type 1, vomiting, at a district site, with a negative urine strip and any glucose below 18 -> nothing. Evaluator (district): adult T1 on insulin, vomiting, glucose 7, urine neg -> EDU-01..05 only; same at glucose 14 -> EDU only; adult T1, vomiting, glucose 7, no ketones -> 23D same_day (so recording the strip silences him); pregnant 12 weeks with type 1 on insulin, vomiting, glucose 9, urine neg -> only DM-ACT-SCREEN-PREG-01 (antenatal referral), no acute item; child 8 with type 1 on insulin, vomiting, glucose 7, urine neg -> {}. At the referral site the same patients get ROUTE-23 (blood ketones not recorded). r9/grid9.py: 20 district cells (adult, older, child, adolescent; T1_ins and ins_nostatus).
findings.why: 23D now stands down on any urine result; its 'repeat it in 2 hours' exists only in the notWhen label, so nobody says it. 21 needs trace/1+; 19 and 34 need 11.1/18 and 19 stands down on a ketone record. The pack's caveat urine_ketones_low_despite_picture says a negative strip with vomiting can miss early ketoacidosis, and REF-DM-ACU-SICKDAY-INSULIN (ISPAD 2022 ch.13) prefers blood ketones and says to check ketones every 1-2 h. D-DM-42's interim ('keep same-day with repeat the strip in 2 hours and say so') is no longer what the build does below 18. Rules 4 and 8.
findings.reviewerFix: 23D: stand down only on urine 2+ or a sign (the interrupting rules); with urine neg/trace/1+ recorded, keep it same_day with the display 'repeat the strip in 2 hours; refer if vomiting continues or ketones rise' (REF-DM-ACU-SICKDAY-INSULIN). Floor row: insulin or type 1, vomiting, district, urine strip only -> same_day.
findings.done: 23D keeps asking for a repeat strip in 2 hours; it never falls silent on a negative strip. DMV-137.

findings.where: 60-acute-route.json DM-ACU-ROUTE-27D notWhen (BP >= 160/110 'rule 28 interrupts') x DM-ACU-ROUTE-28 x.unknownUrgency same_day (T18); k_grid.women_floor; D-DM-41 text
findings.finding: Urgency falls as the picture worsens when pregnancy or the weeks since birth are unanswered. Evaluator: woman 30, pregnancy unanswered, 150/100, headache -> interrupt 27D; same woman at 170/115 with headache -> only DM-ACU-ROUTE-28 same_day (no interrupt); pregnant=false with weeks since birth blank, 170/115, headache -> 28 same_day only; woman 52 with type 2, unanswered, 150/95 headache -> interrupt, at 165/112 headache -> same_day. r9/grid9.py: 8/8 cells (unanswered or notpreg_ppblank x 165/112 or 185/120 x headache, with and without diabetes) below interrupt. Below 180/110 rule 29 cannot rescue her, and 29 does not read headache.
findings.why: 27D hands the patient to 28 above 160/110, but on the unknown path 28 is same_day (T18). D-DM-41's recommended text promises an interrupt for '(or unanswered) ... 140/90 with ... headache'. A woman 2 weeks after delivery who truthfully answers 'not pregnant' with 170/115 and headache has severe pre-eclampsia features by UCG 2023 16.3.7 (UCG-PE-05). women_floor sets this cell to same_day, so the build cannot see it. Rules 2 and 4.
findings.reviewerFix: Make 27D's notWhen hand off only when 28 is met on recorded facts (pregnant, or postpartum_weeks within REF-DM-PREG-PE-POSTPARTUM), or give 28 its same_day unknownUrgency only when hypertensive_symptoms, organ damage and drowsiness are absent. women_floor: POSSIBLE x severe-range BP x headache -> immediate.
findings.done: 27D no longer hands a worse pressure to rule 28's same-day unknown path. Women's floor row. DMV-138.

findings.where: 10-suspect.json DM-SUS-PAED-04 (reads fasting_pg, ogtt_2h_pg, hba1c only), DM-SUS-PAED-01 (stands down on any glucose), DM-SUS-INCID-03 (adult only); T07
findings.finding: T07 is fixed for laboratory values only. A symptomatic child who meets the WHO criteria on a fasting meter reading gets nothing, at either site. Evaluator: child 12 (adolescent band), polyuria, fasting capillary glucose 9.0 -> who_hearts_d_2020 'met', fired {} (referral and district). The adult equivalent is INCID-03 (fasting meter 7.0 or more), which is adult-only; PAED-04 cannot fire at a district site because fasting_pg needs the laboratory.
findings.why: Rule 3 allows recognition and referral under 16, and rule 8 says a district site must reach a safe next step; at a district the meter is the only glucose. REF-DM-SUS-PAED-SAMEDAY (NICE NG18 1.1.2): suspected type 1 in a child is referred the same day. Delay is the path to ketoacidosis.
findings.reviewerFix: PAED-04: add the fasting meter arm (capillary_glucose_context == fasting and capillary_glucose >= REF-DM-DX-FPG) and a 'diabetes criteria met at this visit' arm (who_hearts_d_2020 met, or met ignoring pregnancy); vignette at the district site.
findings.done: DM-SUS-PAED-05 refers a child with a fasting meter value of 7.0 or more the same day. DMV-139.

findings.where: 20-confirm.json validityCaveats hba1c_sickle_cell_disease x.notWhen hba1c_sickle_cell_disease_lifted (k_r8 T16 loop matched ids containing 'sickle')
findings.finding: The T16 fix lifts the sickle cell DISEASE caveat, not only the trait caveat, when the laboratory method is variant-free. Evaluator: sickle cell disease, hba1c_method_variant_free true, HbA1c 6.0, new patient -> caveat gone, ada_2026_prediabetes 'met' (without the flag: 'insufficient'); known type 2 with sickle cell disease, method flag, HbA1c 7.5 -> tgt_hba1c_general and band hba1c_control_general 'above_target' (so 6.8 would read 'at target').
findings.why: In HbSS the problem is shortened red cell survival, not analytical interference, so no method makes HbA1c valid; the caveat itself says 'masks' and its alternative is 'use plasma glucose to diagnose; monitor with glucose readings'. A falsely low HbA1c then reads as 'at target' or 'prediabetes' and hides diabetes or under-treats it. A caveat that should block no longer does.
findings.reviewerFix: Remove the notWhen from hba1c_sickle_cell_disease; keep it on hba1c_variant_trait only. Source: NGSP's HbA1c and haemoglobin variant pages (the T16 source) and ADA Standards 2026 section 2 (plasma glucose only in sickle cell disease). Vignette: SCD + method flag + HbA1c 6.0 -> diagnosis insufficient, no band.
findings.done: Only the trait caveat can be lifted; sickle cell disease never.

findings.where: 40-stratify.json targets tgt_hba1c_ckd, tgt_hba1c_tb (no tier notWhen) x tgt_hba1c_relaxed notWhen (tier in general/tight/avoid_symptoms); band hba1c_control_ckd; 50-act.json DM-ACT-REFER-TARGET-02; semantics.targets
findings.finding: The T06 contradiction returns through supersedes. When the agreed tier is 'avoid symptoms', the relaxed target is suppressed by its own notWhen, so the CKD (or TB) target is no longer superseded and comes back with its band. Evaluator: 80, frail, gliclazide, tier avoid_symptoms, eGFR 45, HbA1c 8.5 -> target tgt_hba1c_ckd (6.5 to 8.0) and band hba1c_control_ckd 'above_target'; 80, insulin, tier avoid_symptoms, HbA1c 8.5 -> DM-ACT-REFER-TARGET-02 'On insulin with HbA1c above 7.5%: refer for review of the insulin'; same with TB -> tgt_hba1c_tb shown. Also insulin with a low needing help (or frailty), HbA1c 7.8 -> band hba1c_control_relaxed 'at_target' beside REFER-TARGET-02 'HbA1c above 7.5%: refer'.
findings.why: The semantics block says 'Avoid symptoms proposes no HbA1c target by design' and 'an agreed tier decides'. An 'Above target' label on a frail person on a sulfonylurea with CKD, whose agreed goal is to avoid symptoms, points to more treatment: the hypoglycaemia harm R8 rated critical in T06. REF-DM-CTRL-OLDER-POOR (ADA 13.7c): focus on avoiding hypoglycaemia and symptomatic hyperglycaemia.
findings.reviewerFix: Give tgt_hba1c_ckd and tgt_hba1c_tb a notWhen 'glycaemic_target_tier == avoid_symptoms' (and decide whether an agreed general or tight tier also stands them down, as the semantics say). REFER-TARGET-02: notWhen tier in [relaxed, avoid_symptoms], frailty, or a significant low on treatment (the relaxed target's own reasons), not only 'relaxed and below 8'. Vignettes for the three patients.
findings.done: 'Avoid symptoms' stops every HbA1c target; CKD stands down under an agreed tier; the insulin referral stands down on a reason to relax. DMV-140.

findings.where: 40-stratify.json DM-STR-STEROID-01, DM-STR-NEURO-01; 30-classify.json DM-CLS-PANC-02; 50-act.json therapyFlag hypoglycaemia_needing_help_on_treatment (ages any); T20
findings.finding: T20 is marked fixed but nothing changed for its patients. Evaluator: child 12 (adolescent band), type 1 on insulin and metformin, numb feet, on steroids -> DM-STR-NEURO-01 (test.order vitamin B12) and DM-STR-STEROID-01 (monitoring.propose glucose after meals); adolescent 13, type 1, low needing help -> hypoglycaemia_needing_help_on_treatment ('re-evaluation of the plan, with a review of the medicine causing it'); adolescent 13, steatorrhoea and abdominal pain -> DM-CLS-PANC-02 (test.order pancreas imaging). The numeric-age change touches only items with x.ages = adult; these have no age gate.
findings.why: Rule 3: under 16, recognition, classification support and referral only. Monitoring plans, work-up and medicine review in a child belong to the paediatric diabetes team. Direct harm is low, but this is a breach of a stated rule that the disposition reports as fixed.
findings.reviewerFix: ageBands adult on STR-STEROID-01, STR-NEURO-01, CLS-PANC-02 with a child variant 'refer to the paediatric diabetes team' (REF-DM-SUS-PAED-SAMEDAY); a child display for the hypoglycaemia flag ('refer to the diabetes team'); a vignette for each.
findings.done: Steroid, neuropathy and pancreatic rules are adult-only; flags shown under 16 carry the refer-only action.

findings.where: 60-acute-route.json acute lane for children with diabetes (ROUTE-23 notWhen bohb < 0.6, ROUTE-32 needs no glucose, ROUTE-25C reads dehydration/acetone only); T05
findings.finding: T05 partly fixed. A child with diabetes who is vomiting, with glucose and ketones recorded and not in a danger range, gets nothing. Evaluator: child 8 with type 1 on insulin, vomiting, glucose 7, bohb 0.2 -> {}; same at district with urine neg -> {}. r9/grid9.py: 56 child/adolescent cells (every diabetes profile, glucose 5 or 7, urine neg or bohb 0.3). The dehydrated child is fixed (25C).

findings.finding: The T06/U06 contradiction survives on the glucose surrogates. 'Avoid symptoms' (or a relaxed tier, or frailty) removes every HbA1c target, but the surrogate 'Fasting glucose below 7.0 / after a meal below 9.0' is still proposed and the meter is banded against it. Evaluator: 80, frail, gliclazide, tier avoid_symptoms, fasting meter 8.5, district -> targets [tgt_fpg_surrogate, tgt_ppg_surrogate, tgt_bp], band fcap_control_who 'above_target'; same with tier relaxed -> tgt_hba1c_relaxed (below 8.0%) beside tgt_fpg_surrogate (below 7.0) and 'above_target'; no tier (frailty relaxes) -> the same; 80 on insulin, avoid_symptoms, post-meal 10.5 -> ppg_control_who 'above_target'. DMV-140 asserts the HbA1c targets absent and does not test the surrogates.
findings.why: At a district site the meter value is the only control measure, so this band is what the clinician acts on. Telling a frail 80-year-old on a sulfonylurea with an agreed 'avoid symptoms' plan that a fasting 8.5 is above target invites intensification, and sulfonylurea hypoglycaemia in frail older people is the harm the relaxed tier exists to prevent (ADA Standards of Care section 13). findings.reviewerFix: Give tgt_fpg_surrogate and tgt_ppg_surrogate the notWhen set of tgt_hba1c_general (avoid_symptoms, relaxed, frailty, cognitive impairment, significant lows, impaired awareness) and give the four glucose bands forTarget so they show only beside a surrogate actually proposed. A relaxed fasting or post-meal goal must come from ADA Standards of Care section 13 (older adults) with the CSO's signature (fold into D-DM-40); until then show the value without an 'above/at target' band. Extend DMV-140 with a fasting meter value and assert no surrogate target and no band.
findings.done: The fasting and post-meal targets stand down under a relaxed or 'avoid symptoms' plan and on the general target's relax reasons; their four bands read only against a target shown. DMV-140 extended; DMV-143.
